title: seat(judge): make alibaba-coding/qwen3.8-max a USEABLE judge without worker use — config-driven judge_only gate in pick_seat
body:
difficulty: heavy
# seat(judge): make alibaba-coding/qwen3.8-max a USEABLE judge without worker use — config-driven judge_only gate in pick_seat

Follow-up to the Nish 2026-09-08 re-scope of #4445. That PR parks alibaba-coding at cap 0 (no worker use) and lands alibaba-coding/qwen3.8-max on `senior_seats_in_order` as a declared-but-inert judge candidate. This issue activates it.

**The gap:** `find_senior_seat` (the judge/senior reviewer resolver) requires `model_cap > 0` and `seat_usable`, so qwen3.8-max at cap 0 is skipped and can never actually be drawn as a judge. Raising its cap makes it worker-pickable again (`pick_seat` and `find_senior_seat` share `SEAT_MODEL_CAP`). There is no config flag that keeps a cap>0 model out of worker `pick_seat` while leaving it usable by `find_senior_seat` — the only worker-exclusion today is the hardcoded `_provider_is_keystone_only` (cursor) and `product_only`.

**Do:** add a config-driven `judge_only: true` flag read by `pick_seat` that skips the seat for every worker difficulty (light/heavy/keystone/senior-review worker picks) while `find_senior_seat` / `senior_seat_available` still use it when it appears in `senior_seats_in_order`. Keep it data-driven (mirror the existing `product_only` gate pattern), land a seat-lib test for the exclusion, and raise qwen3.8-max's cap to 1 with the judge_only flag so it becomes a real, usable judge for the fleet's reviewer/audit roles. No new organs/machinery — extends the existing pick_seat filter chain.

termination: PR merged that adds a config-driven judge_only gate; qwen3.8-max is cap 1 on the roster, `pick_seat` never offers it to a worker, `find_senior_seat` can draw it when earlier senior seats are walled; a seat-lib test pins the worker exclusion.

A signup that originates from any untagged surface (direct type-in, /pricing, /help, an old cached page) records no source, so the acquisition direction cannot answer "which surface produced the 23" — and every distribution bet's termination check ("≥1 signup attributable") is unprovable.

evidence:

- #3514 (guide hidden inputs unread — same seam, one specific inlet)
- merged PR "growth: tag source= on every acquisition-surface signup CTA (#3358)"

- signup_source capture gets a deterministic fallback: when no source marker is observable, record UNKNOWN (never NULL), with the referrer + landing path captured alongside
- /search reads the hidden source= inputs that guide CTAs pass it (closes the #3514 inlet; that issue stays open for its own verify)

- test under tests/integration/** applying real migrations asserting the write path records source for: direct /auth/signup, /search→wall→signup, guide-tagged /search entry

```
npx wrangler d1 execute 0509 --remote --command "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE createdAt > datetime('now','-7 days') AND (signup_source IS NULL)" --json | jq -r '.[0].results[0]'
```

rollback: revert the fallback; column nullable again, no data migration

dedupe: #3514 covers only the guide-inlet read side; #3367 is suggestion-accept funnel; none cover the UNKNOWN fallback + referrer capture

impact: with 23 signups/30d finally moving, the acquisition direction's whole premise — measure which unpaid surface works — fails if signups are unattributable. This is the measurement substrate for every distribution bet.

funnel_stage: signup


title: seo/growth: live sitemap + llms.txt advertise 3 /guides/* and /switch/adspy URLs that 404 — production ~3 days stale, deploy chain red since 2026-09-09 17:03Z
body:
metric: Every URL advertised by the live https://0509.io/sitemap.xml and https://0509.io/llms.txt returns HTTP 200 with non-empty HTML; production runs the current main head (deploy-production.yml conclusion=success on origin/main HEAD); a live canary guards the invariant.

observed: 2026-09-12T03:50-04:10Z, fresh session against https://0509.io:
- sitemap.xml (173 URLs) and llms.txt advertise 6 /guides/* pages, but 3 return 404 ("Page not found | Five to Nine"): /guides/how-to-get-alerted-when-a-competitor-changes-their-offer, /guides/how-to-prove-what-changed-on-a-competitor-website, /guides/how-to-turn-a-one-off-competitor-check-into-a-standing-watch.
- /switch/adspy (merged 2026-09-12T00:21Z, PR #3118/#3091) returns 404.
- The live /guides hub lists only the 3 older children, while main's app/routes/guides.tsx lists all 6.
- Root cause of the divergence: last successful deploy-production.yml run on main is 2026-09-09T17:03:16Z (d16b1f000). Since then: failures (3811a12c5 at 01:46Z, 6fc8d012e at 01:52Z on 2026-09-12), cancellations 01:30Z-03:49Z, and runs 34671488829 (14667a9fc) + 34671703839 (5c9cf8d66) still pending/waiting at check time. Guides routes + sitemap entries merged 2026-09-12T00:18Z (#3116, d6521dd1f — ancestor of pending 5c9cf8d66, NOT of deployed d16b1f000) and were never successfully deployed, while the sitemap/llms.txt surface already advertises them — crawler- and answer-engine-visible 404s.

evidence:
- curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c '/guides/' → 6 entries, 3 404 (repro in termination)
- curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://0509.io/guides/how-to-get-alerted-when-a-competitor-changes-their-offer → 404
- curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://0509.io/switch/adspy → 404
- curl -sS https://0509.io/llms.txt advertises the same 3 dead URLs
- gh run list -R Nishfleet/0509 --workflow deploy-production.yml --branch main: last success 2026-09-09T17:03:16Z d16b1f000; failures 2026-09-12T01:46Z 3811a12c5 and 01:52Z 6fc8d012e
- git merge-base --is-ancestor d6521dd1f d16b1f000 → false; ancestor of 5c9cf8d66 (pending deploy head) → true
- ~2.5 days of merged but undeployed product work also includes: BET 1 digest re-rank pin, #3148 brief placeholder gate, #3094 Visualping switch copy, #3119 sneaker per-brand pages, #3098 per-guide og cards, #3072

accept:
1. deploy-production.yml reaches conclusion=success on the current origin/main head (>= 5c9cf8d66) and the deployed Worker serves all six /guides/* routes plus /switch/adspy with 200 + non-empty HTML carrying canonical + og tags per the #3098/#3122 pattern.
2. Every URL in the live sitemap.xml returns 200 with non-empty HTML — spot-set: all /guides/*, all /switch/*, all /compare/*, /brands, /timeline/nike.com, /ads/nike.com, /sample-brief, /briefs/weekly.
3. Prevention mechanism (mechanical-fix rule): extend the sitemap-coverage observe-to-close guard pattern of PR #3163 (currently /timeline:/ads only) to assert EVERY sitemap URL serves 200 on production post-deploy and auto-file a dedicated issue on any 404/noindex divergence, so source-side agreement tests (#3122) cannot pass while production diverges. Observe-to-close: the guard ships and runs even while green, with a recorded run (or drill) demonstrating it catches the divergence class.
4. If any advertised URL cannot be made 200, remove it from sitemap.xml + llms.txt in the same change — never ship an advertised 404.

verify:
```
for u in $(curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE 'https://0509\.io/(guides|switch)/[a-z0-9-]+' | sort -u); do sleep 1; curl -fsS -o /dev/null "$u" || exit 1; echo "200 $u"; done
gh run list --repo Nishfleet/0509 --workflow deploy-production.yml --branch main --limit 1 --json conclusion,headSha
```

rollback: no code revert required for the fix itself — restoring a green deploy chain is the fix. If an individual merged PR is implicated in the deploy failures, revert that PR per the auto-revert runbook; the canary extension is a single scripts/canary-* file, plain revert.

dedupe: none. #3156 is the crawl-429 rate-limit defect (different failure). PR #3163 covers /timeline:/ads coverage only. Closed #3122 triple-agreement test validates source-side sitemap-route-index agreement, not the deployed site — exactly the gap this issue closes. Existing AUTO-REVERT HALT issues predate this run's red chain.

impact: The sitemap + llms.txt are the top of the acquisition funnel (direction#4518: unpaid distribution, SEO/AEO owned content only). Right now they hand Google and answer engines three dead guide URLs and a dead switch page — soft-404 signals and dead AEO links on the exact queries the guides were written to own. Meanwhile ~2.5 days of merged acquisition work (guides, /switch/adspy, sneaker per-brand pages, per-guide og cards) is invisible to every visitor.

title: stale conflicting PRs #6819 (parent #6782) and #6815 (parent #6032): rebase-or-close with evidence — fleet-merged-pr-close fails loud until they clear
body:
observed: fleet-merged-pr-close.service exits 1 (stale_conflicting_prs=2): PR #6819 (claim/issue-6782) and PR #6815 (claim/issue-6032) have been CONFLICTING for 72h against a 24h bound while their parent issues are OPEN. The detector is correct; the fault is the two branches. Jev triage 2026-09-17: file_stale_pr_issue p=0.47 — coin flip resolved by the standing rule that a failed unit is repaired the same turn.

accept: for EACH PR, exactly one of: (a) rebase onto origin/main, resolve conflicts faithfully to the parent issue's accept lines, push, checks green, auto-merge armed; or (b) close it with a comment citing the merged commit that already delivers the parent issue's accept lines (git merge-base --is-ancestor proof) and unblock/close the parent accordingly. No force-push over someone else's fresh commits; no test removed.
verify: gh pr view 6819 --json mergeable ; gh pr view 6815 --json mergeable ; systemctl --user reset-failed fleet-merged-pr-close.service && systemctl --user start fleet-merged-pr-close.service && journalctl --user -u fleet-merged-pr-close.service -n 5
termination: journalctl --user -u fleet-merged-pr-close.service -n 20 -o cat | grep -q 'stale_conflicting_prs=0'
rollback: a rebased branch can be reset to its pre-rebase SHA (record it in the PR comment first).
dedupe: #6782 and #6032 are the parent work items; this issue is only the branch-hygiene repair.

title: growth: funnel events land in console-only logs — visit→signup conversion is unmeasurable; add a queryable read path (direction#4518)
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#2869 score=0.49 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#2869 (score 0.49). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: the trailing-7d counts of the already-emitted funnel event kinds (home_view, search_preview_submit, search_preview_result, search_preview_error, signup_start) are readable by one operator command in the 0509 checkout, so visit→signup conversion can be computed instead of only the last stage

observed: 2026-09-14 scout run. The RESEARCH CONTEXT Usage block reports every visit-stage source blind: "cloudflare-analytics UNAVAILABLE (token scope)", "/search query log: (empty — no dump at /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/0509-search-log)", "lp_run_audit: (empty)", "Inbound customer email: (none)". In the checkout, app/lib/funnel-measurement.server.ts emits home_view / search_preview_submit / search_preview_result / search_preview_error under the cleared Spec §4 allowlist with GPC opt-out — but the sink is logAppEvent() → console.log (app/lib/log.server.ts lines 45–59): ephemeral Worker logs. grep across scripts/ and app/ finds zero writers of the 0509-search-log dump path. Production runs FUNNEL_MEASUREMENT_ENABLED=1, so the events fire today and vanish. The direction metric (signups/week, D1 user.createdAt) sees only the funnel's last stage.

source: direction#4518 (acquisition is the 0509 direction, metric signups/week) + Usage block lines "cloudflare-analytics UNAVAILABLE (token scope)" and "/search query log: (empty — no dump at /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/0509-search-log)"

evidence:
- app/lib/funnel-measurement.server.ts (emitters, FUNNEL_DETAIL_ALLOWLIST, isGpcOptOut)
- app/lib/log.server.ts:45-59 (writeAppLog → console.*)
- scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs --json (direction metric; its --events-ndjson cross-check has no automated feed)
- RESEARCH CONTEXT Usage block 2026-09-14 (all visit-stage sources UNAVAILABLE/empty)
- direction#4518; market-signal 2026-09-14 (visit-stage volume absent from every report)

accept:
1. The already-emitted funnel event kinds become queryable for trailing-7d/30d counts per kind (home_view, search_preview_submit, search_preview_result, search_preview_error, signup_start) with NO new collected fields: the Spec §4 allowlist in funnel-measurement.server.ts must not widen (no query text, no IP — that exclusion is a privacy decision already made and stays).
2. Preferred organ: a Workers Analytics Engine binding on the existing Worker (writeDataPoint in the existing emit path) — no new Worker, no cron, no D1 migration. VERIFY the organ is available on the current plan before wiring; if it is not, stop and report the blocker rather than substituting any paid organ.
3. This PR must NOT touch migrations/**. If a D1 table turns out to be the only viable store, STOP: the expand/contract rule requires one issue per phase (new table first) — file that phase issue and link it instead of building here.
4. scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs gains a funnel section sourced from the queryable sink, next to the existing direction metric; docs/ga-metrics.md documents the read path.

verify:
```
node scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs --json | jq -e '.funnel.search_preview_submit_7d >= 0 and .funnel.home_view_7d >= 0'
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'https://0509.io/search?q=nike&country=all'
```

rollback: remove the binding and the metrics section; the emit path returns to console-only (behavior-neutral otherwise)

dedupe: none — #2869 is the Nish-reserved Cloudflare zone-analytics token (different organ, still unavailable); #3367 is suggestion-accept instrumentation; #3172/#3177 own onboarding slices; no open issue owns funnel-event persistence/queryability

impact: direction#4518 points all 0509 effort at acquisition measured by signups/week, yet the funnel's top — visits, searches, result rates, error rates — is invisible: every scout Usage block reports the visit stage UNAVAILABLE or empty, the A.7/A.8 machinery can only see the last stage, and BET 5's SEO seeds are chosen blind. The events are already emitted under a cleared privacy spec; only the read path is missing. The first real external users (market signal 2026-09-14: two signups used the product) make the visit stage worth measuring now.

product_surface: visit→signup funnel measurement (/, /search, /auth/signup)

Prior art:
- Workers console logs via logAppEvent — exists, ephemeral, not queryable after the fact; rejected as the read path.
- scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs --events-ndjson — exists (merged), accepts funnel records but only when a human hand-supplies them; no automated feed; rejected as-is because it never runs unattended.
- Cloudflare zone analytics (#2869) — would give visit counts but needs a zone.analytics.read token only Nish can mint; Nish-reserved, still unavailable; rejected for this issue (and this issue must not wait on it).
- Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon — #3338/#3301 adjacent; page-analytics only, no server funnel attribution; rejected.

funnel_stage: visit

termination: node scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs --json | jq -e '.funnel.search_preview_submit_7d >= 0 and .funnel.home_view_7d >= 0'

title: [stuck-packet] 2 alert-repair packet(s) older than 21600s with no terminated chain
body:
<!-- recurrence-of: Nishfleet/fleet-ops#6536 score=1.00 -->
Recurrence of Nishfleet/fleet-ops#6536 — that canonical is CLOSED with a delivering PR; a matching signal re-fired, so this is filed as a NEW claimable issue rather than a comment on a closed ticket (fleet-ops#5687).

metric: every firing alert packet in agent-state/alert-repair/ older than 21600s reaches a terminal disposition (terminated chain, filed repair claim, or reasoned drop with a logged decision); the unclaimed-packet count trends to 0, not up.

observed: the hourly escalation-drain found 2 webhook packet(s) with dispatch instants older than 2026-09-13T19:43:30Z that have NO terminated chain in chains.terminated.jsonl — the terminal ledger (chains.terminated.jsonl, written by the retired fleet-completion-canary mirror) stopped recording terminals, so the drain's absent() fallback re-listed the same packets hourly and the backlog only grew. This issue is the drain's own bounded escalation for the current burst (fleet-ops#5622).

evidence:
- drain run at 2026-09-14T01:43:30Z: 2 stuck packet(s), newest dispatch instant 2026-09-13T19:32:40Z
- terminal ledger: agent-state/alert-repair/chains.terminated.jsonl
- the packets are archived under agent-state/alert-repair/archived/stuck/ with a per-packet DISPOSITION decision line in actions.log (terminal=escalated-filed) — never silently deleted

accept:
- every packet in the dispositioned burst has a terminal disposition (chain, issue, or reasoned drop with a logged DISPOSITION line in actions.log).
- the underlying firing alerts are picked up by the normal alert-repair dispatch / intake repair-rung path; this issue is the escalation surface, not the repair worker itself.
- prevention mechanism (fleet-ops#366): the drain now files this escalation and archives + decision-logs the packets IN THE SAME RUN that detects them, so the hourly LOUD line cannot repeat forever for a settled burst; a NEW stuck packet after the filing starts a fresh filing.

termination: the burst is closed when every archived/stuck packet named by its DISPOSITION line has terminal=escalated-filed (or reasoned-drop) in actions.log and new dispatches resume producing terminal records in chains.terminated.jsonl; the drain's stuck set returns to 0 on the next hourly run.

Relates to #5622

Every one is a how-to; NONE answers the 2026 buyer's first question: "my AI (ChatGPT/Claude/an agent) can just check this — why this product?" The answer already exists, verified: the transformation research (§1.7, 2026-08-25) established it and this scout re-verified tonight — the Meta Ad Library answers 403 to a plain client (curl, 2026-09-13T22:5xZ: 403), an edge AI gets one point in time, no history, no 03:00 vigilance, no tamper-evident capture. Three facts, one page, zero new claims. Production note: #3166 (open) owns the deploy chain that puts guides live — this issue adds the 8th route into that existing pipe and changes no deploy machinery.

evidence:
- ls app/routes/ | grep guides → 7 routes, all how-to-*/meta-*, no AI-question guide (checkout 7cf3c9ccc, 2026-09-13T22:5xZ)
- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -A 'curl/8' 'https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?active_status=active&ad_type=all&country=ALL&q=nike&search_type=keyword_unordered' → 403 (2026-09-13T22:5xZ; first verified 2026-08-25, §1.7)
- direction#4518 (2026-09-09): acquisition, signups/week, unpaid distribution — "SEO/AEO measured+owned-content only"
- tests/guides-routes.test.ts + tests/guides-how-to-*.route.test.ts = the existing route-contract posture to extend

NEW route guides.can-ChatGPT-monitor-competitor-ads following the existing guide-route pattern (guides.how-to-track-competitor-ads.tsx is the nearest precedent), including the #3098 per-guide og:image (PNG) and structured-data posture. The slug is exact: /guides/can-ChatGPT-monitor-competitor-ads.
2. Content = the three fact blocks, from already-public copy only (no new claims, no new numbers — the §3.7 Nish voice gate stays untouched): (a) the 403 — a plain HTTP client gets 403 from the Meta Ad Library (re-verify at build time, record the date); (b) one point in time — your AI sees now, not what the offer said on 12 June; (c) unattended vigilance — somebody has to be there at 03:00, and "we checked 24 ads at 03:00 and nothing moved" is a claim only a system that ran can make. Then the honest conclusion — what an AI does well (summarising, drafting angles: the north-star's parity side) versus what only always-on capture owns — and the exit: the free anonymous /search preview, not a demo form.
3. Prevention/contract: extend tests/guides-routes.test.ts (registry) and add tests/guides-can-ChatGPT-monitor-competitor-ads.route.test.ts in the guides-how-to-*.route.test.ts posture (route renders, meta/og/structured data present, sitemap entry). Bare vitest, no --reporter flag (repo #3370 convention). No test is deleted; if any assertion must be reshaped rather than extended, add the #3414 convention test-removal-justified trailer to the committing commit.

observed: 2026-09-13T09:55Z, clean checkout 7cf3c9ccc. The moment the direction#4518 acquisition wave converts, its headline metric (signups/week) cannot answer WHERE from — which is exactly the question the next seed tranche (the /ads corpus issue) and every listing send need answered.

- app/lib/signup-source.ts L11–16 (contract), L103 (ALLOWED_SIGNUP_SOURCES), L129–146 (`allowlistedSignupSource`: exact constant | lowercase slug | ref:<eTLD+1> — new slugs pass WITHOUT touching the constant list)

title: fix(tests): root-cause the flaky P14 tests seen during the #4263 repair
body:
Part of #6032. Nish 2026-09-12: no glued or taped code; everything by the book.

These fail intermittently (pass solo, fail under parallel load or on hosted runners):
- tests/findings-ledger.test.sh line ~20 writes a fixed /tmp/findings-ledger.test.jsonl (collided or missing on PR #6012's hosted run). Use mktemp.
- tests/agent-cron-seat-rotation.test.sh (hosts the WORKDIR-guard scenario): "cat: write error: Broken pipe", a cat or printf piped into an early-exiting reader under pipefail. Use a here-string or file input.
- tests/fleet-deploy-check.test.sh: "off-main drift must invoke the sanctioned deploy to converge" fails under load. Find the timing assumption and remove it (no sleeps as a fix).

**Do:** fix each root cause. No retries and no sleeps. Grep tests/ for the same classes (fixed /tmp paths; `printf|grep -q` or `cat|` into early-exit readers under pipefail) and fix every instance.

**Files:** tests/ only.

termination: `grep -rnE '/tmp/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.(jsonl|json|log)' tests/*.test.sh` shows no fixed shared paths, and the three tests pass 5/5 under `xargs -P 8`.
accept: P14 green.

title: ci-standards-audit red on main, 2nd leg (2026-09-13): #5889 glob-host fails pi-issue-run-senior-review-routing (passes standalone); glm-5-3 cause fixed by PR #6426
body:
## Fault
`tests/ci-standards-audit.test.sh` exits 1 on current `origin/main` (2970807d2). Nested via `tests/fleet-gap-closure-loop.test.sh:919`:

```
FAIL: glm-5-3 must resolve to the live wired free seat, got {"provider":"zenmux","model":"z-ai/glm-5.3-free"}
```

The resolver picks the zenmux free seat; the assertion expects the wired cline free seat.

## Expected (per the assertion)
provider `cline`, model `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`.

## Actual
provider `zenmux`, model `z-ai/glm-5.3-free`.

## Verified
- Fails identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree at 2970807d2 — pre-existing, not caused by any in-flight diff.
- Full log line: `2029:FAIL: glm-5-3 must resolve to the live wired free seat, got {"provider":"zenmux","model":"z-ai/glm-5.3-free"}`

## Likely cause
Seat-ladder / health-fixture drift: a more recent seat change put zenmux's `z-ai/glm-5.3-free` ahead of (or in place of) cline's `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` for the `glm-5-3` slug, and the gap-closure-loop fixture/assertion was not updated — or the wiring regressed. Fixer should decide which side moved and re-align fixture + assertion with the live wiring (no test-only green).

The child PASSES standalone (exit 0, all four #6393 routing cases) — so this is parent-order / live-state dependence in the #5889 glob-host leg, not a routing regression. The 18:20Z #6474-merge P14 ran green while this exits 1 locally: CI stubs the LiteLLM proxy start (#4398) where this leg exercises the live one — that divergence is #6159's blindness, out of scope here.

evidence:
- 2026-09-13T19:01:57Z run, exit 1: `FAIL: watch.log must contain 'running on litellm/senior (weight=senior-review', got: [2026-09-13T19:01:24Z] pi-issue-run: test-issue target repo=0509 privacy=public` and `FAIL: 1 auto-hosted test file(s) failed via the #5889 glob host: pi-issue-run-senior-review-routing.test.sh` (full log: /tmp/scout-6163.out, scout run)

- #6163 original (2026-09-12, 2970807d2): the then-failing glm-5-3 assertion — since resolved

accept:
1. Name the mover for the watch.log / senior-review expectation — #6426 (public senior-review packets -> senior ladder) and #6474 (senior audits back on cursor-grok-4.6-high) are the candidate movers; cite the culprit with evidence in the PR.
2. Make `tests/ci-standards-audit.test.sh` exit 0 on pristine main WITH the #5889 glob-host leg: the child must pass standalone AND via the host. Prefer making the parent's test-issue leg hermetic (no dependence on live seat/proxy state) over editing expectations; no test-only green.

verify:


rollback: `git checkout origin/main -- tests/ci-standards-audit.test.sh tests/pi-issue-run-senior-review-routing.test.sh` plus any fixture the fixer touched; tests and fixtures only, no gates, no data.

title: search: the base /search?q= leg 500s intermittently — the honest-state contract must hold on every money-path leg (walk 2026-09-14 00:45Z; hubspot+allbirds 06:25Z)
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#3400 score=0.45 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#3400 (score 0.45). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: every leg of the anonymous /search money path — the base ?q= leg included — answers HTTP 200 with rendered results or the product's honest empty/delayed state, never the "Unexpected Server Error" shell, in 3 consecutive paced passes over the 7-domain recall set; a regression test drives the base-leg failure path and asserts the honest degrade.

observed: three independent 500 windows on the base ?q= leg, each recovering within minutes:
- 2026-09-14T00:45Z money-path walk: desktop session on /search?q=nike&country=all → HTTP 500 (blank render; console: "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 ()") while the mobile session on the identical URL returned 200 with results seconds earlier.
- 2026-09-14T06:20–06:27Z sequential run of the §1.8 six-domain recall set (BET 2's own termination set): hubspot.com → 500 and allbirds.com → 500 (19,994-byte "Something went wrong / Unexpected Server Error" shell) while gymshark/ridge/notion/oura → 200.
- 2026-09-14T06:33Z paced re-run (3 s gaps): hubspot 200×2, allbirds 200×2 — intermittent, same shape as #3400's selected-proof 500 (18:45Z, 200×5 by 19:01Z).
Not our edge rate-limiter: the anonymous limit is 20 req/10 min per IP, fail-open, and each window was ≤7 sequential requests. Trigger hypotheses, all in scope (the contract is trigger-agnostic): a cold-domain upstream Meta fetch failure escaping the search loader (the #2810 escape-to-ErrorBoundary pattern), or mid-deploy cache/D1 churn (the shell class #3454 documents for canaries).

evidence:
- /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/scout-money-path/20260914T004546Z/desktop-search.png (500, desktop, /search?q=nike&country=all)
- /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/scout-money-path/20260914T004546Z/mobile-search.png (200, same URL, same walk)
- recall run 2026-09-14T06:20Z: curl 'https://0509.io/search?q=hubspot.com&country=all' → 500; same for allbirds.com → 500; gymshark.com / ridge.com / notion.so / oura.com → 200
- paced re-run 06:33Z: hubspot 200 2.4s + 0.6s; allbirds 200 5.0s + 2.2s
- #3400 (open): the same intermittent-500 family on the selected=proof leg, seam named at app/routes/search.tsx isSelectionReload/selectedAdCapture (~lines 541-798)

accept:
1. The base ?q= leg never 5xx: loader failures (upstream Meta fetch throw or 429, cache/D1 hiccup) degrade to the honest state — results, the honest empty-state copy, or the live/recent/delayed/sample labels the product already promises — on desktop AND mobile render paths.
2. Regression test tests/search-base-leg-honest-state.test.ts: drives the base-leg loader with a failing upstream for a q= query and asserts 200 + the honest state (never the route ErrorBoundary), mirroring the #3400 test family for the selected leg.
3. Production check: zero 5xx and zero error-shells across 3 consecutive paced passes over the 7-domain set (gymshark.com, hubspot.com, ridge.com, allbirds.com, notion.so, oura.com, nike.com).
4. If the root seam is shared with #3400's, one fix may close both — cross-link the PRs; do not re-implement the same guard twice.

verify:
```
for d in gymshark.com hubspot.com ridge.com allbirds.com notion.so oura.com nike.com; do
  code=$(curl -sS --max-time 60 -o /tmp/leg.html -w '%{http_code}' -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) Chrome/126.0' "https://0509.io/search?q=$d&country=all") || exit 1
  [ "$code" = 200 ] || { echo "FAIL $d -> $code"; exit 1; }
  grep -qi 'Unexpected Server Error' /tmp/leg.html && { echo "FAIL $d error-shell"; exit 1; }
  sleep 3
done; echo PASS
```

rollback: revert the PR; loader-level degrade logic only, no data or schema touched.

title: fix(d1): renumber 0088_org_scoped_ownership to 0089 — duplicate 0088 reorder has blocked EVERY production deploy since 03:53Z
body:
Every `Deploy production` run on Nishfleet/0509 main has failed since at least 2026-09-10T03:53Z. `gh run list -R Nishfleet/0509 --workflow "Deploy production" --branch main --limit 40` shows **0 successes in the last 40 runs** (24 failure, 16 cancelled). Product merges are not reaching users at all.

**Root cause (probed, not inferred).** The `Generate D1 remote restore evidence` job fails with `source_backup_migration_ledger_stale`. `allowedProductionMigrationLedgers()` requires the production `d1_migrations` ledger to be a prefix of the repository migration list in **lexicographic** order. Two migrations share the number 0088:

- `migrations/0088_recreate_delivery_hot_path_indexes.sql` — already applied in production
- `migrations/0088_org_scoped_ownership.sql` — merged later (commit 9c8e250a, issue #2176 phase 1), never applied, and sorts **before** the applied one

Probe against the real production ledger from CI run 34439736283:

```
first_divergence_index: 98 allowed: 0088_org_scoped_ownership.sql ledger: 0088_recreate_delivery_hot_path_indexes.sql
suffix: null        # unappliedForwardMigrationSuffix -> null = reorder, not catch-up -> reject
```

A reorder is explicitly not recoverable by the forward-apply path, so this never self-heals.

**Fix, verified by the same probe.** Renaming the unapplied migration so it sorts last makes the ledger a proper prefix again and hands it to the normal forward-apply path:

```
AFTER-RENAME suffix: [ '0089_org_scoped_ownership.sql' ]
```

files:
- migrations/0088_org_scoped_ownership.sql -> migrations/0089_org_scoped_ownership.sql

do:
1. `git mv migrations/0088_org_scoped_ownership.sql migrations/0089_org_scoped_ownership.sql`. There are zero references to the old filename in the repo (`grep -rn 0088_org_scoped_ownership` returns nothing) — if that changes, update them.
2. Nothing else. Do not edit the migration's SQL: it creates the org table and nullable org_id columns, so it is order-independent with respect to the index migration that is already applied.
3. Open the PR, arm `gh pr merge --auto --squash`.

must-not:
- Do NOT edit `scripts/d1-migration-sync-check.lib.mjs`, `scripts/d1-remote-restore-evidence-core.mjs`, the baseline, the retired set, or `.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml`. The gate is correct — it caught a real ordering fault. Weakening it is a motive-1 violation and will be reverted.
- Do NOT apply the migration to production by hand. The deploy's forward-apply path does it.
- Do NOT renumber `0088_recreate_delivery_hot_path_indexes.sql` — it is already in the production ledger under that name.

termination:
`node -e "import('./scripts/d1-remote-restore-evidence-core.mjs').then(async m=>{const l=await import('./scripts/d1-migration-sync-check.lib.mjs');const fs=await import('node:fs');const repo=fs.readdirSync('./migrations').filter(f=>f.endsWith('.sql')).sort();const ledger=l.allowedProductionMigrationLedgers(repo)[0].slice(0,98).concat(['0088_recreate_delivery_hot_path_indexes.sql']);const s=m.unappliedForwardMigrationSuffix(ledger,repo);if(JSON.stringify(s)!==JSON.stringify(['0089_org_scoped_ownership.sql']))throw new Error('gate still rejects: '+JSON.stringify(s));console.log('OK',s)})"`

title: fix(deploy): D1 restore proof auto-refresh runs are cancelled by queue displacement — no exact-SHA evidence produced since 13:41Z
body:
observed 2026-09-11: every `D1 restore proof auto-refresh` run since 13:41Z is `cancelled` (34605774426, 34607797928, 34608926490, 34612462696, 34614766556, 34614869382). The workflow shares concurrency group `0509-production-provider-mutations` (queue max, cancel-in-progress false) with the long Deploy production runs; GitHub keeps only the newest QUEUED run per group, so each new push cancels the queued auto-refresh while a 20-45 min deploy occupies the group. Net effect: no exact-SHA evidence artifact is produced for any main SHA between nightly drills, and every deploy leans entirely on the in-run `generate_restore_evidence` fallback (which then also re-anchors the last-successful chain — see #2976).

impact: the push-trigger evidence design (P9-C) is effectively dead in busy periods; deploy critical path lengthens by the full in-run drill, and a single in-run drill failure strands the deploy.

worth checking: a dedicated concurrency group for the auto-refresh workflow (it mutates provider state via the backup/restore drill, so confirm the shared-group requirement before moving it), or a schedule-only mode with dispatch-on-idle, so pushes cannot displace it.

title: comeback-release organ is blind to #3737 wrapper-marker holds — seats held 8h+ with no probe, workers=0 next to ready work
body:
Live 2026-09-14 07:15-07:33Z, judge fable-check (cursor/kimi-k3):

**Fault.** Every worker seat lane was simultaneously held with zero probes:
- litellm/worker-cheap: spawn-fail corpse seat_dead=true (real 402 wall, correct)
- litellm/worker-capable + worker-private: wrapper bench expired 07:17/07:18Z, held by the fleet-ops#3737 'marker is latest evidence' branch
- devin/swe-2-max (the direct_fallback_seat literal): wrapper marker written 2026-09-13T22:52:44Z, usable_at expired 23:02:44Z, held by the same #3737 branch

Result: pi-issue-run exits no-seat for every packet (fleet-ops-6072 died 3x: 05:55Z, 07:21Z, 07:27Z). workers=0 with 0509 ready=12 and fleet-ops ready=13.

**Root cause.** fleet-seat-comeback-release sweeps LEDGER walls (bench_until/usable_at in ~/.local/state/pi-packet/seat-health/*.json). A #3737 wrapper-marker hold needs a fresh ledger observation (observed_at > marker written_at) to release, but the organ never probes these seats because their ledger carries NO wall — devin__swe-2-max.json has no usable_at field at all. The hold and the probe candidate list read different state. Sweeps run 64/hour and report probed=2 released=0 while marker-held seats accumulate.

**Proof the seat is fine.** Manual probe 07:29:31Z: echo 'Reply with exactly the word PONG' | pi --print --provider devin --model swe-2-max -> PONG in 6s. The ledger was NOT updated by that run (hook does not write outside the worker path) — the standing follow-through note 'a PONG clears it (the hook writes the record)' is wrong for bare probes.

**Accept.** fleet-seat-comeback-release's candidate list includes seats held ONLY by a fresh wrapper spawn-bench marker (usable_at expired, written_at within EMPTY_RUN_COUNT_WINDOW_S, no ledger wall); a successful tool-using probe writes source=comeback_release and the marker hold lifts. Regression test: fixture a marker-held seat with no ledger wall, run the sweep, assert probed >= 1 and the ledger gains a comeback_release row.

required: the sweep covers wrapper-marker holds, not only ledger walls
accept: workers recover without a hand probe; the 07:29 manual PONG class of repair is never needed again

title: seo: /ads programmatic corpus is capped by its 4 seed lists (121 domains, 127 published) — seed the next tranche to 300 via the existing #1549 nightly publisher (BET 5a)
body:
funnel_stage: visit
source: direction#4518

metric: production sitemap `<loc>https://0509.io/ads/...` count >= 300 (from 127 today), with every newly published page admitted by the existing #1549 publish floor (verified+likely >= 1), so no page ships empty — by construction, not by review.

observed: 2026-09-13T09:24Z, clean checkout 7cf3c9ccc (2026-09-12 22:35Z). The programmatic /ads/:domain publisher (issue #1549, BET 5a) is shipped and running: nightly 04:00, one 15-min wall-budget invocation, marks `truncated:true` and resumes, BET-2 gate (`gate: "bet2_inactive"` logging), 429-hardened (paced fetch + `SEARCH_429_RETRY_LIMIT` + `parseRetryAfterMs`), publish floor verified+likely>=1. But its INPUT corpus is 4 seed lists totalling 121 domains — `data/seed-lists/beauty-personal-care.json` (29), `festive-india-2026.json` (30), `saas-software.json` (36), `sneaker-resale.json` (26) — and the production sitemap lists exactly 127 /ads URLs. The machine has churned the whole curated corpus: the ceiling is the seed list, not the mechanism. BET 5a's own bar is "a curated seed list of a few thousand advertisers with real ad coverage". At the documented 15–30 domains/night (the #1549 truncated-resume arithmetic), ~180 added domains = 6–12 nights — sized to the existing mechanism, no acceleration needed.

evidence:
- data/seed-lists/*.json — 4 lists, 121 domains total (jq counts, 2026-09-13)
- app/lib/ads-domain-publisher.server.ts L77 (flattened all-lists run), L101–107 (15-min budget + truncated:true resume), L23–26 (BET-2 gate), L167–172 (publish floor)
- scripts/ads-domain-publisher.mjs — the #1549 local dry-run preflight with `--min-publish` exit-code verify gate
- https://0509.io/sitemap.xml — 127 `/ads/` locs (curl, 2026-09-13); production serves the 09-11+ build (e.g. /switch/magicbrief 200)
- #3280 (merged) — the add-two-seed-domains precedent; #2612 — the seed-quality edge (verified Meta page id)

accept:
1. Expand ONLY the existing seed-list mechanism: edit/extend `data/seed-lists/*.json` (the 4 existing categories and/or 1–2 new category lists in the same schema). No new publisher, no second orchestrator, no new script.
2. Add ~150+ additional advertiser domains (real, currently-adsvertised brands). Every added domain either passes the #1549 floor (verified+likely >= 1) within the tranche window or is removed from the list — the `ads_domain_published` / `ads_domain_skipped` / `ads_domain_failed` telemetry rows are the record; the lists stay honest.
3. Respect the existing rate limiting: the publisher's paced fetch/429-retry must not be weakened (issues #3156/#3278 own the limiter; this issue only widens the input).
4. No D1 migration. If (and only if) a listing-seed adjustment turns out to require one, use the 0081-style additive pattern (INSERT OR IGNORE, explicit rollback) and the fleet-ops#908 senior process; prefer the runtime publish path.
5. No edits to gate-owned paths (.github/workflows/**, .github/scripts/**, deploy gates); no test removed or skipped (if one were, the commit carries `test-removal-justified: <reason>`).

verify:
```bash
npm run seed:publisher -- --list=sneaker-resale --dry-run --min-publish=26   # the #1549 preflight, exit 0
node scripts/check-ads-timeline-links.mjs                                    # #1931 sweep still green
```

rollback: revert the seed-list JSON commits; already-published /ads pages persist (the #1549 cache) and the nightly simply churns fewer — no code rollback needed.

dedupe: none open (checked all 200 open issues + 11 open PRs). Related, not dupes: #3326 (edge caching — theirs), #3156/#3278 (429 limiting — theirs, publisher already self-throttles), #3322 (BET-2 gate state — theirs).

impact: the direction#4518 acquisition play triples the rankable /ads visit-stage inventory (~127→300) with zero new machinery; every published page is gated by the proof floor, so the "no phantom/empty SEO pages" promise holds.

product_surface: https://0509.io/ads/<domain> — the programmatic SEO wall (visit stage)

termination: c=$(curl -fsS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/'); echo "ads=$c"; [ "$c" -ge 300 ]

Prior art:
- Existing: the #1549 nightly publisher (shipped, running, BET-2-gated, 429-hardened, resumes truncation) + its dry-run preflight script.
- Tested: the #3280 merged PR (add asos.com + decathlon.com to sneaker-resale) — the exact seed-edit→publish loop, proven; #2612's GOAT.com verified-page-id work — the seed-quality lesson.
- Why rejected: building a second discovery/publish mechanism — the #3176 house rule ("reuse the existing fan-out, extend, do not add a second orchestrator") and #1549 already answers BET 5a mechanically; only the input list is small.

title: activation: prove the 2026-09-11/12 organic signups' watchlist actually ran — the 09-12 D1 snapshot showed it at 0 runs, 0 events, 0 digests (market signal)
body:
metric: every watchlist created since 2026-09-10 has >=1 watchlist_run row in prod D1 and a first digest scheduled; if a defect is found, the creation-path pickup test is extended to enumerate EVERY watchlist-creation route.

observed: 2026-09-13 02:45Z market signal: "First movement in days: 2 new signups + 1 watchlist (previous 7d: 0) — but 0 paid, 0 runs, 0 events, 0 digests. Usage hasn't followed yet." The signal's D1 snapshot was generated 2026-09-12T04:29Z (22.3h old at signal time), so it predates any later deploy. The watchlist was created ~2026-09-11/12. The activation queueing fix (PR "activation: queue the first scan on the two watchlist-creation paths that lacked it + real-migrations pickup test", issue #3380) is merged — whether it was deployed before this watchlist was created, and whether its first scan actually fired in production, is owned by no open issue or PR.

evidence:
- /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/cron-output/0509-daily-market-signal-2026-09-13.md (signal line verbatim; D1 snapshot generatedAt 2026-09-12T04:29Z)
- merged PR "activation: queue the first scan on the two watchlist-creation paths that lacked it + real-migrations pickup test (issue #3380)"
- e2e/activation-first-brief.spec.ts and tests/activation/ (the code path is test-proven; the live organic instance is not)
- migrations/0001_app.sql watchlist / watchlist_run schema (watchlist.created_at, watchlist_run.watchlist_id)

accept:
1. Read prod D1 (read-only SELECT): every watchlist created >= 2026-09-10 with its watchlist_run count. Mask any PII in the PR/issue output (ids and timestamps only).
2. If every such watchlist has >=1 run: close this issue with the query output as evidence (observe-to-close). Do not change code.
3. If a >24h-old watchlist still has 0 runs: identify the creation path it used, queue its first scan, and extend the #3380 creation-path pickup test to enumerate EVERY watchlist-creation route (route-file enumeration, the #3385 parity-test pattern) — prove the extended test fails without the queueing and passes with it. A bare code fix without the extended pickup test does not close this issue.
4. Confirm a first digest is scheduled for the watchlist (free plan is weekly; a pending delivery row at close time is fine).
5. If step 3 fires, the mechanism answer is the extended pickup test; if enumeration of every creation path proves impossible, state mechanism-impossible with the reason in the PR body for the conference to judge.

verify:
```
# observe: every post-2026-09-10 watchlist must have >=1 run
npx wrangler d1 execute DB --remote --json --command "SELECT w.id, w.created_at, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM watchlist_run r WHERE r.watchlist_id = w.id) AS runs FROM watchlist w WHERE w.created_at >= '2026-09-10' ORDER BY w.created_at DESC" | jq -e '.[0].results | length > 0 and (map(.runs) | all(. > 0))'

# if the fix branch fires: the extended creation-path pickup suite is green
npx vitest run tests/activation/
```

rollback: observe-only path has no rollback. Fix path is code + test revert (no data changes; read-only D1 access throughout).

dedupe: none — #3429 is the BET 1 guard cohort burst (synthetic watchlists); #3177 measures the NEW join path (epic #3172, PRs #3376/#3443 in flight); #3380 is closed (the code fix this verifies in prod); #2919/#2908 predate this watchlist and concern the wiped fixture substrate, not the post-wipe organic signup.

impact: 0509's entire growth story right now is 2 organic signups and 1 watchlist — the first real funnel instances the product has ever had (direction#4518, metric signups/week; live signups_30d=2, last signup 2026-09-11T21:35Z). The last known state of that watchlist was 0 runs. If activation queueing did not reach it, the only real users get no brief and no digest, and signups/week reads zero next week no matter what acquisition ships.

title: seo: the five originally-shipped bare-brand /ads URLs (nike, allbirds, nykaa, lenskart, mamaearth) 404 — 301 them to their domain-keyed pages (roadmap §1.2)
body:
metric: https://0509.io/ads/{nike,allbirds,nykaa,lenskart,mamaearth} each answer 301 to their domain-keyed successor (/ads/nike.com, /ads/allbirds.com, /ads/nykaa.com, /ads/lenskart.com, /ads/mamaearth.com), pinned by a route test; unmapped dotless slugs keep 404ing.

observed: 2026-09-14T06:15Z and 06:55Z live probes: all five bare-brand URLs → 404 ("Not found") while the domain-keyed forms render 200 with populated walls (/ads/nike.com: live ad wall + offer history). The 2026-08-25 transformation campaign verified these five as the shipped /ads surface: "Only 5 of these exist (nike, nykaa, allbirds, lenskart, mamaearth)". The corpus has since moved to domain-keyed URLs — internal links, the sitemap (286 dotted /ads locs) and the loader's own alias logic all use dotted domains — and the dotless legacy slugs fall out of brand resolution before the cache-miss 301-to-/search path can fire (ads.$domain.tsx "no page ships empty" redirect block), so a shipped public URL now dead-ends instead of redirecting.

evidence:
- live: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://0509.io/ads/nike → 404 (same for allbirds, nykaa, lenskart, mamaearth; re-confirmed 06:55Z)
- live: https://0509.io/ads/nike.com → 200, populated wall
- transformation campaign §1.2 (2026-08-25): the five bare-brand URLs verified as the shipped /ads pages
- app/routes/ads.$domain.tsx cache-miss redirect block (issue #1282) and app/routes/ad-aggression-redirect.ts — the in-repo 301 pattern (issue #2022 precedent)

accept:
1. A small legacy-slug map in the ads route (the five §1.2 slugs) 301s each to its dotted canonical — the ad-aggression-redirect.ts pattern; no new machinery, no table.
2. Dotless slugs NOT in the map keep today's 404 — never guess a TLD.
3. Route test asserting the five redirects (status 301 + exact Location target each).
4. No sitemap changes: dotted canonicals only, as today.

verify:
```
for pair in nike:nike.com allbirds:allbirds.com nykaa:nykaa.com lenskart:lenskart.com mamaearth:mamaearth.com; do
  bare=${pair%%:*}; dom=${pair##*:}
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 25 -w '%{http_code}' "https://0509.io/ads/$bare")
  loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 25 -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://0509.io/ads/$bare")
  [ "$code" = 301 ] && [ "$loc" = "https://0509.io/ads/$dom" ] || { echo "FAIL $bare -> $code $loc"; exit 1; }
done; echo PASS
```

rollback: revert the PR; additive redirect logic, no data touched.

dedupe: none open — corpus grep for bare-brand /ads redirect work returns nothing; #3166 is sitemap/llms-advertised 404s (different URLs, deploy-staleness cause); #3356/#3357 are corpus growth and timeline provisioning.

impact: the five most historically-linked brand pages (the homepage proof mechanic pre-redesign, early compare pages and listing drafts pointed here) now hard-404 for anyone arriving from the pre-move era — the same equity loss #2022 chose to prevent for /ad-aggression. Cheap, pattern exists, protects the indexed surface the acquisition direction (direction#4518) drives strangers to.

product_surface: /ads/:domain legacy entry points

termination: npx vitest run tests/ads-legacy-slug-redirects.test.ts

funnel_stage: visit

title: test(deploy-gate): the +x gate only checks the first token of each run: — a multiline run: block invoking ./scripts/foo.sh on line 2+ escapes the net
body:
PR #3435 widened the 0509#3330 +x gate to every job in deploy-production.yml and takes the first token of each `run:` string. A `run: |` block whose script invocation sits on line 2 or later is missed (only the block's first token is checked). Live check by the senior reviewer: zero such lines today — all 8 `./scripts/` refs are single-line; the two multiline blocks use `node scripts/…` (no +x needed). So this is hardening, not a live hole.

title: intake claims frozen 3h+ by graphql-low sidecar gate: workers=0 with ready=46 — main gate never glides to human-gh reads
body:
## Fault

Since ~2026-09-13T23:30Z the pi-intake main gate (bin/pi-intake-tick.sh:1617-1645) has held claims on nearly every tick: 17 of 18 ticks in the trailing 3h printed `gh rate-limit low ... holding claims this tick — gate: gh_rate_limit low`. Result at 2026-09-14T02:20Z: **0 active pi-issue@ workers with agent-ready=21 (0509) + 25 (fleet-ops)**.

## Evidence (verbatim, 2026-09-14T02:24-02:36Z)

- `journalctl --user -u pi-intake@0509.service -u pi-intake@fleet-ops.service --since -3h -o cat | grep -c 'holding claims'` → 20 (17 gh rate-limit, 3 no usable seat)
- Sidecar `agent-state/pi-intake/gh-rate-limit.json`: top-level `low:1, remaining:30, limit:30` (search-pool mirror) while `resources.core.remaining=4651/5000 low:0`, `resources.graphql.remaining=819/5000 low:1`. The hold is driven by GRAPHQL at 16%, and the pool re-trips within minutes of each hourly reset (reset 02:32:43Z passed; 02:36Z tick printed 'resets in 158s' — a NEW low window).
- The #5489 glide (reads fall back to human-gh, writes held) exists only in the PRE-check (tick lines 393-468, reads `resources.core`). The main gate still hard-holds ALL claims on the sidecar's top-level low flag — it never glides.

## Two questions to answer in the fix

1. WHO burns 4200+ graphql points/hour? (merge-queue batches, reconciler, judges' `gh pr view --json`, measure.sh). Tabulate consumers before touching thresholds (evidence rule).
2. The main gate should glide to human-gh reads exactly like the #5489 pre-check, or read `resources.graphql` with a sane threshold — never hold the whole fleet on a 16% graphql dip while core is 93% free.

## Constraints

- No duct tape: do not just raise the threshold or delete the gate (the 2026-09-11 App-token 5000/hr exhaustion, fleet-ops#5489, is the failure this gate protects).
- accept: one intake tick during a graphql-low window shows claimed+spawned via the human-gh glide path, with writes still held; a regression test pins the glide for the main gate.

title: test(d1): migration 0102_podcast (PR #3434) broke the d1-remote-restore-evidence ledger pins — every Deploy production run dies at the Test step
body:
observed 2026-09-13T22:49Z+ (run 34787898963 at main 65776e216, and run 34786485796's successors): job `Deploy Worker`, step `Test` — `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` fails 2 of 10139 tests, so every `Deploy production` run fails before Gate C. This is the current sole Test-step blocker; the no-time-bomb fixture pair it previously hid was defused by #3420.

**Root cause (verified in the run log and on main, not inferred):** PR #3434 (podcast show-RSS connector, merged 2026-09-13T22:49Z) added migration `0102_widen_source_target_connector_podcast.sql`. The pinned ledger fixtures in `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` still end at 0101/0096, so the pins no longer match reality:

1. `pins 0096 interleave planner behavior...` — `expect(productionNames.at(-1)).toBe("0096_error_reports.sql")` (line ~1609) receives `0102_widen_source_target_connector_podcast.sql`. The test's modeled production ledger is built from the current repository migration list, which now carries 0102.
2. `plans catch-up when production applied 0098_gdelt before 0098_bluesky landed` — planner returns `apply_forward_suffix` with migrations `[0098_bluesky, 0099_threads, 0100_hn, 0101_pinterest, 0102_podcast]` (line ~1716 pin expects the same list WITHOUT 0102). The planner behavior is correct — production DOES need 0102 applied; the expected array is stale.

prior art: the same pins were extended for each prior migration (0099–0101 appear in the expected arrays); #3315/#3174 established the order-exception groups the pins guard. This is the mechanical follow-up #3434 missed — no planner change is expected.

do:
1. Update the pinned fixture arrays in `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` to include `0102_widen_source_target_connector_podcast.sql` in the modeled production and repository ledgers and in the expected `apply_forward_suffix` migrations (lines ~1600–1720), mirroring how 0101_pinterest is pinned.
2. Run the full file: `npx vitest run tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` must be green with both pins updated and no assertion weakened or deleted.
3. If the planner genuinely mis-plans with 0102 present (not just stale expectations), STOP and comment — that is a different fault; do not bend a pin to a wrong planner output.

must-not: weaken, skip, delete or make non-fatal any gate assertion; touch `scripts/d1-migration-sync-check.lib.mjs` ORDER_EXCEPTIONS unless step 3's stop-condition fires; rename migrations; edit anything outside `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts`.

termination: `npx vitest run tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` green on the PR, and one `Deploy production` run on main reaches `success` with every gate assertion unmodified.

accept: the two named tests fail before the fixture update (run 34787898963 is the evidence) and pass after; `gh run list -R Nishfleet/0509 --workflow 'Deploy production' --limit 1` shows `success`; no ORDER_EXCEPTIONS edit in the diff unless the stop-condition fired with a comment.

impact: this gates the whole deploy chain — the reopened deploy-fault issues #3409/#3412/#3413 can only close legally on the first green production run, and #3315's termination (green run on main) is still unmet. Every push retries this deterministic reject; land the pin update.


title: [rulebook-redteam] Pre-implementation contract omits Pi from its binding list and keys its packet flow on deleted launcher machinery
body:
The mandatory pre-implementation contract (`nish-vault/_system/shared-memory/pre-implementation-contract.md`), which the CLAUDE.md generated block (`nish-preimplementation-contract`) binds 'for Claude and every Claude subagent' and which /home/nish/AGENTS.md's context table instructs every Pi agent to read as canonical, opens by binding only 'Codex, Claude, Hermes, OpenCode, Cursor, MiniMax, and Command Code' — Pi, the runtime that now does the implementation work ('Everything runs through Pi, directly. No launchers.', Nish 2026-08-23), is absent, so a strict Pi worker can read itself out of the stop-for-approval rule entirely. Worse, section 5 ('Sealed Worker Packets Are Already-Approved Plans') keys the already-approved-plan flow on 'a sealed implementation packet delivered through an approved worker launcher' — the fleet control plane and the implementation-worker-* launcher layer were DELETED on 2026-08-23 (per the CLAUDE.md shared-fleet-routing block), and packets now travel via `pi --print`/`pi-systemd-run` stdin. The always-loaded stop/go switch for non-trivial work therefore doesn't name the fleet's primary workers and describes a dispatch flow that no longer exists. Proposed fix: amend the binding list to include Pi and reword section 5 to the current packet path, landing the amendment as a durable decision per the contract's own Enforcement section (changes require Nish's request).

**Evidence:** Contract opening: 'This rule is automatic and non-negotiable for Codex, Claude, Hermes, OpenCode, Cursor, MiniMax, and Command Code on both Mac and VPS' (no Pi); section 5: 'A sealed implementation packet delivered through an approved worker launcher has already satisfied sections 1 and 2'; vs /home/nish/.claude/CLAUDE.md shared-fleet-routing block: 'The fleet control plane AND the `implementation-worker-*` launcher layer are both DELETED.'

**Verified live today** (`nish-vault/_system/shared-memory/pre-implementation-contract.md`):

title: auto-revert: halt filer creates AUTO-REVERT HALT issues WITHOUT the auto-revert-halt label, so dedupe and close-halts-on-green are both blind (104 duplicates)
body:
## Symptom
`.github/workflows/auto-revert.yml` files halts with `gh issue create ... --label auto-revert-halt` (line ~121) but the issues land with NO labels. Example: #2923, filed 2026-09-11T10:29:26Z by run https://github.com/Nishfleet/0509/actions/runs/34589436185 under `AUTO_REVERT_PAT` (nish3451). Its timeline has no `labeled` event at creation; the only label event is a manual one at 10:43Z.

Consequences, both mechanical:
- The dedupe at line ~116 (`gh issue list --label auto-revert-halt`) never finds an existing halt, so every failed deploy files a NEW halt: 104 open `AUTO-REVERT HALT` issues by title, 0 by label as of 10:40Z.
- The close-halts-on-green step from #2897 closes by `--label auto-revert-halt` and would have closed NOTHING on the first green deploy.

nish3451 hand-labelled all 104 open halts at 10:43Z so the closer works for the current backlog. The filer is still broken for every future halt.

## Do
- Reproduce: run the create line under the same PAT in a scratch issue and inspect `gh api repos/.../issues/N -q .labels`. Check `gh label create` output (it likely errors "already exists" and is swallowed) and whether `gh issue create --label` silently drops a label it cannot resolve under this token (gh resolves labels via GraphQL before create).
- Fix the class: after `gh issue create`, verify the label with `gh api .../issues/$num -q '.labels[].name'` and `gh issue edit --add-label` if missing; fail the step loud if the label still is not present (no silent degraded mode). Apply the same guard to the comment/dedupe path.
- Collapse the duplicates: one open halt per red streak; the dedupe must key on the label AND fall back to a title search so an unlabelled survivor never re-opens the flood.
- Test in `tests/` alongside the existing auto-revert workflow tests: assert the create step is followed by the label verification.

## Evidence
`gh api repos/Nishfleet/0509/issues/2923/timeline -q '.[]|select(.event=="labeled")|"\(.created_at) \(.actor.login)"'` -> only 2026-09-11T10:43:01Z nish3451.
Related: #2897 (closer), #2840 (release-proof gate).

That explains both the silently dropped label and this hard failure. Fix the class: mint the token via the nishfleet-worker GitHub App (actions/create-github-app-token) or a token with working GraphQL access, and add a step that asserts `gh api graphql` works under the token before any filing.

Evidence 2026-09-11 16:05Z, auto-revert run 34619949642 on main 09cbadcc: the workflow still aborts on `gh pr remove-label` (not a gh subcommand; the script's own comment says every run after opening the revert PR dies here) — the fix is `gh pr edit --remove-label`. Three AUTO-REVERT HALT issues sit open (#2909, #2917, #2923: 'main moved after the red commit'), i.e. the fleet's red-main safety net has been failing for days and reports it only as closed loops nobody reads. Under the standing rule (vault global-standing-rules.md, 2026-09-11: nothing fails silently) this organ must (1) use the documented gh form, (2) never halt silently — a halt must file ONE agent-ready issue with the red commit and the reason, deduped, and write the LOUD line the judges read, (3) carry a drill test that simulates 'main moved after the red commit' and asserts the issue + line appear. title: seo: asos.com + decathlon.com are in the sneaker-resale fixture but not the seed list — drift gate is blind to their removal
body:
Found in the #3229 reviewer round (PR #3259). The drift gate's missing-direction check is anchored on `data/seed-lists/sneaker-resale.json` (cluster membership = seed-list ∩ live sitemap), but `tests/fixtures/sneaker-resale-indexable-domains.snapshot.json` and `SNEAKER_RESALE_BRAND_PAGES` also carry `asos.com` and `decathlon.com`, which are not in the seed list. If either ever drops out of the fixture/hub array while still live in the sitemap, no alarm fires — the exact silent-fallback class #3229 closed for seed-listed domains.

The hub test documents their presence as intentional (domains that predate the seed list), so the fix is a product-data call, not a code change:

accept:
- Decide whether asos.com and decathlon.com are sneaker-resale cluster members; if yes, add them to `data/seed-lists/sneaker-resale.json` so the drift gate covers them; if no, remove them from the fixture + `SNEAKER_RESALE_BRAND_PAGES` and the hub test's intentional-exclusion comment.

blocked-proposal (pi-issue-0509-3280)

This issue is a product-data call (brand/cluster membership for ASOS + Decathlon in the sneaker-resale cluster). The acceptance lists two paths; the agent cannot pick between them because either choice changes what the cluster's brand positioning asserts publicly, which is a reserved-class decision.

## Current state (live proof against `bdac8c5d6`)

The two domains are treated as sneaker-resale cluster members in the product surface and excluded from the cluster definition in the data:

- **Product surface (in-cluster):**
  - `SNEAKER_RESALE_BRAND_PAGES` (`app/components/sneaker-resale-landing.tsx:32-33`) — `asos.com`, `decathlon.com` render as brand tiles on `/sneaker-resale`.
  - `tests/sneaker-resale.route.test.ts:64` — `["nike.com", "adidas.com", "asos.com", "decathlon.com"]` is the explicit "every brand tile links to a real `/ads/:domain`" assertion from #1290.
  - `tests/fixtures/sneaker-resale-indexable-domains.snapshot.json:30-31` — both domains are in the indexable sitemap snapshot.
  - `tests/fixtures/indexable-ads-domains.snapshot.json:16,35` — both domains are also in the wider sitemap snapshot.
  - `app/lib/brand-categories.ts:31,121` — `decathlon.com` is "Sport & footwear" (the sneaker-resale cluster category); `asos.com` is "Fashion & accessories".

- **Cluster definition (out-of-cluster):**
  - `data/seed-lists/sneaker-resale.json` — 24 domains; `asos.com` and `decathlon.com` are NOT in the list. `sourceNote` says "established sneaker/resale Meta advertisers" — both qualify under that rationale (ASOS and Decathlon both advertise sneakers at scale on Meta).
  - `tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh:113-119` — the drift gate computes `live_cluster = (live sitemap /ads) ∩ (seed list)`. Because `asos.com` and `decathlon.com` are not in the seed list, `live_cluster` never contains them, and the gate is blind to their removal from fixture + hub array while still live in the sitemap (the silent-fallback class #3229 closed for seed-listed domains).

- **Hub test rationale (`tests/sneaker-resale-hub-links.test.ts:38-39`):**
  - "The snapshot is sitemap-derived and can include domains (asos.com, decathlon.com) that predate the seed list; the seed list is the cluster source of truth, the snapshot is the indexable filter applied to it."
  - Note: the comment claims the snapshot is the seed-list filter, but the drift gate does not actually intersect the snapshot with the seed list — the gate uses `(sitemap ∩ seed)` as `live_cluster`, and the fixture is checked against `live_cluster` (not against `seed`). The hub test itself uses the full snapshot directly. So the comment documents an intent that the drift gate does not implement.

## Both paths in concrete detail

**Option A — yes, they are cluster members (recommended, additive, reversible):**
1. Add `{ "domain": "asos.com", "brand": "ASOS" }` and `{ "domain": "decathlon.com", "brand": "Decathlon" }` to `data/seed-lists/sneaker-resale.json`. Bump `asOf` to today; amend `sourceNote` to note that established sneaker retailers are included alongside sneaker manufacturers and resale-first brands.
2. Drift gate now covers them: if either drops out of the fixture or hub array while still live in the sitemap, `stale_in_fixture` fires; if the snapshot drifts ahead of the live sitemap (current #3229 mode), `missing_from_fixture` still fires correctly.
3. Hub test comment becomes accurate — the snapshot is now actually the indexable filter applied to the seed list (the drift gate is already effectively doing this since `asos.com`/`decathlon.com` were the only domains in the snapshot not in the seed list).
4. No product-surface change. No test in `tests/sneaker-resale.route.test.ts` needs to move; `#1290`'s brand tiles still ship.
5. Reversible: revert the seed-list PR.

**Option B — no, they are not cluster members (deletion):**
1. Remove `asos.com` and `decathlon.com` from `SNEAKER_RESALE_BRAND_PAGES` (`app/components/sneaker-resale-landing.tsx:32-33`).
2. Remove them from `tests/fixtures/sneaker-resale-indexable-domains.snapshot.json:30-31`.
3. Drop them from the `["nike.com", "adidas.com", "asos.com", "decathlon.com"]` linked-domains loop in `tests/sneaker-resale.route.test.ts:64`. The `adsLinkCount >= 4` assertion still passes (Nike + Adidas = 2 + 22 others = 24 ≥ 4), so this assertion is fine; the #1290 proof surface narrows to the manufacturer/resale brands the seed list names.
4. Update or remove the "predate the seed list" comment block in `tests/sneaker-resale-hub-links.test.ts:38-39` (no longer an exception if the seed list excludes them).
5. Both domains still ship on `/ads/asos.com` and `/ads/decathlon.com` (sitemap-indexable, in `tests/fixtures/indexable-ads-domains.snapshot.json`) and in `app/lib/brand-categories.ts` — only the sneaker-resale hub tile list narrows. /brands coverage unchanged.
6. The drift gate remains unchanged and still has the same blind-spot shape (it is anchored on the seed list, which is correct under this option; the gate's behavior is fine, the issue is purely product positioning).
7. Reversible: revert the PR.

## Why I recommend A (data alignment, no product-surface change)

Both paths are reversible and small. The drift-gate bug in the issue title is fixed by either path (B by removing the blind-spot exception; A by promoting the exception into the gate's source-of-truth). The deciding factor is brand positioning:

- The product surface already treats them as cluster members (landing tiles, #1290 proof, hub fixture). Removing them is a brand-positioning move away from "fashion retailers are sneaker-resale-adjacent" and toward "only sneaker manufacturers + dedicated resale platforms count."
- The seed list's own rationale (`sourceNote`) supports including them — "established sneaker/resale Meta advertisers."
- ASOS and Decathlon are the two highest-traffic "fashion/footwear retailers with real sneaker catalogues" the site already names on `/sneaker-resale`. Demoting them from the hub tile list while keeping their `/ads/` pages live would create the second kind of inconsistency (#3229's closing rationale was the opposite direction — adding domains to keep hub and live surface aligned).
- Option A is purely additive data, with no PR touching a public-facing component or test assertion. Option B touches 4 files including a public-facing array.

## Agent cannot pick

Either choice changes what the cluster publicly says about itself. Reserved class (product direction / brand positioning). Recorded as `agent-blocked` so the next lane can pick up the work after the decision lands.

body:

metric: A stranger arriving from a "MagicBrief alternative / shut down" search resolves /switch/magicbrief to a 200 page whose served HTML contains the differentiated MagicBrief→Canva wind-down truth, and sitemap.xml lists that 200 URL.

Issue #3092's own evidence asserts the /switch/ family is "all indexed" — for the MagicBrief trigger it currently is not.

evidence:
- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' https://0509.io/switch/magicbrief → "301 https://0509.io/compare" (2026-09-12T00:04Z)
- curl -sS https://0509.io/compare | grep -ioc magicbrief → 0 (2026-09-12T00:04Z)
- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' https://0509.io/compare/magicbrief → "301 https://0509.io/compare"
- git 13672ea45 (publish /switch/magicbrief, #2887) then 3bad1af09 "retire the legacy switch/magicbrief 301 now that the page is live" (#3035) — the 301 is back
- https://0509.io/sitemap.xml — no magicbrief URL (142 locs, 2026-09-12T00:04Z)

accept:
1. Either restore the #2887-approved wind-down copy at /switch/magicbrief (200), or ship /compare/magicbrief — in both cases /switch/magicbrief must 301 to exactly that 200 page, never to the bare hub.
2. The 200 canonical appears in the generated sitemap.xml.
3. Prevention mechanism (this is a regression fix): before adding any check, verify whether an existing route/SEO canary or test already covers "compare/switch route returns 200 AND the tool name appears AND the route is in the sitemap" (the #3065-adjacent canaries, the compare-citation tests); only add the assertion where none exists, in the existing suite — no new checker organ.
4. If the shipped copy changes beyond #2887's approved text, follow the #3094 mechanism (pin to a NISH approval record with a drift gate); verbatim restoration of approved text needs no new gate.
5. Standing: any removed/skipped test carries a `test-removal-justified: <reason>` trailer; any gate-owned path edit (.github/**, CODEOWNERS, ratchet ceilings) needs a `gate-integrity-attest: <40-hex head sha>` comment from a repo admin whose identity ≠ the PR author (nishfleet-worker[bot] cannot attest).

```
t=$(curl -sS -m 15 -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' https://0509.io/switch/magicbrief); u=${t:-https://0509.io/switch/magicbrief}; c=$(curl -sSL -m 20 -o /tmp/mb-final.html -w '%{http_code}' "$u"); [ "$c" = 200 ] && grep -qi magicbrief /tmp/mb-final.html && curl -sS -m 20 https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -qF "${u#https://0509.io}"
```

rollback: revert the PR (route + sitemap only; no data, no migrations).

impact: MagicBrief is the one verified shutdown in the category and third parties (superscale.ai, peachblue.io, thekeyword.co) already rank for its alternatives — the highest-intent switching query there is. Today that visitor lands on a generic hub that never says "MagicBrief" (BET 8: "MagicBrief→the wind-down + the Canva bundle").

The symptom was a **deploy-lag stale edge**, not a code fault: main's `app/routes.ts` was already correct when the issue was observed at 00:04Z, and the site self-healed before PR #3141 landed. Expected: this worker's `GH_TOKEN` has no Workflows permission by design, so I cannot dispatch a CI run to watch the new assertion execute in Actions. The artifact merged as **#3141** (`f94437081`, on main since 2026-09-12T03:45:48Z). That PR carried `Relates to #3111`, not `Closes #3111`, so GitHub never auto-closed the issue — correct for the `test(...)` trailer class, but it leaves the issue OPEN with all work done.

Loose ends: none on the work itself; only the close action is outstanding.

DECISION (judge opus-5 2026-09-12T06:48Z): **not a duplicate of #3091** — the evidence is URL-family-specific (/switch/magicbrief and /compare/magicbrief both 301 to /compare, whose served HTML contains 0 occurrences of "magicbrief", and neither URL is in sitemap.xml's 142 locs). #3091 does not cover that trigger. The possible-duplicate marker (score 0.43) is below anything decisive; clearing it.

Scope constraint, so this does not collide with the MagicBrief wind-down decision already tracked on #2127: this ticket owns the **SEO consistency defect only** — a trigger that 301s to a page which cannot satisfy the query is broken either way. Two acceptable resolutions, worker picks whichever #2127 implies at implementation time:
 (a) if MagicBrief content stays: serve /switch/magicbrief 200 with the wind-down truth and add it to sitemap.xml; or

must-not: invent new comparative marketing copy, or assert anything about MagicBrief not already sourced on #2127.

decision-resolved: de-duplicated + scoped. This is a technical consistency fix, not a product-direction call, so it does not go to Nish.

title: Orphan Actions registration: standing-rules-drift.yml is state=active with no file on main (branch claim/issue-1145 died) — the #1161 orphan detector cannot see its own repo
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/fleet-ops#4454 score=0.50 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/fleet-ops#4454 (score 0.50). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: every GitHub Actions workflow registration on Nishfleet/fleet-ops with state=active has its file present on the default branch (origin/main), and a standing self-scan exists so the orphan class cannot recur silently (fleet-ops#1161 class).

observed: 2026-09-12T01:20Z — the Actions API lists `.github/workflows/standing-rules-drift.yml` as state=active, but the file does not exist on origin/main (`git show origin/main:.github/workflows/standing-rules-drift.yml` → "path does not exist"). Its only runs are two pull_request runs on the now-deleted branch `claim/issue-1145` (run 33084901690 2026-08-27T14:55:02Z, run 33086255407 2026-08-27T15:09:25Z, both success). 19 of 20 active registrations have files on main; this is the only orphan. The orphan-workflow-detector built for exactly this class (fleet-ops#1161, audit findings 3+4) has ZERO runs on fleet-ops and its default target set hardcodes four other repos (line 83: fleet2, egress-probe, 0509-telemetry, siterep) — it cannot see its own repo's orphan. This scout burned a full investigation cycle on the phantom registration before proving it dead.

evidence:
- `gh api repos/Nishfleet/fleet-ops/actions/workflows --jq '.workflows[] | select(.state=="active") | .path'` → includes .github/workflows/standing-rules-drift.yml (20 active registrations, 19 files on main)
- `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/standing-rules-drift.yml` → fatal: path does not exist in 'origin/main'
- `gh run list -R Nishfleet/fleet-ops --workflow standing-rules-drift` → only event=pull_request, headBranch=claim/issue-1145, last run 2026-08-27T15:09:25Z
- `.github/workflows/orphan-workflow-detector.yml` line 83: `printf 'Nishfleet/fleet2\nNishfleet/egress-probe\nNishfleet/0509-telemetry\nNishfleet/siterep\n' >> repos.txt` (fleet-ops absent)
- `gh run list -R Nishfleet/fleet-ops --workflow "Orphan workflow detector" --limit 12` → no runs ever on fleet-ops

accept:
1. Add `bin/fleet-workflow-registration-scan` (repo arg, default Nishfleet/fleet-ops): lists ACTIVE Actions registrations via the API, diffs against `.github/workflows/**` on the default branch (fetch origin/main to a temp ref; do not require a clean working checkout), writes a report to /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/FLEET-ORPHAN-WORKFLOW-REGISTRATIONS.md, exits 1 when an orphan exists and 0 when clean; `--report` mode always exits 0 after writing the report.
2. Wire it as a fleet-heartbeat-tier1 canary step (bin/-side only; do NOT edit `.github/workflows/**` for the core deliverable) so it runs on the existing heartbeat cadence and lands in the tier-1 rc summary like every other canary.
3. Regression test `tests/workflow-registration-inventory.test.sh` that (a) proves the scanner flags a synthetic orphan (mocked API payload) and (b) proves a clean inventory exits 0. Register the test in the P14 test listing (see #3482/#3483 convention).
4. File the #1161-format orphan report for the standing-rules-drift registration as its own issue, containing the one-command remediation for Nish: deleting/disabling a registration is irreversible and admin-gated per #1161 — a worker must NOT attempt Actions-settings mutations; the deliverable is the mechanism + report + runbook, not the deletion.
5. If the worker chooses the alternative mechanism of extending the reusable detector's default target set to include Nishfleet/fleet-ops (edits `.github/workflows/**`), that PR additionally requires the `gate-integrity-attest: <40-hex current head sha>` comment from a repository admin whose identity differs from the PR author (nishfleet-worker[bot] cannot attest); no test may be removed or skipped without a `test-removal-justified: <true reason>` trailer in the commit.

verify:
```bash
gh api repos/Nishfleet/fleet-ops/actions/workflows --jq '[.workflows[] | select(.state=="active")] | length'   # 20 today
bash tests/workflow-registration-inventory.test.sh
bin/fleet-workflow-registration-scan --report && grep -q "standing-rules-drift.yml" /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/FLEET-ORPHAN-WORKFLOW-REGISTRATIONS.md
```

rollback: remove the canary step from fleet-heartbeat-tier1, the bin helper, and the test; the report file is agent-state scratch. No Actions settings or data are mutated, so rollback is pure file removal.

Prior art: `.github/workflows/orphan-workflow-detector.yml` (fleet-ops#1161, audit findings 3+4) already implements orphan detection and was proven in the 2026-08-27 audit that found auto-merge-arm.yml orphans on fleet2/egress-probe/0509-telemetry (#1161, closed: freeze + delete executed there). It is rejected as-is for this gap because (1) its default target set hardcodes 4 repos and excludes fleet-ops (line 83), (2) it is reusable-call-only with no scheduled self-scan, so it has zero runs on fleet-ops, and (3) its report path files in the TARGET repo, which is right for callers but left the self-repo blind spot open.

dedupe: none — open #3656 covers wiring the standing-rules drift TEST (the function the orphan once carried); #1687 is the orphaned-test-file class; #3128 is fleet2 phantom PRs. No open issue covers the orphan Actions registration on fleet-ops itself or the detector's self-repo blind spot.

impact: the minutes-quota flow: the free org's Actions minutes sit at 3000/3000 (ci-cost-cut backlog queued-2026-08-24-01) and #1161 documents that orphan registrations still bill for any trigger that fires — a latent burn vector on an exhausted quota, one dispatch away from blocking CI minutes for every product repo. Secondary: every audit/scout/inventory pass reads the active-registration list as ground truth; a phantom registration actively misleads (this scout's investigation cycle is the worked example).

product_surface: fleet/CI — Actions minutes quota + workflow registration inventory (control-plane)

termination:
```bash
cd /home/nish/workspaces/tooling/fleet-ops && bash tests/workflow-registration-inventory.test.sh && bin/fleet-workflow-registration-scan --report >/dev/null && grep -q "standing-rules-drift.yml" /home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/FLEET-ORPHAN-WORKFLOW-REGISTRATIONS.md
```
