title: Scout gate feedback loop: 0509 scout parked on runway while product issue creation fell to 5/day; failed scout runs counted as dry
body:
Measured 2026-09-05 08:40Z by the orchestrator: 0509 issues created in the last 24h = 5 (late Aug: 40-100/day), 0509 merged 23 in 24h, 12 scout-candidates unpromoted. `pi-scout@0509` has not run for real since 04:07Z (rc=1, upstream gateway HTML error). `fleet-work-supply-canary gate 0509` returned `rest` at every tick since: first parked on `scout-futility consecutive_dry=7 >= 3` while hours=6-7, then `hours=66 action=rest` after the orchestrator released 59 blocked issues to agent-ready. Feedback loop: blocked workers -> no drain -> "plenty of runway" -> scout skipped -> no new product work. `~/.local/state/scout-futility/0509.state`: consecutive_dry=7, last_exit=1 — a FAILED scout run was counted as dry.

- required: `bin/fleet-work-supply-canary gate <repo>` for product repos must use BOTH signals: rest only when hours_of_work >= buffer AND issues-created-last-24h >= 20; when created-24h < 20 or agent-ready < 40 the gate runs the scout regardless of runway. Ready-count inflated by re-released blocks must not read as supply.
- required: `bin/scout-futility-check end` never increments consecutive_dry when the scout exited non-zero (rc != 0 is an infra failure, not a dry run); it records last_exit and leaves the counter alone. consecutive_dry resets only after a scout run that actually filed >= 1 issue.
- required: replay drill in tests/ (fake gh, fake state file) that fails before and passes after for both rules.
- accept: with created-24h=5 and hours=66 the gate exits 0 (run); with created-24h=30 and hours=66 it exits 1 (rest); an rc=1 scout run leaves consecutive_dry unchanged; PR body carries Verification: with the command and observed output.
- moves: product_merges_per_day

Orchestrator forced one scout run manually at 08:46Z (`systemd-run ... pi-scout-run 0509 scout`) as a stopgap; that is not the fix.

title: Admission panel black hole: 85 EVIDENCE-REFUSED in 24h because auditors run with tools=0 and cannot cite paths; 12 0509 scout-candidates stuck since 08-26
body:
Measured 2026-09-05 08:45Z by the orchestrator: 12 open 0509 `scout-candidate` issues (oldest 2026-08-26) never reach agent-ready. Journal, last 24h: 85 `EVIDENCE-REFUSED` lines from `pi-audit-tally`, e.g. `0509/#1240 EVIDENCE-REFUSED (2-of-3 PASS but keyword-only reasons)` — the panel PASSES but the evidence gate refuses because every auditor reason "lacks repo-specific evidence (issue #, path, or URL)". The same lines show `PACKET-VERDICT tools=0 class=no-tools`: the auditors run with no tools, so they cannot cite a path or URL, so the gate refuses every PASS forever. 19 discards in the same window. Net: the admission queue is a black hole and product supply is the #1 limiter (0509 shipped 23/24h vs target 300).

- required: the admission auditor packet gives the auditor read tools (or the evidence gate accepts a PASS whose reason cites the candidate issue number + one concrete repo path from the issue body) so a 2-of-3 PASS can actually promote. Pick the smaller change; do not add a new organ.
- required: a candidate refused for evidence 3 times is escalated to the orchestrator queue (label escalate-senior), not re-queued forever.
- required: replay drill in tests/ with a fake verdict set (2-of-3 PASS, keyword-only reasons vs path-citing reasons) that fails before and passes after.
- accept: within one tick after deploy, the 12 open 0509 scout-candidates are each either agent-ready, discarded with a cited reason, or escalate-senior; the PR body carries Verification: with the command and observed output.
- moves: product_merges_per_day

Resolved — closed on merged-PR evidence + live state (triage 2026-09-12).

**Merged PRs that land each required:**
- Required 1 (evidence gate accepts a PASS citing candidate# + body path — the smaller change, no new organ): **#3583** merged 2026-09-05 (`admit tool-less senior PASSes that cite candidate# + a body path`, fleet-ops#3573) + **#3961** merged 2026-09-06 (`judge each PASS reason as one unit, not per line`, #3548 follow-up).
- Required 2 (3x-refused candidate escalates instead of re-queuing forever): **#3588** merged 2026-09-05 (`escalate evidence-refused candidates after 3 refusals`, fleet-ops#3574).
- Required 3 (replay drill in tests/): `tests/lifecycle-label-sweep-admission.test.sh` exists and runs in CI; admission machinery is live in `bin/lifecycle-label-sweep` (admit_scout_candidate, fleet-ops#4022 spec gate).

**Live state (2026-09-12):**
- `EVIDENCE-REFUSED` count in the last 24h journal: **0** (was 85/24h when filed).
- The 12 stuck 0509 scout-candidates from 2026-08-26/09-05 are drained — the current open scout-candidate set is today's fresh scout output, flowing through admission normally (multiple candidates created today, none stuck since 08-26).
- `PACKET-VERDICT tools=0 class=no-tools` black hole: auditors now promote via the #3583 path; the panel is no longer a dead end.

Accept criterion (candidates each agent-ready / discarded-with-reason / escalate-senior) is met by live behavior. The nish-reserved label was a mis-route: this was never a reserved-class item — it was fleet work, and it is done.

title: seat registry reaps LIVE Type=oneshot workers after 300s in SubState=start — cap accounting goes blind and over-admits (17 workers, 8 vCPUs, 5 registrations)
body:
source: live seat log 2026-09-10T21:05:05Z — `seat registry: unit pi-issue@0509-2373.service stuck activating 372s (SubState=start, threshold=300s) — wedged pi, reaping seat` (also 0509-2387/2388/2389, fleet-ops-5059/5069/5070 in the same tick; 9 such reaps so far today).

metric: a pi-issue worker that has been running for 6 minutes, 20 minutes or 40 minutes still holds its `active-seats` registration, so `count_active_on_seat`, `count_active_on_provider` and `count_active_total` never undercount a live worker.

observed: 2026-09-10T21:02:45Z and 2026-09-10T21:05:05Z — the registry reaper declared live workers "wedged pi" and deleted their seat registrations while their processes were still running.

evidence:
- Verbatim reap lines in `/home/nish/.local/state/pi-packet/watch.log`:
  `[2026-09-10T21:05:05Z] seat registry: unit pi-issue@0509-2373.service stuck activating 372s (SubState=start, threshold=300s) — wedged pi, reaping seat` (ages 372s, 360s, 348s, 335s, 340s, 327s, 316s across the batch).
- Those units were NOT wedged. At 21:12Z (7 minutes after the reap) `systemctl --user list-units 'pi-issue@0509*'` still shows 0509-2181/2373/2382/2388/2389 `activating`, and `systemctl --user show pi-issue@0509-2181 -p ActiveState -p SubState -p MainPID` → `activating start`, `MainPID=2535151`.
- Root cause: `lib/seat-lib.sh:3690-3703`. When `SubState == "start"` the wedged-age bound is `PI_SEAT_ACTIVATING_NO_PROCESS_MAX_S:-300` (5 min), on the assumption "a real worker transitions to active/running within seconds". That assumption is false for `Type=oneshot`: `systemd/pi-issue@.service:49` is `ExecStart=/home/nish/.local/bin/pi-issue-run %i`, and a running oneshot unit sits in `SubState=start` for its ENTIRE run (observed: `activating start` for both a 4-minute-old and a 25-minute-old worker). Every worker older than 300s is therefore reaped.
- The registry is the ONLY source of truth for those counts, so the reap is not masked. `count_active_on_seat` (`lib/seat-lib.sh:3877-3884`) also greps each unit's `ExecStart` for a hardcoded `--provider/--model`; live units have none (`argv[]=/home/nish/.local/bin/pi-issue-run fleet-ops-5072`), so the legacy fallback counts 0 for every worker.
- Live effect at 21:12Z: 17 active `pi-issue@*` worker units (`fleet_pi_workers_active{kind="sum"} 15`) vs **5** files in `/home/nish/.local/state/pi-packet/active-seats/` — and all 5 registrations are on `devin/swe-2-max`, whose seat cap is 4 (`config/seat-caps.json`), i.e. the survivors already show over-cap admission.
- The same blindness the code comment at `lib/seat-lib.sh:3673-3680` records for fleet-ops#993 ("every live seat got reaped, cap accounting went blind, and pick_seat piled unbounded workers onto the first free seat (the 8-vCPU box saturating at load 87, SustainedLoadHigh alert, zero-tools repair failure)"). Today's recurrence is the same mechanism via a different branch.
- Corroborating: `SustainedLoadHigh` tripped tonight and its repair worker measured "16 pi-issue@ workers on 8 vCPUs ... ~2x oversubscription ... admission is RAM-only" and bound each worker with `CPUQuota=25%` (PR #5112). `CPUQuota` bounds the damage per worker; nothing bounds the COUNT, because the count reads the emptied registry.

accept:
1. `_seat_registry_unit_live` treats a `Type=oneshot` unit in `activating/start` as LIVE for as long as the unit can legitimately run: bound the age by the unit's own `TimeoutStartSec` (read it via `systemctl --user show <unit> --property=TimeoutStartUSec`) rather than a 300s constant. Keep the genuinely-broken paths: `ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic=0` (process never started) and `SubState=auto-restart` stay fail-closed at the short bound.
2. Remove the hardcoded `SubState == "start"` → 300s branch, or keep it only for the `ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic=0` case, with a comment stating why `start` is the normal state for a running `Type=oneshot` worker (cite this issue and fleet-ops#993 / #1361).
3. Fail loud on drift: a test asserts the liveness bound is not below `TimeoutStartSec` in `systemd/pi-issue@.service`, so a future change to either file cannot silently re-open the hole.
4. Regression test `tests/seat-registry-liveness.test.sh` with stubbed `systemctl` output: (a) `activating/start` at 400s and at 40min → LIVE, registration kept; (b) `activating/start` at 50min (past `TimeoutStartSec`) → wedged, reaped; (c) `ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic=0` for 6min → wedged, reaped; (d) `activating/auto-restart` → not live. Prove (a) fails on current `main` and passes after the fix.
5. Do NOT raise `seat_max_concurrent`/`target_concurrent` in this PR. This fix restores the accounting; the correct concurrency after it is a separate measurement.
6. No new timer, no new unit, no new file in `~/.config/systemd/user`.

Prevention (fleet-ops#366 mechanical-fix rule): the guard is the drift test in accept 3 — it fails the PR if the liveness bound drifts below the worker's own timeout, which is exactly how this bug was introduced (a constant chosen against a wrong assumption about oneshot state).

verify:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/tooling/fleet-ops
bash tests/seat-registry-liveness.test.sh
bash tests/fleet-seat-recovery-units.test.sh
bash tests/pi-issue-run-per-seat-timeout.test.sh
# live: a live worker keeps its registration past 6 minutes
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u) systemctl --user show pi-issue@0509-2373.service -p ActiveState -p SubState --value
grep -c 'wedged pi, reaping seat' /home/nish/.local/state/pi-packet/watch.log
```

rollback: revert the PR — the liveness predicate returns to the 300s constant on the next deploy and the next `pick_seat` pass. No data, no migration: the worst case is the current behaviour (registrations reaped). If the fix over-holds wedged units, re-tighten the bound toward `TimeoutStartSec` in a follow-up.

dedupe: no open issue or PR mentions the registry reaper, `SubState`, "wedged pi", or cap accounting (checked all 181 open issues + 6 open PRs). Adjacent but different: #5112 (CPUQuota per worker — bounds the damage, not the count), #5106 / #5093 / #5096 (seat-recovery unit churn), #4723 (per-tick spawn cap).

impact: the concurrent-seat cap — the only thing standing between the fleet and 8-vCPU saturation — reads near-zero for every worker that has run more than 5 minutes, which is nearly all of them. pick_seat then piles workers onto the same seat from a pool the box cannot carry: that is the RAM/CPU oversubscription that slows or kills product workers, that keeps `SustainedLoadHigh` recurring (it is patched tonight with a per-worker `CPUQuota`, one layer below the actual bug), and that makes the `seat_availability` SLO (compliance 0.31 at 21:10Z) a reading of a registry nobody is writing to.

product_surface: fleet worker admission caps (the seat pool the 0509 product lanes draw from) — over-admission starves and slows the product workers.

termination: `cd /home/nish/workspaces/tooling/fleet-ops && bash tests/seat-registry-liveness.test.sh`

That is the fleet-ops#1453 fault shape — the repair queue not consuming repairs — and it is self-reinforcing here, because this issue's own fault (the registry reaping LIVE workers after 300s in SubState=start, so `count_active_*` undercounts) corrupts the very cap accounting that decides how many workers get admitted.

title: fix(worker-prompt): worker.md packet is 32964B, exceeds the 32768B size ceiling (fleet-ops#1902 re-bloat)
body:
The P14 test worker-prompt-size-ceiling.test.sh fails on main: the assembled worker packet (prompts/worker.md + TARGET line) is 32964B, exceeding the 32768B ceiling. This is a pre-existing fault (worker.md last touched by 2a4091e7, fleet-ops#3312) — it does not block merges (P14 is not a required check) but it re-introduces the fleet-ops#1902 empty-run class risk on free-tier seats with limited context windows.

observed: 2026-09-05. `{ cat prompts/worker.md; echo; echo 'TARGET: repo Nishfleet/fleet-ops issue 1902 unit pi-issue-fleet-ops-1902'; } | wc -c` -> 32964 on both origin/main and the worker branch.

fix: trim ~200B from prompts/worker.md (the failed-command shape enumeration is redundant with tests/fleet-failed-command-*.test.sh + bin/fleet-failed-command-flagged lint, per fleet-ops#1902). The ceiling test then goes green.

title: reccos: Fix the one test-isolation bug behind preview-assert, then strip preview-assert back to typecheck+buil
body:
Filed automatically from the Kimi K3 Max 11-lens recommendations pass on 0509 (lens: Tests and CI quality, ref R1, impact/size H/M). Scope is exactly the `do:` line below — no judgment calls, no extra files. If it cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

why: `preview-assert.yml:3-16` says 9 of the last 120 merges were auto-reverted because one test (`tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts:222`) "passes sharded and fails when the whole suite runs together" — a cross-file state-pollution bug. The chosen fix was to run the FULL unsharded suite a second time on every PR (`preview-assert.yml:146` `npm run test`), on top of ci.yml's 4 shards, and deploy-production.yml runs it a third time post-merge (`deploy-production.yml:514`). 6,941 `it(` blocks ×3 per merge to catch one polluted test.

files: tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts
do: bisect the pollution (run `d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` after each sibling file until it fails), fix the shared state, then delete the `npm run test` step from `preview-assert.yml` keeping lines 139/158/183 (typecheck, build, versions upload). Files: the polluting test, `.github/workflows/preview-assert.yml`.
must-not: touch files outside `files:` and the files named in the `do:` step; add a new mechanism, script, or organ; invent product copy, pricing, or unsourced claims; weaken or skip a test.
termination: npm test
accept: preview-assert job drops to build+upload minutes; zero shard-divergence auto-reverts in the next 60 days.
metric: H-impact / M-size per the lens ranking.
depends-on: none

## Judge edits (binding)
- `files:` names the victim, not the polluter — replace with "files: tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts, the polluting test file found by the bisection, .github/workflows/preview-assert.yml." Otherwise the worker must stop the moment bisection names another file.
- Accept "zero shard-divergence auto-reverts in the next 60 days" is not closable at merge — replace with "full unsharded suite passes 3 consecutive CI runs on the PR, including the pairwise order polluter→victim in one invocation."
- Add: "deploy-production.yml:514's post-merge full-suite run is out of scope — do not edit it" (the why: names it; a literal worker may delete it too).

## 1. The bisection finds nothing

The binding `do:` step is "bisect the pollution (run `d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` after each sibling file until it fails)". Run on current `main` (`63e4b9d1`) with vitest 4.1.11 / node 22:

| run | files | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| victim alone | 1 | pass, 36 tests, 1.29s |
| victim + sibling half A | 323 | pass, 4141 tests, 87.8s |
| victim + sibling half B | 327 | pass, 3814 tests, 93.9s |
| **victim + all 648 siblings (full suite)** | **689** | **pass, 8288 tests, 171s** |
| full suite, second run, under concurrent load | 689 | pass, 8288 tests, 194.6s |

No file names itself. There is no shared state to fix, so "then delete the `npm run test` step" has no precondition to satisfy.

I also ran a purpose-built harness that replays the victim test's exact sequence 60 times (`runCaptured` spawn -> poll PID file -> `pidAlive`) both at idle and while the full 689-file suite was running: **0 misses out of 60 in each mode**. `expect(pidAlive(childPid)).toBe(true)` at `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts:222` did not reproduce.

## 2. The justifying failure is gone, and was never shard-divergence

The `why:` rests on "9 of the last 120 merges were auto-reverted" from run `33561746667` (2026-09-01). Verified against live runs:

- **Last occurrence of the d1 failure: 2026-09-01** (run `33561746667`). The flake is 10 days cold.
- **19 deploy runs failed since 2026-09-02.** I read all of them. **Zero** are the d1 test. Causes are other, real bugs:
  - `e2e/journey-3-release.spec.ts:537` — `expect(page).toHaveURL("/app/digests?firstrun=1")` gets `/app/briefs?firstrun=1` (runs `34529182476`, `34528071529`, `34525186232`, `34523274848`, `34520673955`, `34501710905`, `34499830797`, `34512030903`, `34508996720`).
  - `scripts/check-public-home-current.mjs --source-only` (runs `34491624466`, `34489010125`).
- **Both recent auto-reverts** (#2650, #2618) cite a red *Deploy Worker* job. In run `34505121417` (the revert trigger for #2650) the d1 test **passed** (`36 tests, 483ms`), the full vitest suite **passed** (`682 files`), and the job failed on **16 Playwright failures**. In run `34529182476` the full suite passed (`689 passed`) and the job still failed — on e2e.

So `preview-assert.yml`'s full-suite step is not buying what its comment claims. That is a real finding, and it is a **different issue** from the one written here.

## 3. The `do:` step is also gate-path blocked for a worker

`files:` names `.github/workflows/preview-assert.yml`, and `.github/workflows/**` is gate-owned (`.github/scripts/gate-integrity.sh:30,530`). Removing the `Test` step is a gate-path change. Per the gate-integrity rule I must **never** post the attestation myself; a repository admin on a different identity must post `gate-integrity-attest: <40-hex head sha>`. The deletion therefore cannot land from this unit even if the bisection had found something.

## What I did not do, and why

- Did **not** delete the `Test` step. No polluter was named, and the deletion is a self-attestable gate-path change.
- Did **not** touch `deploy-production.yml:514` (out of scope per the binding judge edit).
- Did **not** weaken or skip any test.
- Did **not** edit `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts`. Nothing reproducible to fix; a speculative edit would be a false claim.

## Recommended replacement work (needs a decision, not more bisection)

1. **Close #2373 as superseded.** Its premise is stale; #2382 already reworked this same test file and merged (#2690).
2. **File the real bug:** `journey-3-release.spec.ts:537` asserts `/app/digests?firstrun=1` but the app navigates to `/app/briefs?firstrun=1`. It has failed 9+ deploy runs and caused both recent auto-reverts. This is a product-code bug, not a test bug.
3. **Then, separately, on the CI-cost question:** only after (2) is fixed and the deploy job is green, evaluate dropping the `npm run test` step from `preview-assert.yml`. That is a gate-path change needing an admin attestation, and it should be filed with the measured cost (Test step = **2m58s** of the ~5 min job on run `34532969827`; typecheck 57s, build 14s).

## Evidence

All commands run in worktree `/home/nish/workspaces/agent-worktrees/0509-2373` at `origin/main` = `63e4b9d1`, node `v22.23.1`, vitest `4.1.11` (`.node-version` pins 22.22.0; CI uses the same).

Claim branch `claim/issue-2373` carries **no commits** — nothing to preserve.

`loose-ends: the d1 flake is stale, not fixed — I did not prove it can never recur, only that it did not recur on current main across two full-suite runs, 60 race-probe iterations at idle, 60 under load, and 10 days of deploy history. If it recurs, that is a live repro and a new issue.`

title: reccos: Pre-warm the domains people actually search so the no-account preview never hits the 60s wall
body:
Filed automatically from the Kimi K3 Max 11-lens recommendations pass on 0509 (lens: Onboarding and activation, ref R1, impact/size H/M). Scope is exactly the `do:` line below — no judgment calls, no extra files. If it cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

why: `app/routes/search.tsx:1443-1451` — the live preview polls 5s×12=60s, then "the promised auto-refresh stops silently" and the exhausted state becomes a signup capture (`source=search_warming_exhausted`, `app/lib/signup-source.ts:30`). The live landing page's first promise is "Paste a competitor site — no account needed." A first-time visitor typing an uncached domain gets up to a minute of waiting that can end in a signup wall instead of ads.

files: app/lib/signup-source.ts, app/routes/search.tsx, workers/app.ts
do: use the existing `discovery_warmup` cron (`workers/app.ts:338`, `17 */6 * * *`) to pre-warm the top ~200 domains from `funnel_search_preview_submit` events so previews serve from cache; when warming does exhaust, keep partial rows visible with the signup CTA inline rather than replacing the result area.

proposal: the `do:` line names a data source that cannot produce domains, and its second clause describes a render state that does not exist. Need a re-scope ruling before a worker can build this.

No code was written. Claim branch released. `agent-blocked` + `needs-orchestrator` applied.

## 1. `funnel_search_preview_submit` cannot yield "domains people actually search"

Three independent blockers, each verified in this worktree at `origin/main` (`b96f329d`):

**(a) The event carries no domain, by construction.** `app/lib/funnel-measurement.server.ts:295` is `emitFunnelSearchSubmit(env, request)` — it takes no query. The record is assembled from `FUNNEL_DETAIL_ALLOWLIST` (`:223`), which is exactly `event_id, workspace_id, timestamp, route, result_count_bucket, error_kind, referrer_domain, account_scope`. There is no domain field to read, and `docs/funnel-measurement-spec.md` §3.1 lists *"Query text, typed terms"* as a **forbidden field** on this exact event, with §4 stating "There is no path from a caller-controlled string to a record field."

**(b) The events are console lines, not storage.** `writeAppLog` (`app/lib/log.server.ts:45`) ends at `console.log(line)` (`:59`). No D1 write, no Analytics Engine binding, no log drain: `wrangler.jsonc:8` has only `observability: { enabled: true }`, and a repo-wide `grep` for `analytics_engine` / `log_drain` / `logpush` matches only the generated `worker-configuration.d.ts` type and the built artifact `build/server/wrangler.json`. Even if the field existed, a Worker cannot query its own `console.log` output. Spec §7 confirms the design: "No new storage exists and none is authorized by this document."

**(c) Nothing else records the domains either.** The whole migration set has four tables with a plain-text domain column — `web_mention_target`, `search_domain_identity_cache`, `presence_domain_verification`, `demo_brand_proof_hole_state` — none of them written by an anonymous preview. The search telemetry deliberately stores a one-way hash: `discovery_fetch_log.query_fingerprint` is `fingerprintSavedQuery()` = `hashString(stableStringify(query))` (`app/lib/normalize.ts:118`), and `app/lib/ad-source.server.ts:1369` states "the raw cursor and query text never reach the telemetry table." `search_domain_identity_cache` is dead code — no `.ts` file outside its migration references it.

So the instruction "pre-warm the top ~200 domains from `funnel_search_preview_submit` events" has no input. Producing one means a new table + migration, a per-submit write of the searched term, and a change to the §4 allowlist — i.e. a new mechanism, a file list far wider than `files:`, and a privacy decision the spec says needs owner approval.

## 2. The warm *mechanism* already exists — only the domain list is missing

This part is good news, and it is the cheapest re-scope:

- `app/lib/discovery-panel.server.ts:155` `warmDiscoveryEvalPanel` already warms domains through `purpose: "public_search_warmup"`, and `app/lib/discovery-cache.server.ts:106` `isPublicSearchFamily` documents that interactive preview and the 6-hourly warmup **share a cache family** — so a warm pass is exactly what makes a preview "serve from cache".
- It warms `DISCOVERY_EVAL_PANEL` (`:21`), a fixed 12-brand list. That is the gap versus "the domains people actually search".
- Production is `SEARCH_ROLLOUT_MODE: "v2"` (`wrangler.jsonc:90`), and the v2 cache key for a domain search puts the **plain registrable domain** in `discovery_cache_entry.cache_key`: `search-v2:domain:<registrableDomain>:exact:<provider>:<country>:<cursor>` (`app/lib/search-v2.server.ts:253-273`). Rows are written with `route_context='public_search'` and carry `updated_at`. A "top ~200 domains searched" query is a `SELECT` over an existing table — no new storage, no new mechanism.

## 3. The second clause ("keep partial rows visible … rather than replacing the result area") does not match the code

`warmingPollExhausted` is used in five places: `app/routes/search.tsx:2461`, `:2465`, `:2503`, `:2558`, `:2569`. The results list at `:2473` renders whenever `visibleAds.length > 0`, and the signup capture at `:2569` sits inside the `visibleAds.length === 0` branch (`:2493`). With partial rows on screen at exhaustion the visitor keeps every row and sees the honest "We stopped auto-refreshing. Retry this search to load the rest." line — nothing is replaced. With zero rows there is no result area to replace.

The buildable residue of that clause is only "add the signup CTA inline when partial rows exist at exhaustion" — and it moves none of the `accept:` metrics (it would raise, not lower, the `search_warming_exhausted` share).

## 4. Proposed resolutions (orchestrator picks)

- **(a) Re-scope the source and widen `files:`:** warm the top ~200 registrable domains from recent `discovery_cache_entry` rows with `route_context='public_search'` and a `search-v2:domain:` key, dropping the "from funnel events" wording. Needs `app/lib/discovery-panel.server.ts` (+ `app/lib/monitoring.server.ts` if the loop lives there) added to `files:` — no new mechanism, reuses the existing `public_search_warmup` family and the existing cron. **Smallest change that ships.**
- **(b) Keep the literal source:** then this is not a worker ticket. Storing search terms is a §4 allowlist change + a spec change + a new table + a migration, and the spec routes that through owner approval.
- **(c) Split clause (b) out and drop it** (see §3), leaving the warming work as the whole ticket.

## 5. Gate note

The body's `collision-gate` line lists 13 dependencies; `#2146` and `#2402` are still OPEN, so this ticket was claimed ahead of its own gate. Whatever the re-scope ruling, re-check that gate before re-queueing.

title: harden: ancestor-check the TOLERATE_MAIN_DRIFT branch in ci-verify-provider-main-cas.sh (follow-up to #2701 / PR #2822)
body:
PR #2822 (attested and merging) sets `TOLERATE_MAIN_DRIFT: "1"` on the Deploy production pin step to stop queued runs failing `provider_main_cas_invalid: remote_main_drift` when main advances mid-run. Correct fix for the outage; it leaves one implicit invariant.

In `scripts/ci-verify-provider-main-cas.sh` the ancestorship branch is guarded by the event name:

    elif [[ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME:-}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]] &&
         git merge-base --is-ancestor "$PINNED_SHA" "$remote_sha" 2>/dev/null; then

so on a **push** event the `TOLERATE_MAIN_DRIFT` branch below it accepts any `remote_sha != PINNED_SHA` with no ancestorship check at all. That is safe today only because 0509 `main` disables force-pushes and deletions (`allow_force_pushes=false`, `allow_deletions=false`, verified 2026-09-11T06:53Z), so main can only move forward. If that branch setting ever changes, a rewound main would deploy an orphaned commit silently, and nothing in CI would say so.

required: add `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$PINNED_SHA" "$remote_sha"` as a condition of the `TOLERATE_MAIN_DRIFT` branch itself, so forward drift is tolerated and a rewind/rewrite stays fail-closed by construction on **every** event, not by repo settings.

must-not: do not revert #2822, do not re-fail the pin on forward drift (that is the outage), and do not move the ancestor check behind a new flag.

accept: a test in `tests/production-candidate-workflow.test.ts` (or a unit test of the CAS script) that a non-ancestor `remote_sha` fails `remote_main_drift` even with `TOLERATE_MAIN_DRIFT=1`, and a forward-drift case still passes. Both green in CI.

title: fix: Reactivation order ties on the mass-pause timestamp, resuming an arbitrary (oldest-first) subset (watchlist-plan-reconcile.server.ts)
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-10 10:10 IST) from the Kimi K3 Max whole-codebase review of 0509 @ cdf7d95e (MEDIUM tier), each finding verified by Fable. Scope is exactly the numbered steps below - no judgment calls; if a step cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Finding M13 (Kimi K3 Max), verbatim:**
## F2 [MEDIUM] app/lib/data/watchlist-plan-reconcile.server.ts:224 - Reactivation order ties on the mass-pause timestamp, resuming an arbitrary (oldest-first) subset

- scenario: A user with 10 active watchlists downgrades to a 3-watchlist plan: `deactivateWatchlistsBeyondPlanLimit` pauses 7 rows in one UPDATE, stamping all 7 with the same `updated_at` (single `nowIso()` per call). The user resubscribes to a 5-watchlist plan: `reactivateWatchlistsUpToPlanLimit` computes 2 free slots and selects paused rows `ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT ?` with no tiebreaker. SQLite resolves the 7-way tie arbitrarily (in practice rowid order = oldest created first), so the two *oldest* paused watchlists resume while newer, more recently edited competitors stay paused — the inverse of the newest-kept pause policy and of the function's own "most recently active paused watchlists" comment. Same flaw in the grant path (`buildWatchlistGrantReconcileStatements`, second statement, line ~78).
- evidence:
```
          AND id IN (
            SELECT id
            FROM watchlist
            WHERE user_id = ?
              AND is_active = 0
              AND (paused_reason = 'plan_limit' OR paused_reason IS NULL)
            ORDER BY updated_at DESC
            LIMIT ?
```
- repro: add `tests/integration/watchlist-plan-reconcile.integration.test.ts`: create 4 watchlists (distinct `created_at`), `deactivateWatchlistsBeyondPlanLimit(env, u, 1)`, then `reactivateWatchlistsUpToPlanLimit(env, u, 2)` and assert the resumed row is the newest-created paused watchlist — currently the tie on the identical `updated_at` makes the choice plan-dependent.
- fix: Append deterministic tiebreakers that match the pause policy in both reactivate statements: `ORDER BY updated_at DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC`. One-line SQL change in each of the two statements; no schema or caller changes.
- confidence: 0.7

**Fable verification:** CONFIRMED by reading. reactivation ORDER BY updated_at DESC; a mass pause stamps one timestamp, so the subset is arbitrary.

title: fix: `upsertDeliveryTarget` read-back omits the `targetValue` predicate, so it returns whichever same-cha (+1 more in delivery-records-targets.server.ts)
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-10 10:10 IST) from the Kimi K3 Max whole-codebase review of 0509 @ cdf7d95e (MEDIUM tier), each finding verified by Fable. Scope is exactly the numbered steps below - no judgment calls; if a step cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Finding M10 (Kimi K3 Max), verbatim:**
## F2 [MEDIUM] app/lib/data/delivery-records-targets.server.ts:417 - `upsertDeliveryTarget` read-back omits the `targetValue` predicate, so it returns whichever same-channel target was written last, not the one just upserted

- scenario: Two concurrent writes to the same (user, watchlist, channel) scope — e.g. two Slack webhooks connected in parallel, or a WhatsApp connect racing a pause of another target. The function writes row A with `updated_at = now`, then re-reads `ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1` with only `watchlistId`/`channel` filters; a concurrent write to row B wins the ordering and the caller gets B's record. `connectWhatsAppTarget` then persists the validation attempt with `deliveryTargetId: target.id` (whatsapp.server.ts:181) pointing at the wrong target, so `reconcileWhatsAppSetupTargetFromAttempt` (which keys on `targetId` + `providerMessageId`) applies the delivered/failed webhook to the wrong target's validation state. Same-millisecond sequential upserts can also tie on `updated_at` with an arbitrary winner.
- evidence:
```
  416|  const [target] = await listDeliveryTargets(env, input.userId, {
  417|    watchlistId: input.watchlistId ?? null,
  418|    channel: input.channel,
  419|    limit: 1,
  420|  });
  421|  return target ?? null;
```
(`listDeliveryTargets` already supports a `targetValue` filter — it just isn't passed.)
- repro: add `tests/integration/delivery-target-upsert.integration.test.ts`: seed two slack targets A and B for one user, `Promise.all([upsertDeliveryTarget(A…), upsertDeliveryTarget(B…)])`, assert each returned record's `targetValue` equals its own input (intermittently fails today); deterministic variant: stub two staggered writes and assert the read-back SQL binds `targetValue`.
- fix: Pass `targetValue` (the already-normalized value) into the read-back — `listDeliveryTargets(env, input.userId, { watchlistId, channel, targetValue, limit: 1 })` — so the returned row is the exact row written, independent of concurrent siblings.
- confidence: 0.65

**Fable verification:** CONFIRMED by reading. read-back uses listDeliveryTargets({watchlistId, channel, limit:1}) with no target_value predicate.

**Finding M11 (Kimi K3 Max), verbatim:**
## F3 [MEDIUM] app/lib/data/delivery-records-targets.server.ts:367 - `upsertDeliveryTarget` insert path is read-then-plain-`INSERT`; a concurrent first-time upsert of the same target throws an unhandled UNIQUE constraint and 500s the connect flow

- scenario: User double-submits "Connect Slack/Teams/WhatsApp" (or a connect races an auto-provision of the same address). Both requests run `getDeliveryTargetByUniqueFields` → absent → both issue the plain `INSERT INTO delivery_target … VALUES`. The loser's insert hits `idx_delivery_target_unique_workspace` / `idx_delivery_target_unique_watchlist` and the route returns a 500 even though the target now exists and the connect actually succeeded. The sibling writer in this same file (`provisionVerifiedAccountEmailTargetIfUnsuppressed`) already does the race-safe thing (`INSERT OR IGNORE … SELECT … WHERE NOT EXISTS`), so the pattern is established.
- evidence:
```
  286|  const existingTarget = await getDeliveryTargetByUniqueFields(env, { … });
  …
  367|        INSERT INTO delivery_target (
  …
  391|        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
```
- repro: add `tests/integration/delivery-target-upsert.integration.test.ts`: with no existing target, `Promise.all([upsertDeliveryTarget(X…), upsertDeliveryTarget(X…)])` and assert both resolve to a target with value X (today one rejects with `UNIQUE constraint failed`).
- fix: Make the insert `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (or `OR IGNORE`) against both partial unique indexes, then fall through to the existing update path when the row already exists — or catch `isUniqueConstraintError` from `helpers.server` and re-read + update. Either way the loser converges instead of 500ing.
- confidence: 0.8

**Fable verification:** CONFIRMED by reading. plain INSERT after a read; UNIQUE indexes idx_delivery_target_unique_workspace/_watchlist exist (migrations 0007/0019), so the loser throws.

title: intake park gap: protected issue delivered by non-claim branches re-claims forever (live: #4891)
body:
observed 2026-09-10: fleet-ops#4891 was delivered by merged PRs #4893 + #4897 on `fable/*` branches (not `claim/issue-4891`), its remaining work is delegated to a named runtime event (`remeasure-4891-timer`, fires 2026-09-11 14:05Z), and its body carries no `termination:` clause. It stayed open and re-entered the claimable pool on every claim release — 12 claims in one day, each burning a seat pick plus a worker run re-verifying a date-gate that cannot be met yet.

All three park detectors miss this cell (lib/pi-intake-tick.sh ~2156-2205):
- fleet-ops#4540 park requires protected + `termination:` in body + a merged claim/issue-<N> PR — #4891 fails the last two;
- fleet-ops#4553 land-or-close park requires NON-protected — #4891 is owner-authored;
- the #5045 middle-shape issue covers non-protected + merged claim-branch `Relates to` PR — also not this cell.

Uncovered cell: protected issue, no merged claim-branch PR, no `termination:` clause, work delivered by other branches and/or delegated to a runtime event. #4891 was parked by hand with `awaiting-runtime-gate` (the label works — intake skips it at zero cost) but nothing automatic ever applies it to this shape.

accept:
- A park path for this cell: protected open issue, cumulative claims past PARK_MAX_CLAIMS, no merged claim-branch PR, remaining work either delivered on other branches (detect via a comment or body reference to merged PRs) or delegated to a named runtime event (e.g. a `blocked-on: timer <name>` / `awaiting: <unit>` marker convention). Implementer's call — smallest durable fix; do not widen so far that genuinely unfinished protected issues get parked.
- Regression test covering the shape (protected + no claim-branch PR + runtime-event marker -> parked, not re-claimed).
- Consider merging with the #5045 fix: both are 'the park detector matrix has a hole' — one generalized claim-volume + delivered-signal detector may cover both cells.

title: fix: runBrowserbaseProbe's session-create fetch is the only unguarded probe call; a transient network err (provider-bakeoff.lib.mjs)
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-10 10:10 IST) from the Kimi K3 Max whole-codebase review of 0509 @ cdf7d95e (MEDIUM tier), each finding verified by Fable. Scope is exactly the numbered steps below - no judgment calls; if a step cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Finding M63 (Kimi K3 Max), verbatim:**
## F2 [MEDIUM] scripts/provider-bakeoff.lib.mjs:981 - runBrowserbaseProbe's session-create fetch is the only unguarded probe call; a transient network error aborts the whole bakeoff
- scenario: with `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY`/`BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID` set, any transport failure on the session-create POST (DNS, TCP reset, fetch throw) propagates out of `runBrowserbaseProbe` → `runProviderProbe` → `benchmarkProviders`, crashing the entire bakeoff run (all providers, all queries, plus the prod-canary path if browserbase is ever included) instead of recording one `browserbase` error row. Every sibling probe (`runBrowserlessBqlProbe`, `runZyteProbe`, `runCurrent0509Probe`, `runCdpBackedProbe`) wraps its fetch in try/catch and returns a `ProbeResult` with `status: "error"`.
- evidence:
```
  981|  const sessionResponse = await fetchImpl(request.endpoint, {
  982|    method: "POST",
  983|    headers: request.headers,
  984|    body: JSON.stringify(request.body),
  985|  });
  986|  const payload = await sessionResponse.json().catch(() => ({}));
```
- repro: `node --input-type=module -e "import { runBrowserbaseProbe } from './scripts/provider-bakeoff.lib.mjs'; const r = await runBrowserbaseProbe({ provider: 'browserbase', query: 'nykaa', country: 'India', mode: 'advertiser' }, { env: { BROWSERBASE_API_KEY: 'k', BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID: 'p' }, fetchImpl: async () => { throw new Error('getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.browserbase.com'); } }); console.log(r.status)"` — today it throws `ENOTFOUND` instead of printing `error`.
- fix: wrap the session-create call in the same try/catch shape as `runZyteProbe`: on throw, return a `ProbeResult` with `status: classifyErrorStatus(message)`, `latencyMs` from `performance.now() - startedAt` (start the clock before the fetch), `httpStatus: null`, and the error message as `note`. One provider's network blip then degrades to a row, not a run abort.
- confidence: 0.9

**Fable verification:** CONFIRMED by reading. fetchImpl(request.endpoint, ...) for session-create has no try/catch unlike the sibling probes.

files: scripts/provider-bakeoff.lib.mjs, tests/provider-bakeoff*.test.ts (create if missing)

1. For each finding above: write the failing test first, exactly as its `repro:` line describes (or the closest vitest/node equivalent), and show it RED in the PR body.
2. Apply each finding's `fix:` paragraph as the smallest durable change; no refactor beyond it.
3. Search this file (and its siblings) for the same pattern and fix every instance in the same PR; list them in the PR body.
4. Show the tests GREEN; typecheck.

termination: npx vitest run tests/provider-bakeoff*.test.ts && npm run typecheck

accept: every RED->GREEN test is in the PR and none of the scenarios above reproduce.

title: intake: honour 'collision-gate:' in ticket bodies - a gated ticket is claimed anyway
body:
Filed by a pi-issue worker (2026-09-11). Scope is exactly the step below - no judgment calls; if it cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Why:** the house ticket format carries a line of the form

    collision-gate (Fable <date>): shares <path> with #<n>. agent-ready returns
    automatically when those are merged/closed (gate file: agent-state/fleet-landing-watch/ticket-gates.json)

fleet-ops#4808 added a `depends-on:` gate to `lib/pi-intake-tick.sh`, so that line is honoured. The `collision-gate:` line is not: `rg -n 'collision-gate' bin/ lib/ config/` over the deploy clone returns NOTHING. So the gate is issue-body prose with no machinery behind it.

Live case: 0509#2411 carries `collision-gate: shares app/components/signup-first-brief-view.tsx with #2407`, and `agent-state/fleet-landing-watch/ticket-gates.json` holds `"2411": [2407]` with #2407 still OPEN and an active worktree. Intake claimed #2411 anyway. The worker had to hand-verify the overlap was disjoint before it could proceed - a human doing a machine's job, exactly the failure #4808 fixed for `depends-on:`.

files: lib/pi-intake-tick.sh (the claim path beside the #4808 depends-on gate), its tests, the README section on the ticket format

do: treat a `collision-gate:` line naming not-yet-merged/closed tickets the same way `depends-on:` is treated - skip the claim with a `skipped-collision-gate:#n` reason, resolved by the same DONE rule (issue closed as completed, or a PR linked via "closes #n" merged). Reuse the #4808 resolution helper and its per-tick memo cache; do not add a second resolver.

must-not: add a new organ or a separate gate service; re-implement the DONE resolution #4808 already added; weaken or skip a test.

termination: the pi-intake-tick tests

accept: an issue whose `collision-gate:` names an open ticket is skipped with `skipped-collision-gate:#n` instead of claimed; it is claimed on the tick after that ticket closes.

depends-on: none
owner-decision: no

title: fix: Turnstile widget script-src fingerprint condemns any real page that embeds a Turnstile form widget as `landing_challenge (capture-validity.server.ts)
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-10 09:10 IST) from the Kimi K3 Max whole-codebase review of 0509 @ cdf7d95e, verified by Fable (CONFIRMED by reading). Scope is exactly the numbered steps below - no judgment calls; if a step cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Finding (Kimi K3 Max), verbatim:**
## F1 [HIGH] app/lib/capture-validity.server.ts:88 - Turnstile widget script-src fingerprint condemns any real page that embeds a Turnstile form widget as `landing_challenge_page`

- scenario: A competitor's real, fully-rendered landing page (hundreds of chars of copy) embeds a Turnstile widget on its signup/lead form via the standard `<script src="https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js">`. The challenge branch has no thin-body qualifier (unlike the cookie-wall branch), so every capture of that page — plain-http and rendered — is rejected `landing_challenge_page` → recorded `capture_failed` → no baseline, no diff, no watch event, ever. Run history then publicly labels the page "Anti-bot challenge wall" (`capture-attempt-reason-code.ts`) although the page rendered fine — a false public claim plus a silently dead watchlist. The existing test (`tests/capture-validity.test.ts:82`) only pins a thin shell containing *only* a turnstile container; no test pins a full page with an embedded widget.
- evidence:
```
  /cdn-cgi\/challenge-platform\//i,
  /challenges\.cloudflare\.com\/turnstile/i,
  /window\._cf_chl_opt\b/i,
...
  const hit = matchesAny(html, CHALLENGE_FINGERPRINTS);
  if (hit) {
    return { valid: false, reasonCode: "landing_challenge_page", ...
```
- repro: add to `tests/capture-validity.test.ts`: `assessCaptureValidity({ html: REAL_LANDING_PAGE + '<script src="https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js"></script>', fetchStatus: 200 })` and assert `valid === true` — today it returns `reasonCode: "landing_challenge_page"`.
- fix: Remove the bare `challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile` script-src pattern from `CHALLENGE_FINGERPRINTS` (the interstitial-specific markers — `window._cf_chl_opt`, `cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/`, `cf-challenge-*` ids — already catch real challenge walls), or gate that one pattern behind the same thin-body qualifier the cookie-wall branch uses, so a full page with an embedded widget passes.
- confidence: 0.7

**Fable verification:** CONFIRMED by reading. the challenge branch (line ~210) returns landing_challenge_page on ANY CHALLENGE_FINGERPRINTS hit with no thin-body qualifier; the cookie-wall branch right below it does check visibleBodyText length. The Turnstile widget script src is in the challenge list.

files: app/lib/capture-validity.server.ts, tests/capture-validity*.test.ts (create if missing)

do:
1. Write the failing test first, exactly as the finding's `repro:` line describes (or the closest vitest equivalent), and show it RED in the PR body.
2. Apply the finding's `fix:` paragraph as the smallest durable change; no refactor beyond it.
3. Search the file (and its siblings) for the same pattern and fix every instance in the same PR; list them in the PR body.
4. Show the test GREEN; typecheck.

must-not: widen scope beyond this finding and its exact pattern; change public behaviour not named in the finding; touch files other than the ones on the files: line except to add a test helper.

termination: npx vitest run tests/capture-validity*.test.ts && npm run typecheck

accept: the RED->GREEN test is in the PR, the scenario in the finding no longer reproduces.

metric: none (defect fix)

depends-on: none

owner-decision: no

## Judge edits (binding)
- The finding offers two different fixes ("Remove the bare pattern… **or** gate that one pattern behind the thin-body qualifier") — a literal worker must not choose. Replace do-step 2 "Apply the finding's `fix:` paragraph as the smallest durable change; no refactor beyond it." with: "Gate ONLY the `challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile` pattern behind the same thin-body qualifier the cookie-wall branch uses. Do not remove the pattern — the existing thin-shell pin at tests/capture-validity.test.ts:82 must stay green. Do not touch any other CHALLENGE_FINGERPRINTS entry."
- Add to do-step 1: "The REAL_LANDING_PAGE stand-in must contain more visible body text than the cookie-wall branch's thin-body threshold, or the new test stays red after the correct fix."

title: seat: per-tick spawn cap starves the fleet when devin is the only usable provider (2-3 workers vs target_concurrent=25, 79 ready)
body:
## What

The usable seat pool has collapsed to ONE provider (devin), and the per-tick spawn cap from fleet-ops#3690 then throttles the whole fleet to ~2 spawns per intake tick. Result: 2-3 live workers against `target_concurrent=25` and 79 ready issues.

## Evidence (verbatim, this run 2026-09-09)

`~/.local/state/pi-packet/watch.log`:

```
[2026-09-09T08:47:24Z] pick_seat: excluded 53 seats (cap=0: 33; dead: 9; not-in-allowlist: 11) [cap0-intentional: 15; cap0-stale: 6]
[2026-09-09T08:47:24Z] pick_seat: at-capacity 1 seats [devin/glm-5-2]
[2026-09-09T08:47:24Z] pick_seat: unusable 13 seats [...]
[2026-09-09T08:47:24Z] pick_seat: NO USABLE SEAT — every allowlisted seat is dead/capped/rate-limited.
```

`journalctl --user -u pi-intake@0509.service`:

```
no usable heavy-capable seat (slots=7); holding claims this tick — gate: pick_seat need_capable=1
```

After the orchestrator smoke-released devin/swe-1-7 at 08:53:40Z (it was quota_benched 6h on a single 429; smoke `pi --print --provider devin --model swe-1-7` returned `OK.` rc=0), intake did spawn — and then hit the per-tick cap on all remaining claims:

```
[2026-09-09T08:54:17Z] pi-issue-run: 0509-1988 running on devin/glm-5-2 (weight=light, tried: 1 seat(s))
[2026-09-09T08:55:05Z] seat devin/glm-5-2 AIMD probe admitted (provider devin cap 2 -> 3: 2 active, zero errors, RAM headroom)
[2026-09-09T08:55:33Z] pi-issue-run: fleet-ops-4621 running on devin/glm-5-2 (weight=light, tried: 1 seat(s))
[2026-09-09T08:55:42Z] seat devin/glm-5-2 skipped (per-tick spawn cap reached for devin — fleet-ops#3690)
[2026-09-09T08:55:42Z] seat devin/swe-1-7 skipped (per-tick spawn cap reached for devin — fleet-ops#3690)
[2026-09-09T08:55:43Z] pick_seat: NO USABLE SEAT — every allowlisted seat is dead/capped/rate-limited.
```

That last pair repeated at 08:55:44, 08:55:55, 08:56:03 and 08:56:08 — five claims spawned, two got seats.

## Why the pool is empty (checked, not guessed)

- Every cap-0 seat that is healthy is **intentionally** cap-0 with a dated citation (xkiro deepseek-v4-flash/pro/minimax-m3:free: "36 picks -> 1 PR"; opencode hy3-free: HTTP 401 corpse). Those are correct and must NOT be loosened — motive 1.
- The rest are quota-walled with future `usable_at`: alibaba-coding (2026-09-14/15), cline (2026-09-19), openrouter (2026-09-10..13), mergegateway (2026-09-13/14), straitly/entrim (2027), runinfra (2026-09-09T17:17Z), zenmux (2026-09-09T15:16Z), orcarouter (2026-09-09T20:01Z).
- ollama and paretoinference are `parked` (dead=true, 2036 dates).
- So devin is the only prepaid seat left, and only devin/opencode-anthropic/reasoning models are heavy-capable at all (`enumerate_seats`, lib/seat-lib.sh:1867).

The continuous top-up from the burst-then-idle task IS wired (`ExecStopPost` on `pi-issue@.service:67` starts an intake tick), so the fault is not the tick cadence — it is that a healthy sole provider cannot be filled past 2 per tick.

## required:

The per-tick spawn cap must not hold slots idle when the provider is demonstrably healthy and it is the ONLY usable provider. Ride the existing AIMD ceiling instead of a fixed per-tick number: if the provider's AIMD probe has admitted a cap raise and the last N spawns on it had zero fast deaths (rc=143/124 inside 60s), allow spawns up to the live AIMD ceiling in one tick. No new organ, no new file — this is a condition inside the existing per-tick cap check in `lib/seat-lib.sh`.

## must-not:

- Do not raise any cap that carries an `intentional_cap_zero` citation.
- Do not remove the per-tick cap outright: #3690 exists because 5 simultaneous devin spawns all died rc=143 in under 30s.
- Do not un-park a seat to relieve this.

## accept:

- A test in `tests/` that fails before and passes after: sole-usable-provider + healthy AIMD state => per-tick cap equals the AIMD ceiling; a provider with a recent fast death => cap stays at the current fixed value.
- `tests/seat-lib-aimd`, `fleet-token-economy` and `seat-caps-citation` all green in the same PR.

## termination:

`bash tests/<new-suite>.test.sh` green, plus 30 minutes of live samples after deploy showing `systemctl --user list-units 'pi-issue@*'` above 2 while `agent-ready` exceeds slots.


---

## Spec block added by judge fable-check :40 (opus-5, 2026-09-11T00:50Z) to clear the spec gate

The spec gate (fleet-ops#543) refused `agent-ready` on 2026-09-10T23:56Z purely for missing strict lines, so this critical-path fix has sat unclaimable since 2026-09-09 while the fault it describes is STILL the fleet's top throughput limiter. Re-confirmed live this run:

```
[2026-09-11T00:44:36Z] pi-intake: usable seat slots 2 < capacity slots 5; claiming at most 2 this tick (fleet-ops#3732)
```
with 14 ready 0509 issues logged `skipped-capacity`, `workers=2`, box 83% idle, `oomd_1h=0`, `ram_gb_per_worker=1.5` and 12Gi available. So this is NOT the RAM-bound class of #4891 and must not be fixed by touching the admission charge — capacity slots were 5 and only 2 were usable. Seat census this run: 23 of 66 ledgers held behind a future `usable_at` (quota_exhausted / quota_bench / rate_limited), only 1 smoke candidate and it was below the bar (cf=2).

files: bin/pi-intake (or the tick's spawn-cap path), lib/seat-lib.sh (pick_seat), config/seat-caps.json
required: when usable seats < capacity slots, the per-tick spawn cap must not ALSO throttle — the tick claims up to the usable-seat count, and a seat freed mid-window is refilled without waiting for the next tick.
do:
1. Separate the two caps: the #3690 per-tick burst guard exists to stop a burst onto ONE provider, so scope it per-provider, not per-tick-global.
2. When `usable seat slots < capacity slots`, log the per-provider breakdown (which seats are walled and until when) in the same line, so the next run judges supply without re-deriving a 66-file census.
3. Leave the refill seam from the continuous top-up work in place; do not add a new organ or a new timer.
must-not: do not raise any provider cap, do not release a seat whose `usable_at` is in the future, do not touch `ram_gb_per_worker` (wrong lever for this fault), do not weaken or skip the seat gate, do not retire a seat on infra deaths (rc=124/143, 429, 503, "no seat available" never count as seat yield).
termination: `bash tests/seat-lib-aimd.test.sh && bash tests/fleet-token-economy.test.sh && bash tests/seat-caps-citation.test.sh` all pass (the three config-pinning suites must agree), plus a replay drill where usable=2 / capacity=5 claims 2 and a freed slot refills inside 60s.
accept: over 2h after deploy, no intake tick logs `skipped-capacity` while usable seats remain, and live `pi-issue@` count tracks the usable-seat count rather than sitting at the per-tick cap.
metric: live worker count p50 over 6h rises from 2 toward the usable-seat count; `skipped-capacity` lines per hour fall to 0 while seats are free.
owner-decision: none — buying more seat capacity WOULD be Nish's call, but this ticket is only about not wasting the slots we already have.

observed: 2026-09-09T15:42Z, a `fleet_detached_job_died{unit="test-unit",dispatch="x",...} 1` series has been live in `/var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter/fleet-detached.prom` since starts_at 1788940504 (2026-09-09T07:55:04Z, ~8h). It fires the `DetachedJobDied` critical alert (`expr: fleet_detached_job_died == 1`, config/fleet_rules.yml:49) continuously. Every DetachedJobDied repair-dispatch packet since then lists it as Alert 1 (e.g. packet-DetachedJobDied-20260909T140915Z.md, ...113215Z.md, ...112415Z.md), so the repair worker spends a tool call reading a phantom that can never be relapsed or cleared by a real unit. No systemd unit named `test-unit` exists; `dispatch="x"` is a placeholder, not a UUID. The deadman writes any series to the production textfile regardless of dispatch shape, and a series is only cleared by a success verdict for the same unit or a manual `bin/pi-detached-deadman --clear <unit>` — so a phantom unit name fires forever.

**Blocked — the accept is not reachable from the `do:` line. The premise ("~10 woff2 files") is false, and I measured it.**

I ran the audit the judge edit asked for, then measured the real first-view payload in a real browser. Not changing the href, because no weight trim moves the number.

### 1. Ground truth: first view is 5 font files, not 10

Real Chromium, cold cache, `https://0509.io/` (also reproduced on a local page that renders every weight):

| file | bytes | serves |
|---|---|---|
| `inter/v20/UcC73FwrK3iLTeHuS_nV…` | 48,256 | Inter 400, 500, 600, 700 |
| `bricolagegrotesque/v9/3y9K6as8bTXq…` | 76,888 | Bricolage 600, 700, 800 |
| `ibmplexmono/v20/-F63fjpt…` | 14,708 | Plex Mono 400 |
| `ibmplexmono/v20/-F6qfjpt…` | 14,888 | Plex Mono 500 |
| `ibmplexmono/v20/-F6qfjpt…` | 15,620 | Plex Mono 600 |

**5 files, 170,360 bytes**, plus the 20,097-byte font stylesheet.

The "roughly 10 woff2 files" in the `why:` is the 10 *requested weights* (4+3+3), not files. Inter and Bricolage are variable fonts: every weight of the same family resolves to the same file.

### 2. Trimming the weight lists is a byte no-op for those two families

| requested | latin file |
|---|---|
| Inter 400 | 23,664 (static instance) |
| Inter 400;500 | 48,256 |
| Inter 400;600;700 | 48,256 |
| Inter 400;500;600;700 (today) | 48,256 |
| Inter 400..700 | 48,256 |
| Bricolage 700 | 39,712 (static instance) |
| Bricolage 700;800 | 76,888 (identical to today) |

Real-browser control, same page, all weights rendered:

- today's href → 5 files / 170,360 B
- href with the unreferenced Bricolage 600 dropped → **5 files / 170,360 B** (byte-identical)
- one weight per family → 3 files / 78,996 B (−54%, but that is a redesign, not a trim)

### 3. What the audit actually found

Rules in `app/app.css` that set both a family and a weight — Inter 400 (29), 500 (9), 600 (26), 700 (1); Bricolage 700 (36), 800 (15), 650 (1); Plex Mono 400 (6), 500 (7), 600 (29), 700 (13). No `font-weight` utilities in TSX; `app/root.tsx:94-95` is the only web-font href in the repo.

- The only unreferenced weight is **Bricolage 600**, and dropping it saves **0 bytes** (same variable file). The one Bricolage 650 rule already renders from the 700 face with or without 600, so that drop is visually safe but pointless.
- The only weights whose removal saves bytes are the three Plex Mono ones (static, one file each), and **all three are referenced**: Plex 400 by `.f9-evidence-*` (6 rules), 500 by `.ld-proof-attrib` / `.f9-ads-eyebrow` / `.f9-wk-kick` (7), 600 by 29 rules. Dropping 400+500 = −29,596 B (−17%) and a visibly lighter Evidence Desk / ads surfaces.
- Plex Mono cannot be collapsed to one file either: `IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400..600` returns HTTP 400 `Font family not found`.

### 4. What would actually move the number — this is a decision, not a trim

- **a. Glyph subsetting** (the `text=` parameter on the css2 URL, or self-hosted subsets). The only lever that touches the 125 KB of Inter + Bricolage. `text=` is unsafe here (briefs and page titles are dynamic); self-hosted subsets are a new mechanism and new files, both outside this issue's scope.
- **b. Cut a family or a weight class by design choice**: one weight per family −54%, or one fewer Plex weight −17%. Both are visual changes.
- **c. Accept 170 KB as the design cost.**

Recommendation: close #2396 as premise-wrong — no weight trim reaches ~40%. If the payload still matters, take option (a) or (b) as its own decision with a design owner.

### 5. Separate finding, not fixed here

13 rules ask for IBM Plex Mono 700 but the sheet loads 400/500/600, so they render from the 600 face. Closing that gap costs +15,620 B, or the rules can be re-pinned to 600 for free. Filed as its own issue.

### Reproduce

UA='Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/140.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'
HREF='<the href in app/root.tsx:95>'
curl -s -A "$UA" "$HREF" | grep -o 'url(https://fonts.gstatic.com[^)]*' | sort -u | wc -l
#    -> 25 unique files across all subsets. The latin subset, which is what a first view
#       fetches, is 5 of them: 1 Inter, 1 Bricolage, 3 Plex Mono.
# 2. first-view bytes: load https://0509.io/ in Chromium with a cold cache and sum the
#    fonts.gstatic.com responses -> 5 files, 170,360 bytes.
# 3. same page with the Bricolage 600 instance removed from the href -> 5 files, 170,360 bytes.
```

title: Signup gauges compare ISO-8601 TEXT against datetime('now','-N days'): a 29-hour-old row counts as 'last 24h' in fleet_product_signups_24h, activated_24h, briefs_delivered_24h and fleet_signups_7d
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/fleet-ops#5000 score=0.53 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/fleet-ops#5000 (score 0.53). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: all four trailing-window D1 reads in the product-outcome family compute the TRUE window: `fleet_product_signups_24h`, `fleet_product_activated_24h` and `fleet_product_briefs_delivered_24h` cover exactly the last 24 hours and `fleet_signups_7d` exactly the last 7 days, proven by a boundary test in which a row 25 hours old is EXCLUDED and a row 23 hours old is INCLUDED (and 8 days old excluded / 6d23h included for the 7-day gauge).

observed: 2026-09-10T15:23Z — all four queries compare an ISO-8601 TEXT timestamp (`user.createdAt TEXT NOT NULL`, `delivery_attempt.sent_at TEXT`) against `datetime('now','-N days')`, which returns a SPACE-separated, no-`Z` string. SQLite compares them as TEXT, so every row on the cutoff *calendar day* counts as inside the window regardless of the hour:

```
$ sqlite3 :memory: "select datetime('now','-1 day'), '2026-09-09T10:00:00.000Z' >= datetime('now','-1 day'), '2026-09-10T08:00:00.000Z' >= datetime('now','-1 day'), '2026-09-08T20:00:00.000Z' >= datetime('now','-1 day');"
2026-09-09 15:23:25|1|1|0
```

The first row is **29 hours old and counted** as "last 24h". Same for the week: cutoff `2026-09-03 15:26:14`, and `'2026-09-03T08:00:00.000Z' >= datetime('now','-7 days')` → `1` for a row 7d7h old. So `fleet_product_signups_24h` is really "signups since 00:00 yesterday" (24–48h) and `fleet_signups_7d` is really 7–8 days.

evidence:
- `lib/fleet-product-slo.py:1079` (`signups_24h`: `WHERE createdAt >= datetime('now','-1 day')`), `:1087` (`activated_24h`: `WHERE u.createdAt >= datetime('now','-1 day')`), `:1098` (`briefs_delivered_24h`: `WHERE status='sent' AND sent_at >= datetime('now','-1 day')`); `libexec/fleet-metrics-export.py:1648` (`_S7_SQL`: `WHERE createdAt >= datetime('now','-7 days')`).
- 0509 schema: `migrations/0000_auth.sql:9` `createdAt TEXT NOT NULL`; `migrations/0007_proof_first_change_alerts.sql:239` `sent_at TEXT`. Stored values are ISO-8601 with `T`/`Z` (0509 test fixtures write `"2026-04-19T00:00:00.000Z"`).
- `sqlite3 :memory: "select datetime('now','-1 day')"` → `2026-09-09 15:23:25` (space, no `T`, no `Z`) — the two formats never compare correctly.
- The correct parse is already used three lines away in the same dict: `:1089` `AND (julianday(da.sent_at)-julianday(u.createdAt))*1440.0 <= 5.0`.
- Live gauges 2026-09-10T15:26Z: `fleet_product_signups_24h 0`, `fleet_product_activated_24h 0`, `fleet_signups_7d 0` — the bug is latent today because the true count is 0, and it inflates the number the moment signups resume.
- `tests/fleet-product-slo.test.sh` (green on main, `OK: fleet-product-slo: …`) and `tests/fleet-metrics-export.test.sh` assert gauge values from mocked D1 rows but exercise no boundary, so the format mismatch is invisible.

accept:
- 1. Every window comparison parses both sides: `julianday(<column>) >= julianday('now','-1 day')` (and `'-7 days'`). An explicit ISO cutoff (`strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now','-1 day')`) is equally acceptable. A pure TEXT comparison is not — that is the defect.
- 2. Fix all four: `signups_24h`, `activated_24h`, `briefs_delivered_24h` in `lib/fleet-product-slo.py` and `_S7_SQL` in `libexec/fleet-metrics-export.py`. Do not change any other predicate, the token handling, the ID validation, or the absent-not-zero contract.
- 3. `tests/fleet-product-slo.test.sh` gains a boundary scenario driven by fixture rows through the existing mocked D1 seam (no network): rows dated 25h ago, 23h ago, 8d ago, 6d23h ago; assert `fleet_product_signups_24h` counts only the 23h row and `fleet_signups_7d`… is asserted in the sibling suite below. Keep every existing scenario.
- 4. `tests/fleet-metrics-export.test.sh` gains the mirror boundary scenario for `_S7_SQL` (rows 8d old excluded, 6d23h old included) next to the existing `fleet_signups_7d` block at lines ~4290-4351.
- 5. The boundary must be asserted at the *day boundary* specifically — a row at `now - 25h` on the previous calendar day is the exact shape the current query gets wrong; a same-day row alone would pass the broken code.
- 6. No new timer, unit, service, MANIFEST entry or token. No rule-threshold change.

verify:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/tooling/fleet-ops-deploy-clone
# the bug, isolated: the left expression must be 0 after the fix is applied to the queries
sqlite3 :memory: "select '2026-09-09T10:00:00.000Z' >= datetime('now','-1 day') AS text_compare_is_wrong, julianday('2026-09-09T10:00:00.000Z') >= julianday(datetime('now','-1 day')) AS julianday_compare_is_right;"
bash tests/fleet-product-slo.test.sh
bash tests/fleet-metrics-export.test.sh

title: reccos: Stop leaking release identity from `/api/health.deep` to anonymous callers
body:
Filed automatically from the Kimi K3 Max 11-lens recommendations pass on 0509 (lens: Security and privacy, ref R5, impact/size L/S). Scope is exactly the `do:` line below — no judgment calls, no extra files. If it cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

why: `app/routes/api.health.deep.ts` returns `releaseIdentity: readReleaseIdentity()` plus scheduled-work health (`ok`/`degraded`) to anyone; its own comment says "Unauthenticated but rate-limited". Worker version id + cron health is free recon for timing deploy windows and knowing when monitoring is degraded.

files: app/routes/api.health.deep.ts, app/routes/api.health.ts, scripts/prod-canary.lib.mjs, scripts/verify-post-deploy-release.mjs, ops/liveness/0509-liveness-probe.sh, .github/workflows/uptime-health.yml
do: Gate the `releaseIdentity` field behind the `x-0509-canary-token` header (value: env `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN`) in both `app/routes/api.health.ts` and `app/routes/api.health.deep.ts` (omit the field for anonymous callers). Keep both status bodies public. Update the VPS liveness probe and the uptime-health workflow so they tolerate a missing `releaseIdentity` and keep asserting `status` / `app` / `checks`. Do not provision `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN` onto the no-secrets DynamicUser liveness unit. If #2359's shared helper is already on main, use it; do not wait for #2359. If the App token refuses the workflow file, still ship the routes + canary scripts + probe; leave the workflow hunk in the PR.
must-not: touch files outside `files:` and the files named in the `do:` step; add a new mechanism, script, or organ; invent product copy, pricing, or unsourced claims; weaken or skip a test; put a canary token on the DynamicUser liveness unit.
termination: npm test
accept: unauthenticated `curl https://0509.io/api/health` and `/api/health/deep` show no `releaseIdentity`; tokened canary scripts still pass; the liveness probe still exits 0 on public status/app/checks without identity.
metric: L-impact / S-size per the lens ranking.
depends-on: none
owner-decision: no
~~blocked-on: orchestrator~~

## Judge edits (binding)
- Wrong endpoint. The leak and all its consumers live on `/api/health`, not health.deep: `api.health.ts:23,30` returns `releaseIdentity` in the body; `prod-canary.lib.mjs:208,221` and `verify-post-deploy-release.mjs:282,294` read it from `/api/health` for deploy-convergence. Gating only health.deep leaves the leak fully open.
- Replace the `do:` line with: "Gate the `releaseIdentity` field behind the `x-0509-canary-token` header in both `app/routes/api.health.ts` and `app/routes/api.health.deep.ts` (omit the field for anonymous callers); keep both status bodies public so the liveness probe and uptime checks still pass."
- Replace `files:` with: `app/routes/api.health.deep.ts, app/routes/api.health.ts, scripts/prod-canary.lib.mjs, scripts/verify-post-deploy-release.mjs` — the two scripts' `/api/health` fetches must attach the token or the accept criterion cannot pass.
- Name the header: replace "Require the `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN` header" with "Require the `x-0509-canary-token` header (value: env `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN`)" — a literal worker will otherwise invent a header named `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN`.
- If #2359 lands first, use its shared helper; add `depends-on: #2359`.

## Orchestrator edits (binding, 2026-09-10)
- Supersedes the judge `files:` line and the `#2359` wait. Probe + uptime workflow are live consumers of `releaseIdentity` and must be in scope.
- Anonymous callers omit `releaseIdentity`. Probes assert public health fields only. No secret on the DynamicUser unit.

claimed by pi-issue-0509-2352 at 2026-09-10T13:35:12Z

**blocked-on: orchestrator** — binding-spec internal conflict: the `releaseIdentity` gate and a live production consumer cannot both be satisfied within the given `files:` allowlist.

**The conflict**

The judge's binding edits (spec-judged, 2026-09-10):
- `do:` — "Gate the `releaseIdentity` field behind the `x-0509-canary-token` header in both `app/routes/api.health.ts` and `app/routes/api.health.deep.ts` (omit the field for anonymous callers); **keep both status bodies public so the liveness probe and uptime checks still pass**."
- `files:` — exactly `app/routes/api.health.deep.ts`, `app/routes/api.health.ts`, `scripts/prod-canary.lib.mjs`, `scripts/verify-post-deploy-release.mjs`.

But there are **two additional live consumers of `releaseIdentity`** that are NOT in the allowlist and that fail hard when the field is absent:

1. **`ops/liveness/0509-liveness-probe.sh`** — currently deployed on the VPS (`/opt/0509-liveness/0509-liveness-probe.sh`, installed 2026-08-13, `0509-liveness.service`/`.timer` run every 5 min). Its shallow and deep checks both do:
   - `identity = payload.get("releaseIdentity") or {}`
   - require `identity.workerVersionId` to be a non-empty safe string and `identity.searchRolloutMode == "v2"`, else `SystemExit("health worker version was missing or unsafe")` / probe exits nonzero.
   - The unit runs `DynamicUser=yes`, "uses no secrets… only needs outbound HTTPS to 0509.io" (and `provision-production-liveness.sh` states the same). It has **no** `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN` and cannot be given one without changing its no-secrets security model — out of scope.
   - Gating `releaseIdentity` makes the probe red every 5 minutes: `worker_version_parse_failed` / degraded.

2. **`.github/workflows/uptime-health.yml`** — the on-demand/shallow check reads `releaseIdentity.workerVersionId` + `searchRolloutMode=="v2"` from `/api/health` and the deep check cross-checks `workerVersionId` against it. Runs with `permissions: contents: read` only — **no secrets** — so it cannot attach the token either. It would fail on the next manual/on-demand run.

**Why it cannot be done as written**

- Option A — gate within the allowlist only: breaks the live liveness probe (violates the binding `do:` "liveness probe… still pass").
- Option B — keep the probe passing: requires editing `ops/liveness/0509-liveness-probe.sh` (and provision script + service to credential it) and `uptime-health.yml`, which are outside the binding `files:` allowlist, AND requires provisioning a secret to a no-secrets DynamicUser probe — a category change the allowlist forbids.

Both binding requirements (gate + probe passes) + the binding file allowlist cannot be satisfied simultaneously.

**Proposed resolutions (pick one)**

1. **Add the liveness probe + uptime workflow to the allowlist**, and gate them too — have them read `releaseIdentity` only when a token is available, else tolerate absence (keep `status`/`app`/`checks` assertions). This keeps the shallow liveness read (worker alive, D1 ok, scheduled ok) and drops the worker-version identity assertion for the unauthenticated path. Smallest risk of breaking the live probe.
2. Re-scope to gate `releaseIdentity` only in the deep route `/api/health/deep`, leaving `/api/health` (shallow, edge-only, monitor-facing) public — narrower fix, but means the shallow probe keeps the leak (the judge already rejected this endpoint in the first judge edit, so not my preference).
3. Provision `CANARY_BYPASS_TOKEN` to the liveness unit and have the probe attach it (largest change — touches the no-secrets probe design and deploy provisioning).

I recommend **resolution 1** as it honors both the leak-gate and the live-probe continuity with the smallest blast radius, but I need the scope widened since the probe/workflow files are currently out of the binding allowlist.

The route + canary-script implementation is done and green (see worktree `claim/issue-2352`); I've paused rather than ship a spec-blind change that takes down a live 5-minute monitor.

#2375 asked for exactly this (`files: scripts/ci-authorize-candidate.sh`, "replace all 9 inline copies with one call", same `sha_pattern`-drops-to-0 `accept` line). Orchestrator verdict 2026-09-10T20:55:46Z: "close. **1. It is 13 guard bodies in 9 files, not 9 blocks, and not one block.** Five distinct event contracts (A `ci.yml`×5 + `preview-assert.yml`; A' `secret-scan.yml`; B `d1-backup-r2.yml` + `d1-restore-proof-auto-refresh.yml`; B' `d1-remote-restore-evidence.yml`; C `deploy-production.yml`; D `gate-integrity.yml` + `required-verifier-integrity.yml`, which carry no `sha_pattern` at all). `grep -rn "sha_pattern" .github/workflows/ | wc -l` = 33. "One call per job" therefore means the event policy becomes a mode argument — a design decision the `do:` line says not to make.

**2. The pinned tests forbid the only implementation that can satisfy the judge's binding edit.** The judge edit requires the script to "execute from the base-ref checkout, never the PR head tree". Every authorizer is step 0 with no prior checkout, and four of them run with `permissions: {}`, so that can only be met by adding `contents: read` plus a `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` fetch to each — which four pinned tests explicitly prohibit:

- `tests/d1-backup-workflow.test.ts:60` — `expect(authorize?.permissions).toEqual({})`
- `tests/d1-backup-workflow.test.ts:62` — `expect(JSON.stringify(authorize)).not.toMatch(/actions\/checkout|secrets\.|wrangler|cloudflare/i)`
- `tests/production-candidate-workflow.test.ts:98` — `expect(authorize?.steps).toHaveLength(1)`, with the same `permissions: {}` and `not.toMatch` pins at :95 and :100
- `tests/d1-backup-workflow.test.ts:66` — `expect(authorizeScript).toBe([...])`, byte-exact on the whole inline body

Satisfying `accept:` therefore means deleting security assertions, i.e. weakening a gate: forbidden, and the reason the repo pins them there in the first place.

**3. Two gates the plan does not account for.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `secret-scan.yml`, `required-verifier-integrity.yml` and `deploy-production.yml` are all on `protected_files` in `.github/scripts/required-verifier-integrity.sh` (jq block at lines 207-217), and every in-scope path matches `.github/workflows/**` in `gate-integrity`'s `gate_globs`. title: feat(landing-page): fix top-3 bail-out reasons after #1500 telemetry (follow-up)
body:
## Follow-up to #1500: post-telemetry bail-out fixes + docs

Issue #1500 ships the `lp_run_audit` instrumentation that makes the CTA
detector's silent-77-day failure diagnosable, plus a 7-day canary that
fires when the detector goes silent again. This issue tracks the
telemetry-driven second half: read one week of `lp_run_audit` lines
from Workers Logpush, document the top bail-out reasons by frequency,
and fix the top 3.

Motive: paid-quality wedge — the landing-page CTA detector is the thing
that keeps the public /compare and /search surfaces from regressing; the
top bail-out reasons are the wedge's hidden failure points, so fixing them
is direct product-quality work in front of prospective buyers.

### What needs to happen (in order)

1. **Read one week of audit data.** After #1500 lands in production,
   accumulate at least 7 days of `tag: "lp_run_audit"` lines. Group by
   stage + outcome, sort by frequency.
2. **Write `docs/detector-bail-out-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`.** Top 5
   bail-out reasons by frequency, one worked example per reason (real
   domain, real HTML, real bail). Commit the doc to the repo.
3. **Fix the top 3 bail-out reasons in the same PR series.** Each fix
   ships a unit test under `tests/unit/landing-page-extractor/` that
   feeds mock HTML exhibiting the bail pattern and asserts the fix
   either emits the field or records a specific, narrower bail reason.
4. **Extend the 7-day canary.** Once fixes land, the canary should
   alarm on a rate below 1 event per 25 watchlists per 7 days. The
   current canary already exits 1 on zero events in the window.

termination: `npm run canary:cta-detector` exits 0 against production D1 in a 7-day window that produced at least 1 CTA event, and `docs/detector-bail-out-audit-2026-*.md` exists naming the top bail-out reasons.
accept:
- `docs/detector-bail-out-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` committed to the repo.
- Top 3 bail-out reasons each ship a fix + a unit test under `tests/unit/landing-page-extractor/`.
- `npm run canary:cta-detector` exits 0 against production D1 in a 7-day window that produced at least 1 CTA event.
required: no new D1 table; the audit stream lives in Workers Logs / Logpush; no DDL in the same commit as a fix.

### Related

- Blocked-by: #1500 (audit instrumentation needs to be in production for at least 7 days before the telemetry can be read).
