title: throughput: measure whether local vitest/workerd runs inside worker worktrees are the CPU limiter on the 8-core host (load 13-16 with 68 ready items), then trial 'vitest related' + CI offload
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-10 00:40 UTC) after Nish asked "make sure the fleet is going ham at all times". Population-first per the no-fixes-from-log-lines rule: this ticket MEASURES before it changes anything.

**Snapshot (one sample, not proof):** load 16.4/7.7/6.8 then 13.3/9.5/7.5 on 8 cores; CPU 53% user, 12% sys, 6.7% iowait, 25% idle; RAM 7.6 GB available (not the limiter). Top consumers: `tsc -b` in agent-worktrees/kimi-issue-2174 (118%), `vitest run --project workers` in kimi-issue-2106 with six `workerd` children (79% + 6x20-50%), camoufox (a reviewer). Ready queue: 0509=45, fleet-ops=23. Merged last 24h: 0509=63, fleet-ops=45, total 109 vs the 300/day target. Active implementers: 4 Kimi K3 Max (cursor-agent) + ~7 pi-issue. Adding workers on this box would oversubscribe CPU further, so seats are not the binding constraint right now; CPU per worker-run may be.

files: libexec/fleet-metrics-export.py (or the metrics path it feeds), a new short-lived sampler under libexec/ (delete after the study), docs/ (one findings note), and - only if the study confirms - the worker prompt/wrapper that tells implementers how to run tests (pi-issue-run + prompts/*, kimi-issue-run.sh in agent-state/fleet-landing-watch/acq-pass2)

do:
1. Sample for 24h at 60s: load1, %idle, %iowait, per-process CPU seconds attributed to worker worktrees (pi-issue-*/kimi-issue-*/issue-*), grouped by command class (tsc, vitest+workerd, wrangler/esbuild, node build, git, gh, pi/cursor-agent). Store as one JSONL under agent-state/fleet-metrics/ (no new timer: run the sampler as ONE pi-systemd-run unit with --deadline 1500 that exits on its own).
2. Join with merged-PR timestamps (gh, one call per repo) to produce: CPU-seconds per merged PR, share of CPU by command class, and hours where load1 > 2x cores while ready > 20 (the "saturated with backlog" condition).
3. Control: the same numbers for a 24h window from 7 days earlier if the metrics export already has them; otherwise state "no control".
4. Decision rule written in the findings note: if vitest+workerd+tsc are >= 50% of worker CPU AND the saturated-with-backlog condition holds >= 6 of 24 hours, the limiter is local test runs. Then, and only then, run a 24h trial on ONE repo (0509): worker instructions change from full `vitest run` to `vitest related <changed files>` + typecheck, with the full suite left to CI on the hosted runners (0509 already runs CI there). Measure merges/day and revert-rate before/after. If the rule is not met, close this issue with the numbers and name the next suspect (seat rate limits / claim-loop empty-success churn - see #4457 - are the two candidates seen in the same snapshot).
5. Findings note in docs/ with the exact commands; delete the sampler.

must-not: change worker prompts before the decision rule is met; add a timer or dispatcher; touch CI workflows; run the trial on more than one repo; weaken any gate (CI still runs the full suite).

termination: the findings note exists with the four numbers (CPU share by class, CPU-seconds per merge, saturated-with-backlog hours, control or "no control") and either the trial result or the named next suspect

accept: a decision backed by 24h of population data, not a snapshot

metric: merged PRs/day (target 300) and revert-rate, before vs after the trial

depends-on: none. Possible duplicate: search fleet-ops for an open throughput-limiter ticket naming CPU first; if one exists, fold these numbers into it and close this.

owner-decision: no

The credential-expiry canary detected a model-seat credential with a known

seat-health ledger only records credentials_bad AFTER a worker burns a slot

Renew the `xai-oauth` credential. For xai-oauth (SuperGrok), the
grok-token-refresh.timer is the heal path — check
`systemctl --user status grok-token-refresh.service` and
`journalctl --user -u grok-token-refresh.service`. If the timer is
healthy the next tick will rotate the token and this issue auto-closes
(observe-to-close).

The credential-expiry canary next tick no longer reports
PRE-EXPIRY-DETECTED for `xai-oauth` — this issue observe-to-closes.

title: intake: honor 'depends-on: #N' in ticket bodies - never claim a ticket whose named dependencies are not merged/closed (0509 seam batch had to be hand-gated tonight)
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-10 01:25 IST). Scope is exactly the numbered steps below - no judgment calls; if a step cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Why:** every ticket in the house format carries a `depends-on:` line, but `rg -i depends-on` over bin/, libexec/, lib/, pi-intake*, pi-issue-run finds NOTHING - intake claims regardless. Tonight's 0509 batch (seam #2218 first, six sources in parallel after it, #2213 -> #2217, #2188 last) had to be hand-gated by removing agent-ready and asking the hourly Fable check to re-add labels on merge. That is a human doing a machine's job.

files: the intake claim path (locate: pi-intake / ready-work dispatch where `skipped-claim-pr-open` and `skipped-reclaim-cooldown` are decided), its tests, README section on the ticket format

do:
1. Parse `depends-on:` from the issue body: extract every `#<n>` (same repo) and `owner/repo#<n>`; ignore prose like "none" or "any of".
2. Before claiming, resolve each referenced issue: DONE if it is closed as completed OR has a merged PR whose branch is `claim/issue-<n>` / `fable/issue-<n>` / any PR linked via "closes #n". If any referenced issue is not DONE, skip with reason `skipped-depends-on:#n` (same log line shape as the existing skip reasons); do not de-label.
3. Cache the resolution per tick (one gh call per referenced issue per tick, memoised).
4. Tests: parse cases (none / one / many / cross-repo / prose), DONE via closed, DONE via merged PR, not DONE -> skip line, cycle (A depends on B depends on A) -> skip both with reason `depends-on-cycle`.
5. README: document the line format and the skip reason.

must-not: add a scheduler or a second queue; change claim ordering for tickets without depends-on; treat an OPEN PR as DONE.

termination: the fleet-ops test suite passes with the new tests && one real tick log shows `skipped-depends-on:#2218` for 0509#2181 while #2218 is unmerged

accept: no ticket with an unmerged dependency is ever claimed; the hand gate in the Fable brief can be deleted.

metric: claims on tickets with unmet depends-on per day (target 0)

depends-on: none

owner-decision: no

title: cursor_today reads $0.00 while 50 Cursor senior-review sessions ran in 24h — $400 API pool expires ~2026-09-21 (child of #3150)
body:
Child of #3150 (metered spend is invisible).

## Evidence (this run, 2026-09-09 08:20 IST / 02:50Z)

```
$ bash agent-state/fleet-landing-watch/measure.sh
usd_24h: metered=29.550083 flat_share=0 cursor_today=0.000000 cursor_target_per_day=28

$ cat ~/.local/state/pi-packet/prepaid-usage/cursor*.json
{"week":"2026-W37","count":4}
{"week":"2026-W37","count":98,"usd_today":"0.000000",...}

$ grep -a 'running on cursor/' ~/.local/state/pi-packet/watch.log | (24h window)
cursor_runs_24h=50     # incl. weight=senior-review pi-issue and agent-cron runs
```

50 Cursor sessions ran in 24h on `cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high` (the senior/keystone
seat) and the spend reader still reports `usd_today=0.000000`.

## Why this matters

The $400 Cursor "API Usage" pool expires at the cycle reset (~2026-09-21, 12 days).
The standing target is >= $28/day. Every run the judge reads `cursor_today` to
decide whether to raise the senior-review share — and that number has been 0 while
the seat was demonstrably busy. The judgment input is unusable either way.

## Two candidate causes — decide by evidence, not by log lines

1. **Reader blind.** The prepaid-usage reader never populates `usd_today` for
   cursor (writes the literal "0.000000"), so real burn is invisible.
2. **Wrong billing lane.** The sessions bill the Cursor Ultra *included*
   subscription, not the $400 API pool, so 0.000000 is truthful — and the pool
   will expire ~100% unused on 2026-09-21.

These need opposite fixes, so do NOT patch from the log lines.

## Required
- Determine which lane the 50 sessions billed to (Cursor dashboard/API export vs
  the reader's source), with the raw numbers pasted.
- If (1): fix the reader so `usd_today` reflects real API-pool spend.
- If (2): say so explicitly and report what routing change would move senior work
  onto the API pool — do NOT make a spend commitment; the pool is already paid for,
  but any change in billing lane is reported, not decided, by the worker.

## Accept
- `measure.sh` prints a `cursor_today` that provably tracks real spend (one command
  reproducing the same figure from the vendor side), or a one-line stated reason
  the pool cannot be billed by fleet sessions.
- Deadline matters: after ~2026-09-21 the pool is gone and this issue is moot.

No money decision is being asked for here — the pool is already purchased.

Ship it as a PR series (each PR <= ~800 lines, tests green, no new deps, no design-system rewrite, no pricing changes, no MagicBrief references). List every product decision you could not make in a 'needs Nish' section of the final PR body; never guess on money, pricing, legal, or brand copy — build behind a nish-reserved label instead.

Thesis: 8 of 15 signups never created a watchlist; every rival makes the customer know and hand-add competitors. Auto-discovery (#1366, phases 1-5 merged) exists but is a panel inside the app.

5. Tests: handoff token round-trip, onboarding creates N watchlists within limits, first-capture trigger fires once (idempotent).

termination: npm run typecheck && npm test

body:

metric: Every sitemap-canonical /compare/* page carries at least one interior link to a live /ads/:domain (or /timeline/:domain) page that returns HTTP 200 with verified ads, so a comparison-page visitor can see the product working instead of only reading claims.

observed: 2026-09-09T05:27Z live. `/compare/visualping-ad-libraries` is the sitemap canonical for the Visualping comparison (BET 5 / BET 8). The page names Visualping's Ad Library playbook and 0509's domain-paste job, then the CTA is a bare `/search`. A visitor comparing 0509 to Visualping never sees a real brand wall, even though 52 `/ads/:domain` pages sit in the sitemap and `/ads/nike.com` returns 200 with 14 verified ads.

The north-star rule is "be clearly better than the customer's own AI". A comparison page that only asserts "domain paste + proof" without showing one proof page is parity copy. The unpaid-distribution direction needs these pages to convert comparison-intent into a signed-in watch; the missing worked example is the conversion leak.

evidence:
- https://0509.io/compare/visualping-ad-libraries — unique `/ads/` hrefs = 0, unique `/timeline/` hrefs = 0, CTA `/search`
- https://0509.io/compare — unique `/ads/` hrefs = 0

title: /search mislabels all major-brand ads as 'Unmatched' while /ads/:domain treats them as verified/brand-owned
body:
source: north-star rule ("If it is not verified, say so. If it is verified, do not present it as unverified.") + market-signal 2026-08-27 §1.8 ("verified copy must match the first visible row") + 2026-08-28 merged PR "fix(search): attach domainMatch tier labels to q= keyword results", which deployed the tier-label code but still leaves major-brand results as "Unmatched".

observed: 2026-08-29T10:48Z UTC, production https://0509.io.
- `/search?q=nike&country=all` says "Nike ads from the Meta Ad Library's all-countries query" and renders 18 results.
- Every result row is labelled `Unmatched — …` (e.g. `Unmatched — Compra los mejores estilos con la mejor tecnología e innovación Nike…`).
- The public brand page `/ads/nike.com`, using the same ad set, says "Nike was running 18 Meta ads at the last check" and lists the same ad copy without the `Unmatched` caveat.
- Same for `/search?q=adidas&country=all` (24/24 `Unmatched`; `/ads/adidas.com` says "Running 24 Meta ads") and `/search?q=shopify&country=all` (28/28 `Unmatched`; `/ads/shopify.com` says "Running 24 Meta ads").

impact: The free preview is the only first-value moment in the funnel (transformation campaign §1.2, BET 2). A buyer evaluating Nike/Adidas/Shopify sees the product disclaim its own subject on every row — the exact trust-destroying pattern the north-star rule forbids. It also makes the programmatic `/ads/:domain` pages (BET 5) harder to trust from the top of the funnel.

verify: Playwright prod-public test loads `/search?q=nike&country=all` and asserts at least one result row does NOT start with `Unmatched —` (i.e. the brand/advertiser is recognised as verified or likely, not unmatched).

termination: `npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts --project=prod-public tests/e2e/search-major-brand-verified-labels.spec.ts` exits 0. Do not close until the same assertion passes for `/search?q=adidas&country=all` and `/search?q=shopify&country=all`.

dedupe: Not a duplicate of #1269 (slack/tcs 0 rows), #1376 (pre-search brochure state), or #1431 (`/ads/notion.so` noindex). This is the tier-label regression left by the search-v2 domainMatch change.

title: Shrink VPS off-site backups: exclude regenerable trees, cap the locked mirror, decide B2 vs R2 (~$1.55/mo → ~$0.50)
body:
## Measured 2026-09-17
- Live restic repo `nish-hostinger-kvm4-backups/hostinger-kvm4`: 19 snapshots, 42.3 GiB stored (compression 3.23x), latest snapshot restores to 129.4 GiB / 2.23M files. Sources: /home/nish /etc /root /usr/local /var/spool/cron /var/lib/docker/volumes. Retention: backup script `--keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4`, maintenance `--keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 5 --keep-monthly 12`. Still carries July `hostinger-kvm4` snapshots.
- Locked mirror `nish-hostinger-kvm4-backups-locked`: rclone copy, never deletes, 40.7 GB Standard + 21.3 GB IA, growing ~1 GB/day (script comment).
- R2 cost ≈ $0.72 live + $0.82 locked ≈ $1.55/mo. Nish asked to bring it down (2026-09-17).

## Do (in order, each reversible)
1. Measure what dominates the 129 GiB: `restic ls latest` size by top-level dir under /home/nish. Expected: agent-worktrees (~440 MB each), ~/.pi sessions, Documents/Last30Days raw dumps, workspace .git objects that exist on GitHub. Add the regenerable ones to /etc/restic/hostinger-r2-excludes; keep agent-state, vault, ~/.config, dotfiles, docker volumes.
2. Drop the July hostinger-kvm4 host snapshots (`restic forget --host hostinger-kvm4 --prune`) after confirming netcup snapshots cover everything.
3. Locked mirror: switch from a single ever-growing copy to dated prefixes (`hostinger-kvm4/<YYYY-MM>/`) with a 90-day expiry on the bucket, per the r2-restic-lifecycle-trap note (never age-expire a live restic repo; dated whole-repo copies expire as a unit).
4. Price B2 ($6.95/TB, free egress to 3x stored) for the locked mirror only; R2 stays for the live repo (zero egress for restore tests). Report both numbers; switch only if Nish says so (new account = money class).

Proof: `r2StorageAdaptiveGroups` max payloadSize per bucket after one weekly maintenance cycle, and `restic-r2-restore-test` still green.

title: fix(test): mention-digest-resweep idempotency-key regex hardcodes 2026-08, flakes on month boundary (blocks codex-node-checks)
body:
metric: `tests/integration/mention-digest-resweep.integration.test.ts` hardcodes `2026-08-\d{2}` in the presence-digest idempotency-key regex, so the test flakes on every month boundary. Today (2026-09-08) it fails: `expected 'presence-digest:user_0017:2026-09-01' to match /^presence-digest:user_\d{4}:2026-08-\…/`.

observed: 2026-09-08, codex-node-checks (shard 1) fails on `main` and on every open PR with this one assertion. The idempotency key date is derived from `Date.now() - lookbackHours*3600*1000` (lookback 168h, `app/lib/presence-digest.server.ts:32,55`), so it rolls with the current date; the test regex does not.

evidence:
- `tests/integration/mention-digest-resweep.integration.test.ts:281` — `expect(call[1].idempotencyKey).toMatch(/^presence-digest:user_\d{4}:2026-08-\d{2}$/);`
- `app/lib/presence-digest.server.ts:32` — `const since = new Date(Date.now() - lookbackHours * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();` ; line 55 — `idempotencyKey: \`presence-digest:${userId}:${since.slice(0, 10)}\``
- Local run on clean `origin/main` (no PR changes): `npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/mention-digest-resweep.integration.test.ts` → `1 failed | 5 passed`, `AssertionError: expected 'presence-digest:user_0017:2026-09-01' to match /^presence-digest:user_\d{4}:2026-08-\d{2}$/`.
- Last green CI on `main` was 2026-08-23 (still August, regex matched); every CI run since the Sep 1 boundary fails this assertion.

accept:
- Change the regex at `tests/integration/mention-digest-resweep.integration.test.ts:281` to be date-agnostic: `/^presence-digest:user_\d{4}:\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/` (assert the SHAPE of the key, not a hardcoded month). The test already asserts the full key shape (`presence-digest:user_<4 digits>:<ISO date>`); hardcoding the month was the bug.
- `npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/mention-digest-resweep.integration.test.ts` exits 0.
- codex-node-checks on `main` and dependent PRs goes green again.

rollback: revert the one-line regex change.

dedupe: none found — no other test hardcodes a `2026-08` presence-digest date.

impact: blocks the required `codex-node-checks` check on every open PR from 2026-09-01 until fixed; no PR can merge.

title: canary:bet7 — fresh-email signup → on-screen first brief → first-brief email (BET 7 activation verification)
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1408 score=0.50 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1408 (score 0.50). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: A fresh-email end-to-end run produces an on-screen first brief with ≥1 evidence-linked item within 5 minutes of signup AND a delivered `first_brief` digest/email within 60 minutes. Proven by a repo canary that exits 0, in the same class as canary:bet2/bet3/bet9.

observed: 2026-08-29. The BET 7 activation feature has shipped and its loader has a unit/integration test, but NO repo canary or live verifier exercises the full signup → first scan → on-screen brief → first-brief email path. `package.json` ships `canary:bet2`, `canary:bet3`, `canary:bet9` (and `canary:proof/billing/pricing/fanout/presence`) but NOT `canary:bet7`. The merged onboard PR ("feat(onboard): enable SIGNUP_FIRST_BRIEF_ENABLED and pin parser regression") and the first-brief loader integration test (`tests/integration/signup-first-brief.integration.test.ts`, from closed issue #1276) cover the loader's ready/waiting states and the `funnel_first_brief_viewed` event with SEEDED rows — not a real unattended fresh-email signup. BET 7's whole point (research §3.4) is that the free plan's first real output is a weekly brief, so a new user waits up to 7 days; the fix is "send a real brief on screen inside the same session" + "a 'your first brief' email within the hour." Nothing proves that delivered.

evidence:
- `package.json` scripts: `canary:bet2`, `canary:bet3`, `canary:bet9` exist; `canary:bet7` does not
- `tests/integration/signup-first-brief.integration.test.ts` (Issue #1276 — seeded loader test, not end-to-end)
- merged PR title: "feat(onboard): enable SIGNUP_FIRST_BRIEF_ENABLED and pin parser regression"
- Precedent for bet-canary issues: #1408 (Add canary:bet1), #1270, #973, #972

accept:
- Add `canary:bet7` → `node scripts/bet7-activation-verification.mjs --json`.
- The script performs a genuine fresh-email signup (non-reused address per run), triggers the first scan, and asserts:
  (a) an on-screen first-brief payload with ≥1 evidence-linked item appears within the same session (≤5 min), and
  (b) a `first_brief` digest run / delivered-email row exists in D1 within 60 minutes (support a `--window` flag and a wait loop, matching the bet2/bet1 canary style).
- Reuse the existing auth/e2e infrastructure (`scripts/e2e-auth-capture.mjs`, `e2e:serve:local`) if signup requires email verification, so the canary runs unattended.
- Do NOT gate pass/fail on `FUNNEL_MEASUREMENT_ENABLED` funnel events: the funnel-measurement compliance gate is `[NISH]` (campaign §3.7) and the fleet should not decide it. Assert on the brief + email artifacts instead.
- Pin a parser-regression assertion (reuse the CLI check the merged onboard PR pinned) so the scanning pipeline is proven end-to-end.
- If the house wires bet canaries into CI or a scheduled canary group, do the same for bet7; otherwise a locally runnable script that exits 0 is sufficient.

verify: `npm run canary:bet7 -- --email=<fresh> --domain=nykaa.com` (after the script lands) exits 0.

rollback: Remove/revert the canary script and its package.json entry. No data or schema change; no migration. Additive.

dedupe: #1276 (first-brief loader) is CLOSED and is unit/integration level on seeded rows. This is the end-to-end live verification, same class as #1408 (canary:bet1). No open issue (of the 86 checked) runs an unattended fresh-email signup→brief→email check; `canary:bet7` is absent from package.json.

impact: BET 7 is the retention door for the product's real (if tiny) user base: 2 external signups with 0 watchlists each, newest 63+ days ago (research §1.4). A user whose first brief never arrives, or takes a week, churns. The shipped feature needs a proof it actually delivers the free plan's promise — that is exactly what a canary provides, and the house already runs canaries for bets 1-3 and 9.

product_surface: signup → `/app/onboard?step=first-brief` → first-brief email (BET 7 activation).

termination: `node scripts/bet7-activation-verification.mjs --json` exits 0 (the canary is the deliverable: it must assert the on-screen brief with ≥1 evidence-linked item and a delivered `first_brief` email).

source: Transformation campaign §3.4 BET 7 — "Send a 'your first brief' email within the hour rather than on the weekly cron" + BET 7 termination check: "A clean end-to-end run from a fresh email address produces an on-screen brief with ≥1 evidence-linked item within 5 minutes of signup and a delivered email within 60 minutes." North-star rule: hands-free finished outcomes the customer's own AI cannot produce for them.

title: robots.txt serves two User-agent: * groups + duplicate AI-bot blocks — Cloudflare managed robots collides with repo ROBOTS_TXT
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1447 score=0.42 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1447 (score 0.42). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: `curl -sS https://production-origin/robots.txt` contains exactly one `User-agent: *` group and each AI-training crawler appears exactly once; no bot block is duplicated.

observed: 2026-08-30 against production `https://0509.io/robots.txt`. The live file has TWO `User-agent: *` groups and every AI-training crawler is listed twice. The Cloudflare edge "managed robots" feature prepends a managed block (a `User-agent: *` group with `Content-Signal` + `Allow: /`, then 8 AI-bot `Disallow: /` entries framed by `# BEGIN Cloudflare Managed content` / `# END Cloudflare Managed Content`), and the repo's own `ROBOTS_TXT` in `app/lib/seo.ts` ALSO serves the same 8 AI-bot deny block plus a second `User-agent: *` group + `Sitemap:` directive. The seo.ts comment says "The Cloudflare edge managed robots.txt enforces the same deny list at the zone; this file carries the policy in repo so the stance survives edge feature changes. Keep the lists in sync" — but "in sync" while both are active means duplicated, not mirrored.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^User-agent: \*'` → `2`
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^User-agent: GPTBot'` → `2` (same for Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, ClaudeBot, CloudflareBrowserRenderingCrawler, Google-Extended, meta-externalagent)
- `app/lib/seo.ts:416-435` — `AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS` (9 bots) → `AI_TRAINING_BLOCK` → interpolated into `ROBOTS_TXT`, which is served by `publicSeoFileForPathname("/robots.txt")` via `workers/app.ts:100`
- Live file lines 27-60 carry the Cloudflare-managed block (comments + `User-agent: *` + 8 denies); lines 62-99 carry the repo block (8 denies again + second `User-agent: *` + `Sitemap:`)

accept:
- Pick ONE source of truth for the AI-training deny list and remove the other. Either (a) drop `AI_TRAINING_BLOCK` from the repo `ROBOTS_TXT` and rely on the Cloudflare managed-robots zone feature (keeping the repo wildcard group + `Sitemap:` directive only), or (b) disable the Cloudflare managed-robots feature at the zone and keep the repo `ROBOTS_TXT` as the sole source. State which path was chosen in the PR body.
- The served `robots.txt` has exactly one `User-agent: *` group.
- Every entry in `AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS` appears at most once in the served file.
- The `Sitemap: https://0509.io/sitemap.xml` directive is preserved (it currently only lives in the repo block; if path (a) is chosen, confirm the directive still renders).
- If path (a) is chosen, add a one-line comment in `app/lib/seo.ts` noting the AI deny list is owned by the Cloudflare managed-robots zone feature so a future reader does not re-add it. If path (b), update `docs/ai-crawler-policy.md` to record that the zone feature is off and the repo is sole source.
- No change to the actual crawl policy: search/AI-answer engines stay allowed, AI-training crawlers stay denied, `/share/` stays crawlable, `/app` and `/api/` stay disallowed.

verify:
```
curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^User-agent: \*'   # expect 1
curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^User-agent: GPTBot' # expect 1
curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^Sitemap:'          # expect 1
curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -i 'Disallow: /$'        # AI-training denies still present
```

rollback: revert the `app/lib/seo.ts` change (and re-enable the Cloudflare managed-robots zone feature if path (b) was taken). The duplication is cosmetically ugly but not a crawl outage, so re-introducing it is a safe rollback state.

dedupe: none. No open issue or PR addresses robots.txt structure. #1283/#1442/#1431 cover /ads noindex gating; #1457 covers hreflang; none cover the robots.txt duplication.

impact: BET 5 distribution depends on clean, unambiguous crawl signals for the programmatic /ads/:domain surface (now ~30 indexable brand pages in the sitemap). Non-spec-compliant crawlers that pick the first matching `User-agent: *` group and stop can mis-resolve the policy when two wildcard groups disagree in ordering; the duplicate AI-bot blocks signal an unmaintained policy to anyone inspecting the file. This is the single public file that tells every crawler what the programmatic SEO surface is allowed to do.

product_surface: public crawl policy / SEO (robots.txt)

termination: `test "$(curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^User-agent: \*')" = "1" && test "$(curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep -c '^User-agent: GPTBot')" = "1" && test -n "$(curl -sS https://0509.io/robots.txt | grep '^Sitemap:')"`

source: BET 5 — "Add every compare page and every /ads/ page to the sitemap, with per-page structured data" (transformation campaign, 0509-daily-market-signal 2026-08-29); north-star rule "be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI" requires the distribution surface to actually reach crawlers, and robots.txt is the gate.

title: BET 7: First brief on screen in same session — signup → activation scan → real brief before they close the tab
body:
metric: A clean end-to-end run from a fresh email address produces an on-screen brief with ≥1 evidence-linked item within 5 minutes of signup and a delivered email within 60 minutes; funnel events show `signup → first_brief_viewed` in the same session.

observed: 2026-08-31 against production. Two plausible external signups (2026-06-23 and earlier), **zero watchlists between them**. The free plan's first real output is a *weekly* brief — a new user waits up to 7 days for the thing they signed up for. The bulk competitor import (`app/lib/competitor-import.ts`) is buried in the onboarding checklist, not reachable from `/app/watchlists`. Research: "the first paid path still feels like separate features instead of one Market Desk setup that produces a useful brief."

evidence:
- Research: category-research.md §1.4: "2 plausible external signups, both with zero watchlists, none in 63 days, 0 paid, 1 checkout attempt ever"
- Research: category-research.md §3.4 BET 7: "Signup → activation scan → **a real brief on screen inside the same session**, built from the baseline capture plus whatever history exists for that domain, not an empty 'we'll email you Monday' state. Surface the bulk competitor import on `/app/watchlists` too. Send a 'your first brief' email within the hour rather than on the weekly cron."
- Research: category-research.md §1.7: "The free search preview is the *only* first-value moment in the funnel." But after signup, the value drops to zero until the weekly cron.
- Open issue #1445: canary test only (`canary:bet7 — fresh-email signup → on-screen first brief → first-brief email`); #1266: bulk import on `/app/watchlists` only. Core activation flow not filed.

source: category-research.md §3.4 BET 7 (transformation bet) + §1.4 traction data + §1.7 funnel analysis + north-star rule (memory north-star-edge-ai-cannot-match: "finished hands-free outcomes")

accept:
1. After email verification, the onboarding flow triggers an immediate activation scan for the first competitor (or pasted list via bulk import) and renders a real brief on `/app/onboarding/brief` (or equivalent) within the same session — not a "check your email Monday" placeholder.
2. The brief uses the baseline capture + any existing history for that domain (even if only the proof brief demo data), showing at least one evidence-linked item (screenshot, page text, source link).
3. The bulk competitor import (CSV/paste) is accessible directly from `/app/watchlists` (not only in onboarding checklist) — one click to "Import competitors".
4. A "Your first brief" email is dispatched within 60 minutes of signup (via Cloudflare Email Service), not gated on the weekly cron.
5. Funnel measurement (`FUNNEL_MEASUREMENT_ENABLED=1` in production) emits `signup`, `activation_scan_started`, `first_brief_rendered`, `first_brief_email_sent` events.
6. A regression test under `tests/activation/first-brief-same-session.test.tsx` runs a clean signup flow (test auth bypass), triggers activation scan for a seeded domain, and asserts (a) on-screen brief renders with ≥1 evidence item, (b) email dispatched within test time budget.

verify:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509
npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts --project=workspace tests/e2e/activation-first-brief.spec.ts
# Test: fresh signup → onboarding → activation scan → on-screen brief with evidence → email sent
```

rollback: Revert the activation scan trigger, on-screen brief route, bulk import placement, and immediate email dispatch. The weekly cron and existing onboarding checklist remain intact. No D1 schema changes (uses existing `watchlist`, `proof_capture`, `user` tables).

dedupe: Not a duplicate of #1445 (canary test only), #1266 (bulk import placement only), or #1278 (BET 10 claim reconciliation). This issue is the core activation flow implementation.

impact: 2 signups in 63 days, zero watchlists. The activation gap is the arithmetic reason for zero retention. A user who signs up and sees a real brief *now* has a reason to stay; a user who sees "check email Monday" bounces.

product_surface: `/app/onboarding` → on-screen brief + `/app/watchlists` (bulk import) + first-brief email (delivery)

termination: `npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts --project=workspace tests/e2e/activation-first-brief.spec.ts` exits 0, asserting on-screen brief with ≥1 evidence-linked item renders in the same session as signup and first-brief email is dispatched.

body:
difficulty: senior-review

~~blocked-on: Nishfleet/fleet-ops#4219~~
~~blocked-on: Nishfleet/fleet-ops#4404~~ (closed)

Unblocks when #4404 (402 cooldown + non-dead-end fallback) lands and a follow-up dual-run shows 0 credit-exhaustion dead-ends. #4219 (P3a) is closed. Scope from #4130: pick_seat collapses to group selection already done in P3a; this PR DELETES lib/pi-packet/seat-lib.sh, its tests, the seat ledgers/bench markers/prepaid-usage files, and the seat logic in pi-issue-run, agent-cron-run, pi-packet-run, pi-scout-run, pi-audit-run and the 10 other callers listed on #4130 (each becomes pi --print --provider litellm --model <group> or a LiteLLM /health,/spend,/model/info query). Net line count in the PR body (must be strongly negative). Vault ledger line. Proof: grep -rl seat-lib ~/.local/bin ~/.local/lib ~/.config/systemd/user returns nothing; 2h of merges through the proxy at or above the pre-cutover rate.

## Spec lines (added 2026-09-12 by the orchestrator so the spec gate admits this — fleet-ops#543)
Context: the first attempt, PR #4422 (+1228/−16567), was closed 2026-09-10 because `main` kept growing CI-pinned `pick_seat` callers while the PR sat conflicting for 3 days. Nish 2026-09-12: "nothing with duct tape" — the RAM admission cap was hand-tuned three times today (ram_gb_per_worker 1.0→0.6→0.5) because seat-lib's static governor is the only thing left deciding worker count; every such edit is tape on an organ this issue deletes. Land the deletion.

termination: `lib/seat-lib.sh` is gone from `main`; no file under bin/ or lib/ sources it or calls `pick_seat`/`ram_governor_cap`/`active_ram_charge`; worker admission is decided by systemd resources (MemoryMax, oomd) plus the LiteLLM proxy's group routing — no hand-set per-worker RAM charge remains in config.
accept: `git grep -lE 'seat-lib|pick_seat' -- bin lib tests` returns only the deletion test; `tests/` gains one test that asserts the file is absent and the callers are gone; one full intake tick on the host admits and starts a worker with the proxy route (journal shows `pi-intake@…: claimed+spawned` and no `seat-lib` log line).
required: freeze first — before the rebase, open a one-line PR that makes P14 fail on any NEW `pick_seat` caller (the reason #4422 died), so the deletion PR cannot be re-conflicted while it is open; the deletion PR itself is one PR, net strongly negative, with the same three conflict files resolved on the deletion side as in the #4589 rebase.
metric: `git grep -c pick_seat -- bin lib` on main — >40 call sites today, must be 0 after merge; hand edits to `ram_gb_per_worker` in config/seat-caps.json after merge — must be impossible because the key no longer exists.

title: seat: wire ElectronHub Turbo DevPass (deepseek-v4-flash-0731:dev FP8, glm-5.3:dev) as a prepaid seat, cap 5 — everything except the $40 payment
body:
Nish 2026-09-07 evaluated ElectronHub DevPass (docs: https://docs.electronhub.ai/billing/coding-plan.md). Turbo = $40/mo flat, unlimited tokens, 5 parallel requests, tool calling on /v1/chat/completions; included :dev models: deepseek-v4-flash-0731:dev (400K ctx, FP8+FP4 — PRIMARY), deepseek-v4-flash:dev (1M ctx, NVFP4 — audition only), glm-5.3:dev (262K, FP8 — capable), glm-5.3-flash:dev, minimax-m2.7:dev, mimo-v2.5:dev. Base URL https://api.electronhub.ai/v1, header Authorization: Bearer ek-dev-<key>. Terms: one seat per person; personal machines incl. CI count as that seat; no key sharing/pooling/resale. Soft daily+weekly headroom and a ~24h low-interactivity mode reduce concurrency under sustained load (429 with Retry-After, never a hard stop).

Do, in this order:
1. Create the ElectronHub account with Nish's usual signup path (account signups are pre-approved; NO payment). Store credentials in the usual VPS credential location; never in repo/vault.
2. Add provider 'electronhub' to ~/.pi/agent/models.json (openai-completions, baseUrl above, apiKey via the existing '!cmd' resolver pattern) with modelOverrides for the three models above (contextWindow/maxTokens/reasoning per the docs).
3. Add rows to config/entitled-seats.json (class prepaid) and config/seat-caps.json: electronhub cap=5 total; deepseek-v4-flash-0731:dev capable=1; glm-5.3:dev capable=1; deepseek-v4-flash:dev audition=true cap=1. Provider quota_bench_default_s tuned for the 429+Retry-After behaviour.
4. STOP before payment. Post the exact checkout URL for Turbo and the one-line smoke test (echo 'Reply with exactly: SEAT-OK' | pi --print --provider electronhub --model deepseek-v4-flash-0731:dev) in a comment. Nish pays; the next tick's seat-live-validate proves the seat and it joins rotation. Money is Nish-only.
5. After #4130 P3, this seat becomes a LiteLLM deployment in the worker-cheap and worker-capable groups (max_parallel_requests=5); note that in the PR.

title: fix(ads): /ads/notion.com and /ads/notion.so are duplicate indexable pages — extend the alias canonicalization table past ridge/oura
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1446 score=0.50 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1446 (score 0.50). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: exactly one of {/ads/notion.com, /ads/notion.so} is indexable (in sitemap, canonical-to-self, 200); the other 301-redirects to it. Today both are indexable and both serve the same 2 verified Notion ads.

observed: 2026-09-06, both URLs are in https://0509.io/sitemap.xml, both return HTTP 200, both carry <link rel="canonical"> pointing to themselves (not to each other), and both render "2 Meta ads linking to notion.{com,so} — 2 from Notion" with the same ad set (Juan Dussán with Notion, T-Pain with Notion). notion.so is Notion's real domain; notion.com is the natural alias a buyer types. Two self-canonical, indexable pages with identical ad content split the brand's verified ads and link equity and self-compete for the "Notion facebook ads" query in Google.

evidence:
- sitemap: `grep -c 'ads/notion.com' sitemap.xml` = 1; `grep -c 'ads/notion.so' sitemap.xml` = 1
- https://0509.io/ads/notion.com → HTTP 200, canonical = https://0509.io/ads/notion.com, "2 verified"
- https://0509.io/ads/notion.so → HTTP 200, canonical = https://0509.io/ads/notion.so, "2 verified"
- PR #1714 (claim/issue-1446) added BRAND_PAGE_CANONICAL_ALIASES for ridge.com→ridgewallet.com and oura.com→ouraring.com only; notion is not in the table. PR #1714 is currently failing CI on a brand-attribution integration test (oura brandOwnedAdCount expected 1, got 2), so the alias mechanism is still being landed.

accept:
- Add notion.com → notion.so (or whichever is the populated canonical) to the alias canonicalization table introduced by PR #1714, gated the same way: the alias 301-redirects to its canonical ONLY when the canonical page is actually populated; otherwise the alias renders normally and stays noindex via the existing anti-thin-content guard.
- Decide the canonical direction from data: whichever of notion.com / notion.so has the larger verified-ad set becomes the canonical; the other 301s to it. (Both currently show 2 — pick notion.so as the real-domain canonical and redirect notion.com to it, consistent with how the real web resolves notion.com → notion.so.)
- Remove the redirected alias from sitemap.xml; keep the canonical in sitemap.
- Add a regression test under tests/integration/** that asserts the alias 301-redirects to the populated canonical and that the canonical is the only one of the pair in the sitemap. Mirror the existing ridge/oura alias test shape.
- Re-fetch both URLs after the fix: the alias returns 301 to the canonical; the canonical is the only indexable URL of the pair.

verify:
```
curl -sI https://0509.io/ads/notion.com | grep -i '^location' | grep -q '/ads/notion.so'   # alias 301s to canonical
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c 'ads/notion.com'   # must be 0
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c 'ads/notion.so'    # must be 1
npm test -- --project workers tests/integration/ads-alias-canonical.integration.test.ts   # passes (new or extended)
```

rollback: remove the notion entry from the alias table; both pages render at 200 again. No schema change, no data migration — pure read-path redirect config.

dedupe: #1446 ("/ads/:domain alias brand pages are not redirected/canonicalized") is the umbrella issue and PR #1714 is its first PR, scoped to ridge.com→ridgewallet.com and oura.com→ouraring.com only (confirmed: #1446 body mentions ridge and oura, not notion; #1427 is oura-specific). This issue tracks the notion pair specifically so a worker can ship it as a discrete unit while #1714 lands the ridge/oura pair. If #1446 is preferred as the single tracker, close this as a duplicate and append the notion pair to #1446's acceptance instead.

impact: Two indexable, self-canonical pages with identical ad content is textbook duplicate content / keyword cannibalization — the exact self-competition #1446 was filed to stop, for a brand (Notion) that buyers will actually search for. Every additional un-aliased brand pair (notion is the visible one today; there may be more) dilutes the programmatic /ads/:domain distribution bet (BET 5) the same way.

product_surface: /ads/:domain (public, sitemap-indexed programmatic buyer surface)

source: scout walk of https://0509.io/sitemap.xml on 2026-09-06 (every sitemap URL fetched, status + canonical + verified-count recorded); transformation campaign BET 5 "Somebody has to see it" — "Add every compare page and every /ads/ page to the sitemap, with per-page structured data" (no self-cannibalization). Usage telemetry block was empty this run, so this candidate is walk-sourced per the scout NOTE.

termination: curl -sI https://0509.io/ads/notion.com | grep -i '^location' | grep -q '/ads/notion.so'

title: BET 10 sub: /trust page enumerates 'landing-page snapshots' as a stored data category while landing_page_snapshot has 0 rows in production
body:
metric: `curl -sS https://0509.io/trust` does NOT mention "landing-page snapshots" as a category of stored product data, OR `app/lib/landing-page-snapshot.server.ts` (or equivalent) writes a row to `landing_page_snapshot` for every fresh `proof_capture` of a watched `landing_page_*` event within 7 days of a starter/agency signup.

observed: 2026-08-31T08:00Z. The `/trust` page is the public trust surface. It enumerates what Five to Nine stores so a buyer can verify the data-handling claim. The current enumeration reads (verbatim, from the data-handled block):

> "Five to Nine stores account records, saved searches, watchlists, collections, notes, reports, share links, delivery settings, API keys, proof-backed changes, **landing-page snapshots**, source URLs, delivery attempts, and service logs needed to run the product."

"Blanding-page snapshots" is named as a stored data category. Per the live D1 inspection on 2026-08-25 (research §1.5c), `landing_page_snapshot` has **zero rows** in production — and `website_watch_target` is also zero — so the trust page advertises a stored data category that does not yet exist in the database a buyer is being told they can rely on. `docs/launch-readiness.md` records Gate A–C readiness as 0/6 for the timeline surface.

This is the same family of defect as #1265 ("Stop selling landing-page change history on /pricing") and #1278 (BET 10 umbrella), but on the **trust** surface. A buyer who reads /trust first — which is exactly what an enterprise security review does, often before /pricing — finds a data category the system does not actually store. Combined with #1265 the claim appears on three surfaces (`/pricing`, `/help`, `/docs`, `/competitor-monitoring`, `/ads/:domain`, `/trust` all share the pricing widget that contains "Landing-page change history as scheduled watches complete"), plus /trust's separate "landing-page snapshots" line. The /trust one is the most damaging because the trust page is also where the data-retention claim lives — "storing X" implies the system actually stores X.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/trust | grep -A 2 'landing-page snapshot'` (2026-08-31) → matches the line above
- D1 inspection 2026-08-25 (live): `landing_page_snapshot` row count = 0; `website_watch_target` row count = 0 (research §1.5c)
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/timeline/nike.com` → 404 (no public timeline surface)
- `app/lib/pricing.ts` `planMarketingFeatures` pushes "Landing-page change history with screenshots" on Starter/Agency — covered by #1265
- Source: research transformation campaign §1.5c ("`landing_page_snapshot` and `website_watch_target` are both empty (0 rows). Landing-page history — a named Starter/Agency feature — has no stored corpus in production."), §3.4 BET 10 ("Say only what is true… Either make each claim true or change the sentence"), §3.5 quick win #1 in BET 10 ("Either make each claim true (bets 1, 3, 4 do most of this) or change the sentence")

accept:
- Either path is acceptable, but **the trust-page line is what this issue closes**:
  - **Path A (preferred — matches #1265's spirit, faster):** change the data-handled enumeration in `/trust` so it does not list "landing-page snapshots" as a stored category. The honest replacement: drop the phrase, OR replace it with a hedged sentence ("Five to Nine stores account records, saved searches, watchlists, collections, notes, reports, share links, delivery settings, API keys, proof-backed changes, source URLs, delivery attempts, and service logs. Landing-page snapshots are kept only after a starter-or-above plan has run a successful landing-page watch for at least one domain — see `/timeline/:domain` for current coverage.") Only ship the hedged sentence when the timeline route is actually live; otherwise drop the phrase entirely.
  - **Path B (closes the BET 10 root cause):** wire `app/lib/landing-page-snapshot.server.ts` (or equivalent) so every `proof_capture` of a watched `landing_page_*` event produces a `landing_page_snapshot` row within 60 seconds, then make `/timeline/:domain` return 200 with at least one dated state for the demo brands (covered by #1449). Once that path is shipped, the trust-page claim becomes true and can stay.
- A lock test under `tests/trust-page-data-handled-claim.test.ts` that renders `/trust` and asserts one of:
  - the data-handled block does not contain "landing-page snapshots" as a stored category, OR
  - `landing_page_snapshot` row count ≥ 1 in the staging D1 bind (so the prod-staging parity is checked), AND `/timeline/:domain` returns 200 for at least one demo brand
- The `app/lib/trust.ts` (or equivalent) copy lives in one place — no surface-by-surface fix.
- No D1 schema change. No gate-owned CI path edit.

verify:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509
node --test tests/trust-page-data-handled-claim.test.ts
# live check
curl -sS https://0509.io/trust | grep -c 'landing-page snapshot'   # 0 (Path A) or staging check passes (Path B)
# staging D1 row count
curl -sS https://0509.io/timeline/nike.com | grep -c 'Page not found' # 0 (Path B only)
```

rollback: Revert the `/trust` data-handled enumeration and the test file. No D1 schema change.

dedupe: #1265 covers `/pricing`'s unqualified "Landing-page change history with screenshots" claim and has a similar lock test pattern. #1278 (BET 10 umbrella) covers the broader reconciliation including the funnel flag and GA copy. Neither names `/trust` as a distinct surface. #1449 (Backfill landing_page_snapshot for the 5 demo /ads/:domain brands) is the implementation track for Path B. #1240 / #1272 / #964 cover the timeline-route build and sitemap inclusion — Path B depends on those landing first.

impact: A buyer running a vendor-security review reads `/trust` first. The page enumerates stored data so the reviewer can map it to their own data-handling questionnaire. Naming "landing-page snapshots" as a stored category when the table is empty is a **trust-page contradiction at the highest-stakes surface in the funnel**. Combined with the same claim's presence in the pricing widget on `/pricing`, `/help`, `/docs`, `/competitor-monitoring`, `/ads/:domain`, and `/search`, the company is currently selling a feature on seven surfaces and storing the data on zero. The trust page is the one a buyer cites in a procurement doc; fixing `/trust` first and pairing it with `#1265` closes the worst half of the surface area.

product_surface: `/trust` public trust page (data-handled block). The fix is in the trust-page copy module; the lock test asserts the claim holds.

termination: `cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509 && node --test tests/trust-page-data-handled-claim.test.ts && curl -sS https://0509.io/trust | (grep -q 'landing-page snapshot' || ! grep -q 'landing-page snapshot') && echo ok` — exits 0 when the lock test passes AND the rendered `/trust` page either (a) does not contain "landing-page snapshot" as a stored-category phrase, or (b) Path B is live and the page text matches the live data state.

source: 2026-08-30 daily market signal §1.5c (`landing_page_snapshot` empty, `website_watch_target` empty) + §3.4 BET 10 ("Say only what is true") + §3.5 Q1 ("Every public sentence on `/`, `/pricing`, `/api/docs`, `/timeline/:domain`, and `/compare/*` maps to a live query or test that passes"). North-star rule (memory north-star-edge-ai-cannot-match): "be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI" — and a trust page that names a stored category the system doesn't store is worse than what the buyer's own AI would have written, because it would have said "we don't store this yet."

## Prior art
- What exists: this is a fix inside an existing 0509 surface (/trust page + app/lib/landing-page-snapshot.server.ts). No new tool, service, or pipeline is built; the change is copy/link/render logic in the route that already serves this page.
- What was tested: the `observed:` line above is the live reproduction; nothing new to evaluate before building.
- Why rejected: no alternative needed, the existing route is the only place this can live.

(Prior-art section added by the orchestrator, fable-fleet-check 2026-09-06, after the spec gate bounced a surface fix as a tool build.)

title: Do not convene a conference below quorum: seat preflight is a precondition, not a vote entry
body:
WHY: termination-cycle4 and termination-cycle6 both recorded seat-preflight refusals as vote entries (_seat_preflight for glm-5-2, glm-5-3, senior) and still produced verdicts; cycle6 additionally accepted a run with tools=0 class=no-tool. Root cause is open as #4296; credential-blocked seats are open as #4233. A verdict produced by fewer real judges than the panel claims launders blind seats into a result, and both other auditors cited this exact failure in their NOT-DONE votes.

CHANGE:
1. In the orchestrator that convenes research/termination conferences, run seat preflight BEFORE dispatch. Quorum = the configured panel size, distinct and healthy.
2. Below quorum: do not convene. Do not write to verdict_history. Print PACKET-VERDICT seat-preflight-failed with the refused seats and reason, exit non-zero, and file or annotate a repair issue linking #4296 and #4233.
3. Delete the code path that appends a _seat_preflight refusal as a round-1 or round-2 vote entry, and the code path that accepts tools=0 class=no-tool as a judge output.
4. Reuse the existing seat-health source that pick_seat already uses. If seat-lib is deleted first (#4263, #4264), implement quorum inside its replacement.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Fixture forcing one unhealthy seat: no conference row, no verdict_history entry, repair issue filed, non-zero exit.
- Fixture with three healthy distinct seats: conference proceeds with exactly three round-1 entries.
- Fixture with a tool-less run: rejected, not scored.

ROLLBACK: revert.
OUT OF SCOPE: no new health checker, no new timer. Do not repair #4233 credentials in this PR.

comments.body:

decision-resolved: close as subsumed by #4296 (duplicate research-delta filing; dedupe #6496, #5734 precedent: close the newer). Do not re-label agent-ready (fleet-ops#5723).

title: fix(ci): gitleaks false positive on salvage commit 1f285a08 blocks all PRs — add .gitleaksignore entry (needs admin attestation)
body:
metric: every open PR's required Gitleaks check passes.

observed: 2026-09-06, the required Secret Scan (Gitleaks) check fails on every open PR (#1786, #1760, ...) with a `stripe-access-token` finding in commit `1f285a08bba6194b26325946a14a6beef4d81a02` on branch `wip/pi-issue-0509-1752-20260906T115133Z`. The `gitleaks git .` scan walks all refs in the fetch-depth:0 checkout, so a false positive on ANY branch fails the check for EVERY PR.

evidence:
- Gitleaks finding: `1f285a08:tests/release-hydration-bridge.test.ts:stripe-access-token:89`
- The offending line is a test fixture simulating a hydration error message: `Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match token=sk_live_abc123def456` — a hardcoded, obviously-fake dummy value. The test asserts the redaction logic strips it (`expect(detail.message).not.toContain("sk_live_")`). It is not a credential.
- The salvage commit is on a WIP branch for unit pi-issue-0509-1752 (issue #1752 still open, agent-in-progress). It is not on main and not in main's history.
- Main's Secret Scan passes (push events scan only main's history).

accept:
- Add the fingerprint `1f285a08bba6194b26325946a14a6beef4d81a02:tests/release-hydration-bridge.test.ts:stripe-access-token:89` to `.gitleaksignore` with a justifying comment (following the existing pattern from commit b157f14f).
- The gate-integrity check flags `.gitleaksignore` as a gate-owned path, requiring a repository admin to post `gate-integrity-attest: <40-hex head sha>` on the PR, then re-run the check. This is Nish-reserved (the worker app has no admin permission and the worker rules forbid posting attestation comments).
- After the attestation, confirm the Gitleaks check passes on at least one previously-blocked PR.

verify:
```
gh pr view <PR> -R Nishfleet/0509 --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.name=="Gitleaks") | .conclusion'   # must be SUCCESS
gh pr view <PR> -R Nishfleet/0509 --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.name=="gate-integrity") | .conclusion'   # must be SUCCESS
```

rollback: revert the `.gitleaksignore` entry; Gitleaks resumes failing on all PRs.

dedupe: none. #1729 is the timeline brand-attribution fix whose PR (#1786) carries the `.gitleaksignore` entry to unblock itself; this issue tracks the repo-wide CI blocker independently so it survives even if #1786 is closed.

impact: every open PR is currently unmergeable because of this false positive. No product work can land until it is resolved.

product_surface: CI / Secret Scan (infrastructure, not customer-facing)

source: investigation during pi-issue-0509-1729 (PR #1786 gate-integrity failure)

termination: gh pr view 1786 -R Nishfleet/0509 --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup[] | select(.name=="Gitleaks") | .conclusion' | grep -q SUCCESS

title: SLO snapshot must fail closed when repair or starvation is unmeasured
body:
Goal: fleet-gap-closure-slo must not report green:true when time_to_repair_per_class is empty or queue_starvation_minutes is null. A green snapshot over missing data is how cycle-5 shows slos_green=true while pct_auto_repaired=0, time_to_repair={}, and starvation=null.

They: DORA gates on failed-deployment recovery time and change-fail rate being measured, not on merge_count. Google error-budget policy only freezes once remaining budget is a real number over a four-week window.

We: bin/fleet-gap-closure-slo hardcodes time_to_repair_per_class:{}. queue_starvation_minutes is null when ~/.local/state/fleet-heartbeat/queue-starvation.json is missing. green is true iff detector_drill_pass_rate>=1 and quality cycle_verdict is not FAIL. merge_count=100 cannot flip FAIL. Cycle-5 snapshot is green on stub drills (unit-failure-escalation, timer-mask-detection, failed-units-signal) while repair and starvation are unmeasured.

Change, existing rails only:
1. Fill time_to_repair_per_class from unit-escalation / failed-reaper timestamps already on disk (journal or gap-closure failed-units). If the map is empty after that read, green=false.
2. If queue_starvation_minutes is null, green=false. If the starvation JSON is missing, write it from time-since-last-successful-claim per enrolled repo (heartbeat already has the claim clock). Do not add a timer.
3. Do not add fleet_dora_fdrt_seconds or fleet_dora_cfr gauges. Do not freeze auto-merge in this issue. HALT (stop-the-line-detector) stays the freeze until remaining budget is a real number.
4. pct_auto_repaired=0 with closed>0 is a measured zero, not missing; do not fail closed on that field.

Out of scope: error-budget merge freeze (rejected this cycle as premature). New Prometheus metrics. Killing live LiteLLM or Postgres.

Tests: add cases next to the existing slo snapshot test. Missing starve file => green=false. Empty repair map => green=false. Both populated and drills=1 and quality not FAIL => green=true.

Proof: bash the slo / gap-closure tests green. Re-run fleet-gap-closure-slo against current state.json and show green=false while starvation is null or repair is {}.

Citation: https://dora.dev/guides/dora-metrics/

pid 3661244  timeout --kill-after=30s 2520s pi --print --provider litellm --model worker-cheap

title: Landing-page CTA-change detector has produced 4 events in 4 months — instrument extraction pipeline to find the bail-out point (BET 1)
body:

Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#972 (score 0.45). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: ≥1 landing_page_cta_changed event captured per week on a fixed 20-competitor live cohort over 72h, with instrumentation showing ≥80% of watchlist runs reach the CTA-extraction stage (not bailing out earlier in the pipeline).

observed: research context §1.5 (2026-08-25 ground truth): "landing_page_cta_changed: 4 events, 0.4% share, most recent 2026-06-15". Across 88 watchlists, in four months, the CTA-change detector has fired 4 times — and zero times since 15 June 2026.

evidence:
- research context §1.5: full watch_event distribution; CTA-change silence since 15 June 2026
- research context §3.4 BET 1 (page 1): "find out why the landing-page detectors are near-silent: 4 CTA-change events in 4 months across 88 watchlists is a detector bug, not a quiet market — instrument how many checks reach the extraction stage vs. bail out, and fix the bail-outs"
- the live /capture-rules page names what should NOT bail out: error pages, challenge pages, cookie walls, partial loads, timestamp-only edits, rotating banners, scheduled maintenance. None of those should silently drop a real CTA change.
- BET 1 acceptance: ≥60% of brief headline items are landing_page_* events (today: 4.6%); cannot be measured as true while the CTA detector is silent.

accept:
1. The CTA extraction pipeline emits an instrumentation event per stage (page-fetch, validity-gate, DOM-extract, change-diff) for every landing-page check. Each stage records an incrementing counter and the reason for any bail-out.
2. A new queryable counter table or log exposes per-stage counts per day: checks_started, page_fetch_succeeded, validity_passed, dom_extracted, diff_computed, event_emitted. The counter is queryable in D1 (or as an /api/v1 endpoint for the fleet).
3. On a fixed 20-competitor live cohort run for 72h, at least 80% of checks reach the dom_extracted stage. The current behaviour is unknown because there is no counter — this number is the baseline.
4. A regression test in tests/integration/cta-pipeline-instrumentation.test.ts (or .sh) asserts the counter increments at each stage and that a real CTA change (synthetic fixture) emits exactly one landing_page_cta_changed event.

# Pass: rows for all 6 stages; checks_started > 0; event_emitted > 0; the ratio event_emitted/checks_started is reported.
```

rollback: revert the PR and drop the new counter table. The instrumentation is additive; removing it reverts to silent.

dedupe: sub-issue of BET 1 (#1483) — focused on the instrumentation step the BET 1 acceptance requires. Not a duplicate: #1483 is the broader digest re-ranking; this issue is the instrumented pipeline needed to know whether the BET 1 acceptance is achievable at all.

impact: 95.4% of all shipped watch events today are `ad_new` / `ad_inactive`. The whole landing-page differentiator the homepage, the deck, the meta description, and every compare page rest on is firing 4 times in 4 months for the CTA surface — the silent detector is the single largest gap between the product's promise and its behaviour. Without instrumentation, every BET 1 fix is blind to whether it moved the metric.

product_surface: landing-page CTA-change detection (the headline differentiator per research §1.1 and §1.7)

# Pass: rows for all 6 stages; checks_started > 0; event_emitted > 0; the ratio event_emitted/checks_started is reported.
```
Exit 0 means: the test passes, the counter table exists, and 72h of live cohort data shows non-zero counts at every stage.

title: /ads/notion.so is noindex and missing from sitemap despite verified Notion ads
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1427 score=0.57 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1427 (score 0.57). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: `/ads/notion.so` is indexable, listed in `sitemap.xml`, and reachable from `/search?q=notion` as a brand destination.

observed: 2026-08-29T00:15Z UTC. `/ads/notion.so` returns a real brand page with 2 verified Notion ads, but it carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex"/>` and is absent from `https://0509.io/sitemap.xml`. The free search preview for `notion` works, yet the result rows do not link to the brand page, so the programmatic SEO surface for Notion is invisible to Google and hard to reach from the first-value moment.

evidence:
- `curl -sS -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://0509.io/ads/notion.so | grep -oE '<meta[^>]+name="robots"[^>]*>'` returns `<meta name="robots" content="noindex"/>`.
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/notion.so | grep -oE 'See [0-9]+ Meta ads linking to notion.so'` returns "See 2 Meta ads linking to notion.so — 2 from Notion".
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -q 'ads/notion.so'` returns no match.
- `curl -sS 'https://0509.io/search?q=notion&country=all' | grep -o 'href="/ads/notion.so"'` returns no match.

accept:
1. Remove the `noindex` meta tag from `/ads/notion.so` so it matches other populated `/ads/:domain` pages (e.g. `/ads/nike.com`, `/ads/allbirds.com`).
2. Add `https://0509.io/ads/notion.so` to the dynamic sitemap at `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts`.
3. Add a "View brand page" link (or make the advertiser name link to `/ads/notion.so`) from the Notion search result rows once the page is indexable.
4. Add a regression test that asserts any `/ads/:domain` page with `verifiedLinkCount > 0` is indexable and in the sitemap; no D1 schema change needed.

verify:
```bash
# After fix, the brand page has no noindex meta and is in the sitemap.
curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/notion.so | grep -q 'noindex' && echo "FAIL: still noindex" || echo "ok"
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep 'ads/notion.so' || echo "FAIL: not in sitemap"
```

rollback: Re-add the noindex meta tag, remove the sitemap entry, and revert the search link.

dedupe: #1427 covers the oura.com / ouraring.com alias gap; the root cause is different (Notion has one canonical `notion.so` domain and verified ads). #1269 / #1396 cover slack.com / tcs.com 0-result dead-ends. #973 is the BET 2 25-domain verification script. none of the open issues cover `/ads/notion.so` being noindex and missing from the sitemap.

impact: A buyer searching "Notion facebook ads" sees 11 results on `/search` but cannot land on an indexable, sitemap-backed `/ads/notion.so` page. The search preview gives value, but the programmatic SEO/brand destination is invisible. This wastes the BET 5 distribution engine on a brand that already has verified ads.

product_surface: `/ads/:domain` programmatic SEO brand pages and the `/search` first-value preview.

termination: `bash -c 'curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/notion.so | grep -q "noindex" && exit 1; curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -q "ads/notion.so" || exit 1; exit 0'`

source: BET 2 §1.8 (allbirds / notion / oura dead-ends) + BET 5 ("scale /ads/:domain into the natural landing page for '<brand> facebook ads' queries, gated so no page ships empty") + 2026-08-29 live curl of `/ads/notion.so`, `sitemap.xml`, and `/search?q=notion`.

title: Duplicate /compare/* URL pairs (visualping / visualping-ad-library, foreplay / foreplay-spyder) ship in sitemap with no canonical disambiguation
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1463 score=0.49 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1463 (score 0.49). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: Every `/compare/<vendor>` URL in `https://0509.io/sitemap.xml` either (a) has a unique intent covered by no other `/compare/*` URL and no self-referential `rel=canonical` to a sibling, OR (b) 301s/canonicalizes to a single canonical sibling.

observed: 2026-08-31 against production. Two pairs of `/compare/*` URLs ship in the sitemap at identical priority (0.7) with no canonical disambiguation between siblings — a textbook duplicate-content SEO defect:

- `/compare/visualping` (title: "Five to Nine vs Visualping"; meta desc: "Visualping monitors public pages for visual, text, and element changes...") AND `/compare/visualping-ad-library` (title: "Five to Nine vs Visualping for ad libraries"; meta desc: "Visualping can watch a Meta Ad Library URL on a free plan..."). Both carry their own `<link rel="canonical">` pointing at themselves, neither references the other, both appear in the sitemap. Body text diverges at character 25 and only on the H1; the actual comparison content is largely the same Visualping-vs-0509 narrative.
- `/compare/foreplay` (title: "Five to Nine vs Foreplay") AND `/compare/foreplay-spyder` (title: "Five to Nine vs Foreplay Spyder") — same pattern: distinct H1, near-identical body text, both in the sitemap at priority 0.7, no canonical between them.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/compare/visualping | grep -oE '<link rel="canonical"[^>]+>'` → `href="https://0509.io/compare/visualping"`
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/compare/visualping-ad-library | grep -oE '<link rel="canonical"[^>]+>'` → `href="https://0509.io/compare/visualping-ad-library"`
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -E 'compare/(visualping|foreplay)'` returns both URLs per pair.
- Byte-length delta per pair: visualping 25,416 vs visualping-ad-library 24,634 (~3%); foreplay vs foreplay-spyder ~2%.
- `<title>` and meta description differ on framing only; comparison copy targets the same buyer intent ("Visualping vs 0509"). Google can interpret these as duplicate SERP targets and split link equity.

accept:
- For each pair, decide which URL is the canonical target (the more specific one — `visualping-ad-library` and `foreplay-spyder` — names the narrower intent and should win), and either:
  - 301 redirect the loser to the winner, OR
  - Add `<link rel="canonical" href="<winner>">` on the loser and remove the loser from `sitemap.xml`.
- The winner stays in the sitemap with its real value-proposition headline (no `all-countries query` jargon — see #1464) and is reachable from `/compare` and from the nav.
- The loser returns HTTP 200 with the canonical pointing at the winner (or 301s to it) — never 404.
- A regression test under `tests/seo/**` parses the sitemap, asserts each `/compare/*` URL has a unique or canonicalised-to sibling, and checks both pair losers carry the right canonical.

verify:
```
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE '<loc>[^<]+compare[^<]+</loc>' | sort -u
# expect: only one of {visualping, visualping-ad-library} and only one of {foreplay, foreplay-spyder}
curl -sS https://0509.io/compare/visualping-ad-library 2>&1 | grep -oE '<link rel="canonical"[^>]+>'   # if loser still exists, it must point at the winner
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://0509.io/compare/visualping
# either 301 to /compare/visualping-ad-library, or 200 with canonical pointing there — never 404
```

rollback: remove the canonical/redirect; restore both URLs in the sitemap. No data loss; both URLs were near-duplicates with no per-URL analytics binding.

dedupe: None of the open `/compare/*` issues (#1411, #1456, #1463, #1466, #1288, #1417, #1418) cover duplicate-URL-within-sitemap. #1411 covers missing first-party citations on spyland/pulzifi; #1456 covers missing FAQPage JSON-LD on `/switch/*`; #1417 covers orphan /ads/* pages.

impact: Two competing URLs in the sitemap at the same priority splits Google PageRank and can knock both below the "Visualping alternative" / "Foreplay alternative" SERPs that BET 5 names as the goal for distribution. Buyers searching "Foreplay alternative" or "Visualping alternative" already hit a competitor's content page; a duplicate internal pair makes 0509's own compare pages rank worse than they should, on top of everything else in the category (§2 of research context).

product_surface: /compare/<vendor> (SEO landing pages — distribution surface)

source: BET 5 ("scale /ads/:domain into a real programmatic SEO surface… sitemap ≥1,000 URLs, all returning 200 with non-empty content; each queued listing submission has a receipt") + north-star rule ("be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI — through verified evidence and finished hands-free outcomes" — competing with ourselves for SERP placement is not better, it's worse).

termination: `bash -c 'set -e; cd ~/workspaces/products/0509; npx vitest run tests/seo/compare-canonical.test.ts' ; curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE 'compare/(visualping|foreplay)' | sort -u | wc -l` — exit 0 AND count == 2 (one of each pair).

title: fix(quality-gate): mechanical senior conference enforcement for large diffs
body:
## Spec

**Problem**: 0509#1712 (721 additions across 10 files) merged without senior conference verdict, violating ledger 2026-08-26 "serious builds get the senior conference" — multi-hour/large diff requires panel audit before merge.

**Mechanism**: Add a required CI check that blocks merge on PRs exceeding size threshold (lines changed >500 OR files touched >10 OR touches critical paths: deploy, migrations, security, branch-protection) unless they carry the `conference-approved` label.

**Deterministic-required**: Yes (CI gate + label check)
**AI-advisory**: No

**Termination command**: 
```bash
# Verify the gate works
gh pr create --title "test large diff" --body "large diff test" --base main --head test-branch
gh pr edit <PR> --add-label conference-approved  # should unblock
gh pr edit <PR> --remove-label conference-approved  # should block
```

**Evidence**: 0509#1712 merged 2026-09-05 with 721 additions, CI checklist unchecked, no conference verdict referenced. Ledger 2026-08-26: "serious builds get the senior conference... mechanically, automatically, for every build that trips the seriousness gate."

**Role-gate catalog hit**: senior-conference-gate (new), ci-quality-gate (existing)

title: /ads/:domain pages lack breadcrumb navigation + BreadcrumbList structured data
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1417 score=0.63 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1417 (score 0.63). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

source: Transformation campaign state PART 3 §3.4 BET 5 ("Add per-page structured data" to every /ads/ page) + §2.5 capability table (the /ads surface is the programmatic SEO play). North-star rule: the /ads page is the natural landing page for "<brand> facebook ads" queries — breadcrumbs help Google understand site hierarchy and can show in search results.

metric: Every sitemap /ads/:domain page has visible breadcrumb navigation (Home > Ads > <brand>) and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD structured data.

observed: 2026-08-28, live production. The /ads pages have WebPage + Service + Organization + WebSite structured data, but no BreadcrumbList. There is no visible breadcrumb navigation on the page — a user who lands on /ads/nike.com from Google has no way to navigate "up" to a brand browse page or understand where they are in the site hierarchy.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -oE '"@type":"BreadcrumbList"'` → empty (no BreadcrumbList)
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -oiE 'breadcrumb|crumb'` → empty (no visible breadcrumb)
- Structured data types present: WebPage, Service, Organization, WebSite — no BreadcrumbList
- No BreadcrumbList anywhere in the codebase: `grep -rn 'BreadcrumbList' app/` → empty

accept:
- Add a visible breadcrumb element to the /ads/:domain page (e.g., "Five to Nine > Ads > Nike")
- Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD structured data matching the visible breadcrumb, with itemListElement entries for Home, /ads (or /brands hub), and the current brand page
- Add a test that asserts the BreadcrumbList structured data is present on /ads/:domain pages
- If a /brands hub page is created (see #1417), the breadcrumb should link to it; otherwise link to /search as the parent

verify:
```
curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -oE '"@type":"BreadcrumbList"' | wc -l
curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -oiE 'breadcrumb' | wc -l
```

rollback: Remove the breadcrumb component and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD from the /ads route. No data migration involved.

dedupe: none. #1417 covers internal linking between /ads pages (horizontal); this covers breadcrumb hierarchy (vertical). #966 is about page scale-out, not structured data on existing pages.

impact: Breadcrumbs in search results improve click-through rate and help Google understand the site hierarchy. For a programmatic SEO surface targeting "<brand> facebook ads" queries, breadcrumb rich results make the listing more prominent and clickable. This is a cheap, mechanical SEO win for a product with 0 search presence.

product_surface: /ads/:domain brand pages (programmatic SEO surface)

termination: curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -q '"@type":"BreadcrumbList"'

title: linkedin ads presence source: LinkedIn Ad Library snapshots per tracked competitor via Decodo universal target (standard pool, no JS), diff + alert on the Meta path
body:
Filed by Fable (2026-09-09, Nish: "add tiktok and linkedin?"). Scope is exactly the numbered steps below - no judgment calls; if a step cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

**Why:** LinkedIn is a must-not-claim today (#2141) and the existing "linkedin" presence source has no ad data. The LinkedIn Ad Library is public but returns 403 to datacenter IPs. Verified live by Fable through Decodo's universal target with NO JavaScript rendering: HTTP 200 in ~4.7s, 24 ads per page, pagination works.

**Verified requests (reproduce first; save responses as fixtures):**
- `POST https://scraper-api.decodo.com/v2/scrape`, `Authorization: Basic $DECODO_SCRAPER_AUTH` (same secret as #2181), body `{"target":"universal","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/search?accountOwner=Notion","geo":"United States","proxy_pool":"standard"}` -> upstream 200, 24 ads, all by advertiser "Notion".
- Page 2: same with `&start=25` -> 24 different ads. Page size is 25.
- Keyword variant `?keyword=<term>` also works but matches ad text, not the advertiser - do not use it for competitor tracking.
- Detail: `https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/<id>` -> 200, exposes "Advertiser <name>" and "Paid for by <entity>" plus the creative; ad ids come from `ad-library/detail/(\d+)` links on the search page. EU impressions/targeting appear only for EU-shown ads.
- ALWAYS send `"proxy_pool":"standard"` - Decodo defaults to premium, which halves the free plan (2,000 standard vs 1,000 premium requests per month). JS rendering (`headless`) is unnecessary and costs more; do not use it.

files: app/lib/sources/linkedin-ads.server.ts (replace the stub), app/components/sources/linkedin-ads.tsx (replace the stub), tests/sources/linkedin-ads*.test.ts, tests/fixtures/linkedin-ad-library/**

do:
1. linkedin-ad-library.server.ts: fetchAdsByAccountOwner(name, { maxAds: 25 }) -> page 1 only (start=0; the newest page suffices for change detection, same argument as #2194). Page size is 25 (the start param); a full page returned 24 cards in verification - do not assert a fixed card count, one Decodo request per page, ONE attempt per page, 60s timeout; parse each ad card: ad id, advertiser name, promoted text (first ~200 chars), creative image url if present, detail url. Return normalized list or { unavailable: true, reason } on Decodo status 613 / non-200 / zero cards with no "Promoted" text (treat as parse break, not "no ads"). Do NOT fetch detail pages in this issue (N+1 budget); record the detail url only.
2. Account owner = the tracked competitor's display name; if the search returns ads whose advertiser name does not case-insensitively equal the name, keep only exact matches and record `ambiguous: true` when non-matches were dropped.
3. linkedin-ads-snapshot.server.ts: weekly gate on the existing cadence (same 7-day gate plumbing as #2194), snapshot the ad list. Diff: new ad ids; ad ids gone (removed from the library); copy changes on same id. Emit through the Meta alert path tagged source "linkedin". Unavailable never blocks the Meta check. Call the decodo-budget helper from the seam #2218 (app/lib/decodo-budget.server.ts) BEFORE every request; on deny record { unavailable: true, reason: 'quota' }. Budget math after this edit: 50 competitors x 1 page x 4.33 weeks = ~217/month; with #2181's ~1,500 = ~1,717 < 1,800.
4. Competitor page: render latest snapshot inside the existing presence-source section (advertiser, total ads, new since last check, up to 12 creative previews, links to the public detail pages).
5. Claim table: LinkedIn Ad Library row, status live only when the Decodo secret is set in production.
6. Tests: fixtures for page 1 + page 2 of one advertiser, an advertiser with zero ads, a 613 failure, the exact-name filter, the diff cases.

must-not: use `headless`/JS rendering or the premium pool; hit linkedin.com directly from the Worker (403); fetch detail pages per ad; add a schedule of its own; retry inside the app; fork the Meta helpers; claim impressions or spend (EU-only, partial); add TikTok scope.

termination: npx vitest run tests/linkedin-ad-library.server.test.ts tests/linkedin-ads-snapshot.server.test.ts && npm run typecheck

accept: in production, one tracked competitor shows its LinkedIn ads on its page and the second check produces a diff entry tagged source "linkedin" (or a clean no-change record).

metric: tracked competitors with a LinkedIn ads snapshot

depends-on: #2218 (sources seam) merged. Parallel with every other source ticket; no shared files. Budget helper = app/lib/decodo-budget.server.ts from the seam (consumer only).

owner-decision: no

**Ownership (binding, Fable 2026-09-10 01:15 IST):** this ticket edits ONLY the files listed on its `files:` line. Every shared file (presence-types.ts, presence-source-coverage.server.ts, env.server.ts, the claim table source rows, the competitor page, the registry, migrations, decodo-budget.server.ts) belongs to #2218 (sources seam). Register nothing by hand: the seam already wired the stub at your path; replace the stub's contents. If you need a file outside your line, STOP and comment - never edit it. Full map in #2218.

## Judge edits, batch 2 (Kimi K3 Max, binding, applied by Fable 2026-09-10 08:40 IST)
Apply each bullet as written; where it quotes a sentence, that sentence is replaced.
