title: Homepage 'Signal, not noise' section mocks 'new ad' pings while 95.4% of shipped events are exactly that
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1363 score=0.52 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1363 (score 0.52). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

source: Transformation campaign state PART 1 §1.5a ("95.4% of everything the product has ever told a user is a 'new ad' or 'ad inactive' ping — precisely the output the homepage mocks competitors for ('Ad-spy tools drown teams in new ad pings')") + PART 3 §3.4 BET 1 ("The brief only contains changes") + BET 10 ("Say only what is true"). North-star rule: be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI — and a product that mocks a behavior it itself exhibits is worse than silent.

metric: The homepage "Signal, not noise" section (app/routes/marketing.tsx, id="signal") no longer claims "Five to Nine alerts you when something actually moved" as a present-tense fact while the product emits 95.4% ad-new/ad-inactive pings. Either the copy is hedged to acknowledge the current state, or BET 1 (#972) has landed and the claim is true.

observed: 2026-08-28, live production + campaign doc §1.5a event distribution. The homepage renders:

"Ad-spy tools drown teams in 'new ad' pings. Five to Nine alerts you when something actually moved — and tells you what it checked when nothing did."

The all-time watch_event distribution (campaign doc §1.5a, queried from production D1 2026-08-25):
- ad_new: 794 (76.0%)
- ad_inactive: 203 (19.4%)
- landing_page_form_changed: 21 (2.0%)
- landing_page_offer_changed: 11 (1.1%)
- landing_page_headline_changed: 8 (0.8%)
- landing_page_cta_changed: 4 (0.4%) — silent since 2026-06-15
- landing_page_url_changed: 4 (0.4%)

95.4% of everything the product has ever told a user is the "new ad" / "ad inactive" ping the homepage mocks competitors for. The three sub-points (baseline-first, 48h suppression, all-quiet heartbeat) are all true and shipped; the headline claim is not.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ | grep -o 'alerts you when something actually moved'` — returns the claim, live 2026-08-28
- `app/routes/marketing.tsx:827` — "Ad-spy tools drown teams in "new ad" pings. Five to Nine alerts you when something actually moved — and tells you what it checked when nothing did."
- Campaign doc §1.5a: all-time watch_event distribution, 95.4% ad_new + ad_inactive
- #972 (BET 1 verification): the fix that would make this claim true — not yet landed

accept:
- The "Signal, not noise" lede in `app/routes/marketing.tsx` (line 827) is rewritten so it does not claim, in present tense, that Five Nine filters out ad pings today. Two acceptable forms:
  (a) Hedged: acknowledge the current state honestly — e.g., "Ad-spy tools drown teams in 'new ad' pings. Five to Nine's brief leads with offer, price, and CTA moves — and tells you what it checked when nothing did. Creative churn is a footnote, not the headline." — only if BET 1 (#972) has landed and the termination check passes.
  (b) If BET 1 has NOT landed: remove the contrast with "Ad-spy tools" and state what IS true today — the baseline-first, 48h suppression, and all-quiet heartbeat — without claiming ad pings are filtered.
- The three sub-points (baseline-first, one-change-one-alert, silence-you-can-trust) stay — they are true and shipped.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass.

verify:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509
# the old unconditional claim must be gone:
rg -n 'alerts you when something actually moved' app/routes/marketing.tsx
# must return 0 matches after the fix
npm run typecheck && npm test
```

rollback: Revert the lede edit in `app/routes/marketing.tsx`. No schema, no D1, no bindings — pure copy edit.

dedupe: #1278 (BET 10) is the claim-reconciliation umbrella whose audit table would eventually catch this row. #972 (BET 1) is the fix that would make the claim true. Neither is a specific copy fix for this section — #1278 is an audit-table + funnel-flag + missing-ledger PR, and #972 is a digest re-ranking verification. This issue is the specific two-line copy hedge on the homepage's most prominent differentiator claim, fileable and verifiable independently of both.

impact: The "Signal, not noise" section is the homepage's core differentiator claim — the one sentence that tells a buyer why this product is not an ad-spy tool. A buyer who reads it, signs up, and receives a digest of 95% "new ad" pings sees the product mocking itself. This is the highest-trust-cost claim/reality gap on the site.

product_surface: / (homepage, "Signal, not noise" section, id="signal")

termination: `test "$(rg -c 'alerts you when something actually moved' app/routes/marketing.tsx || echo 0)" -eq 0` — the old unconditional claim is gone from the homepage source.

title: Workspace memory activation — collections, boards, notes, tags, external evidence links
body:

metric: A free/Scout tier user can create ≥1 collection, add ≥1 saved query, add ≥1 note, add ≥1 tag, and add ≥1 manual external evidence link (TikTok/YouTube/LinkedIn/Pinterest) in a single session; `collection` table row count >0 from non-Nish accounts

observed: 2026-09-02. Research §1.5d: "Workspace memory is unused: 0 collections, 1 saved query, 0 API keys, 2 share links. The 'compounding layer' compounds nothing yet." Research §1.2 lists the workspace features: collections/boards, notes, tags, manual external evidence links (TikTok/YouTube/LinkedIn/Pinterest — storage only, no automated ingestion), agent memory, client rooms, share links + PDF, team seats, agency report branding, support cases. All are built but the UI/onboarding doesn't surface them. The free plan includes "1 Collection" and "Saved competitor research" but users never reach them.

evidence:
- Research §1.5d: "Workspace memory is unused: 0 collections, 1 saved query, 0 API keys, 2 share links. The 'compounding layer' compounds nothing yet."
- Research §1.2: Full workspace feature list (collections, boards, notes, tags, external evidence links, agent memory, client rooms, share links, PDF, team seats, agency branding, support cases)
- Research §1.3: Free plan includes "1 Collection" and "Saved competitor research"
- Research §3.4 BET 7: "Surface the bulk competitor import (already built at app/lib/competitor-import.ts, currently buried in the onboarding checklist) on /app/watchlists too"
- `collection` table: 0 rows in production (Research §1.5d)

accept:
1. Add a "Workspace" or "Collections" tab/section in `/app` navigation (visible on Free+ tiers)
2. Create collection CRUD UI: create, rename, delete, add/remove saved searches, add/remove notes, add/remove tags
3. Surface "Add note" on watchlist items and search results
4. Surface "Add tag" on watchlist items and collections
5. Surface "Add external evidence link" (TikTok/YouTube/LinkedIn/Pinterest URL input with validation) on watchlist items and collections
6. Ensure all workspace features work on Free tier (1 collection limit enforced, but functional)

# Check workspace nav item exists

# Verify collection creation works (requires auth - manual check)
# Verify database has collection rows after test

rollback: Hide workspace nav item; keep collections/notes/tags tables (data preserved)

dedupe: Nishfleet/0509#1266 covers bulk competitor import on /app/watchlists. Nishfleet/0509#1487/#1445 cover BET 7 first brief. This issue is the workspace memory layer (collections, notes, tags, external links) activation.

impact: The "compounding layer" is the retention moat — users who build collections, notes, and external evidence links don't churn. 0 collections in 4 months means this moat is dead. Activating it turns single-session users into compounding-workspace users.

product_surface: /app/workspace, /app/collections, /app/watchlists (note/tag/actions), onboarding completion

termination: curl -sf https://0509.io/app/collections | grep -q "collection\|Collection" && curl -sf https://0509.io/app | grep -qi "workspace\|collections\|boards"

title: Withdrawn scout proposal #3532: stale evidence or duplicate scope; do not implement
body:
WITHDRAWN FROM SCOUT INTAKE. Filed before full-body dedupe. The three-tier model already exists according to #3331 and #2075; #3109 owns the empty-state issue. The August snapshot does not prove a current regression. The proposed search-recall-probe.mjs was not verified to exist. Do not implement this ticket or admit it to workers. The original broad defect claim is retracted.

The original unverified proposal follows for audit only. Its acceptance criteria are NOT authorized work.

---

<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#3109 score=0.58 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#3109 (score 0.58). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: a first-time visitor searching any well-known advertiser domain sees ad results (labelled by confidence) — 0 dead-end empty states over a 25-domain probe

observed: 2026-08-25 live product test (headless Chromium, production) — allbirds.com (~20s, 0 verified of 17 candidates), notion.so (24.7s, 0 of 11), oura.com (23.8s, 0 of 24) all rendered "No verified ads found" empty states. 3 of 6 recognisable brands dead-end the only first-value moment in the funnel, after a 16–25s opaque spinner. Search v2's verified-domain post-filter fixed the okara.ai precision bug by destroying recall.

evidence:
- RESEARCH CONTEXT market signal 2026-09-17, §1.8 live product test table
- BET 2 "The preview never dead-ends" (roadmap rank 2)
- related but distinct: #3331 (keyword-only likely intent), #2075 (ridge aliases), #3288 (cold latency), PR #3466 (streaming shell)

accept:
- three-tier result model: verified (as today) / likely (brand-name match with a visible confidence label + one-click "yes, that's them") / unmatched — never render an empty page when candidates exist; show them labelled
- keep the okara.ai precision fix: unmatched rows must never silently render as the competitor's ads
- streaming/progressive first card may be delegated to PR #3466 — this issue owns the recall tiers only
- a live probe script over ≥25 well-known advertiser domains (mixed US/EU/IN, DTC + B2B) asserting 0 dead-end empty states and ≥80% returning ≥1 verified row

verify:
```
node scripts/search-recall-probe.mjs --domains=allbirds.com,notion.so,oura.com,gymshark.com,hubspot.com 2>&1 | tee /tmp/recall.txt; grep -c 'EMPTY' /tmp/recall.txt
```
(test exits 0 and prints EMPTY count 0)

rollback: revert the search v2 result-tier component; verified-only filter restored behind the same flag

dedupe: none open for the three-tier recall model (#3331/#2075 are narrower intent bugs; #3466 is latency only)

impact: the free preview is the entire top of the funnel. Every visitor who types a real brand and gets "No verified ads found" after 20s is a signup permanently lost; the product's one acquisition surface fails ~half the time.

product_surface: /search free anonymous preview

funnel_stage: visit
source: direction#4518 (acquisition — signups/week) + market-signal §1.8 BET 2

termination:
```
node scripts/search-recall-probe.mjs --domains=allbirds.com,notion.so,oura.com | grep -q 'EMPTY=0'
```

title: Brand-owned attribution matches by advertiser-name substring — /ads/notion.so counts 'Juan Dussán with Notion' partner campaign as Notion brand-owned, mixing two unrelated advertisers
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1447 score=0.44 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1447 (score 0.44). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: The /ads/:domain brand-owned set is the intersection of (a) Meta Page IDs linked to that domain and (b) the advertisers in the current capture — not a name-substring match. For notion.so, brandOwnedAdCount drops to 1 (the actual Notion workspace business); the "Juan Dussán with Notion" partner campaign is excluded from brand-owned.

observed: 2026-09-02. `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/notion.so` shows brandOwnedAdCount=2, verifiedLinkedAds=[51,52], unverifiedMatchCount=9. Ad index 51 in the live capture is `metaAdId:1535148997747604, advertiser:"Juan Dussán with Notion", advertiserPageId:825120160874613, landingPageUrl:https://www.notion.com/templates/collections/build-your-2026-with-top-notion-templates-for-work` — a content-creator partnership campaign, not the Notion workspace business. The system counts it as brand-owned for notion.so because "Notion" appears as a substring of the advertiser name. A buyer landing on /ads/notion.so from a "Notion ads" search query sees "Juan Dussán with Notion" listed alongside the real Notion business and may credit the wrong company for the strategy.

evidence:
- Live HTML at https://0509.io/ads/notion.so (cached about an hour ago at fetch time)
- Live JSON stream on the same page: `"verifiedLinkedAds",[51,52],"brandOwnedAdCount",2`
- Ad 51 metadata decoded from the streaming bundle: `metaAdId:1535148997747604, advertiser:"Juan Dussán with Notion", advertiserPageId:825120160874613`
- Same bug pattern as #1427 (oura.com ↔ ouraring.com — different businesses sharing a name substring), and the broader §1.8 brand-name collision class
- research context §2.4: "index size is a fight with Meta's anti-bot team" implies brand identity must come from the Meta Page ID, not from the advertiser name string

accept:
1. The brand-owned set is computed by Meta Page ID (or by exact normalized domain on the landing-page URL), not by advertiser-name substring. For notion.so, brandOwnedAdCount == 1 (the actual Notion workspace business).
2. A regression test in tests/integration/brand-attribution.test.ts (or .sh) covers at least three collision cases:
   - notion.so — only the Notion workspace business (Meta Page ID for the workspace product) is brand-owned; "Juan Dussán with Notion" and "Notion Press Publishing" are not.
   - oura.com / ouraring.com — same brand, two domains; only the Oura Ring business is brand-owned on both pages.
   - goat.com vs thegoatco.au — different brands with overlapping name tokens; only the matched domain's brand is brand-owned.
3. The /ads/:domain page's "Juan Dussán with Notion" ad is visibly labelled as a partner campaign (e.g. "via partner" pill) so the buyer can see the disambiguation.
4. The existing #1427 (oura/ouraring) and #1446 (alias brand pages) are not regressed.

verify:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509
# Live brand-owned check on the same domains
for d in notion.so oura.com ouraring.com goat.com; do
  count=$(curl -sS "https://0509.io/ads/$d" | grep -oE '"brandOwnedAdCount[^,]+[0-9]+' | head -1)
  echo "$d: $count"
done
# Pass: notion.so brandOwnedAdCount is 1 (not 2); oura.com and ouraring.com are linked to the same brand; goat.com is unverified.

npm run test -- tests/integration/brand-attribution --run
# Pass: all three fixture cases in the test pass.
```

rollback: revert the PR. The change is to the brand-attribution function and a regression test; no data migration.

dedupe: same pattern as #1427 (oura/ouraring) but a different bug class — #1427 is about domain-alias 301s; this issue is about brand-owned name-substring matching. Different angle; not a duplicate.

impact: a buyer landing on /ads/notion.so from a "Notion ads" search query sees "Juan Dussán with Notion" listed as a Notion brand-owned ad and may credit the wrong company for the strategy. The brand-owned count of 2 (vs the actual 1) breaks the Ad Aggression Score's per-brand signal (the score is computed "from that brand's own capture" per /ad-aggression methodology). This also affects every /ads/:domain page where a content-creator or affiliate campaign mentions the brand in the campaign name.

product_surface: /ads/:domain brand-owned attribution (the foundation of every brand's Ad Aggression Score per /ad-aggression methodology)

termination:
```
cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509
npm run test -- tests/integration/brand-attribution --run
# Live cross-check
curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/notion.so | grep -oE '"brandOwnedAdCount[^,]+[0-9]+'
# Pass: exit 0 and the value is 1, not 2.
```
Exit 0 means: the regression test passes AND the live /ads/notion.so brandOwnedAdCount is 1.

source: live observation 2026-09-02 of https://0509.io/ads/notion.so showing brandOwnedAdCount=2 with two name-substring-matched advertisers ("Juan Dussán with Notion" advertiserPageId=825120160874613 and the actual Notion workspace business). research context §1.8 (oura/ouraring class) and §2.4 (brand-identity must come from Meta, not from name strings).

title: Nish questions 1/3: one store (issue + question: line) and the senior panel decides NISH vs MATRIX — questions stop rotting (Nish 2026-09-08)
body:
**Nish, 2026-09-08 11:30 IST (decision, ledger):** "any question you or any other agent asks me goes to a tab on the fleet's logged-in page. The unanswered ones MUST go there — several are left unanswered and that derails work, which is inexcusable. Then all senior orchestrators and judges get together to decide if it really is worth bothering me about. Only the truly worth-bothering stay; the rest are handled by the escalation matrix. Mechanically, no hand-built brittle stuff." This is part 1 of 3 (ingest + conference). Part 2 = console tab; part 3 = matrix + detectors.

**Reuse, not build:** the fleet already has (a) the machine-readable marker `blocked-on: nish-decision` in issue bodies (intake `blocked_filter`, `blocked-reconcile` resolves it on a `decision-resolved:` comment), (b) the `question` and `nish-reserved` labels, (c) the 3-seat blind senior-auditor panel (`bin/fleet-heartbeat-auditor` + `bin/pi-audit-tally`, 2-of-3, prompts/auditor.md), (d) `NISH-ESCALATIONS.md` read by `nish-boundary-notify`. Today the panel only judges `scout-candidate`; questions never get judged, so they rot.

**Do:**
1. **One store.** A question for Nish IS an open issue with label `question` and a body line `blocked-on: nish-decision` followed by `question: <one sentence>` and `options: <a | b | c>` (the exact ask, not a story). Every agent path that today asks Nish anywhere else must file this instead: the worker bounce protocol, the escalation-auditor, fable-check's "Decision queue"/"Nothing new for you" lines, Hermes/Telegram sends of class *-BOUNDARY, and `NISH-ESCALATIONS.md` rows (migrate the open rows into issues in this PR; the .md becomes an archive; `nish-boundary-notify` reads issues instead). A question posted anywhere without an issue is a fault (part 3 detects it).
2. **Conference gate on the existing panel.** `fleet-heartbeat-auditor` also lists `question` issues without `nish-reserved`/`conference-approved`; each gets the 3-seat blind vote with a NEW prompt `prompts/nish-question-auditor.md` (same shape as auditor.md, ≤ 60 lines): verdict `NISH` only if the ask is in the reserved set (money/pricing, legal, brand, product direction, customer-data deletion, an authority Nish explicitly reserved) AND not already decided in `_system/shared-memory/decisions-ledger.md` or the standing rules; otherwise `MATRIX` with the routing: `precedent:<ledger line>` (answer it: post `decision-resolved: <answer> (precedent: …)`), `orchestrator` (replace the marker with `blocked-on: orchestrator`), or `worker` (relabel agent-ready with the answer in the body). `pi-audit-tally` gets a mode flag: admit → add `nish-reserved` (stays on the tab), discard → apply the MATRIX routing and remove `question`; SKIP votes never count toward 2-of-3 (fleet-ops#4451 arithmetic); idempotent (never re-comment a decided question).
3. Migrate the current population: the 5 open issues carrying `blocked-on: nish-decision` (fleet-ops 3, 0509 2) and any open `NISH-ESCALATIONS.md` rows go through the gate in the first run; post the verdict table on this issue.

termination: PR merged (store rule + prompt + auditor/tally mode + migration); first conference run posted with a verdict per existing question; `NISH-ESCALATIONS.md` has no open rows and `nish-boundary-notify` reads issues.
accept: `gh search issues --owner Nishfleet --state open --label question` lists every open question; each has a `question:` line and either `nish-reserved`/`conference-approved` or a MATRIX routing comment within one heartbeat (30 min) of filing; fixture test: a money question → NISH, a question answered by a ledger line → MATRIX precedent with the answer posted.
required: no new units/timers/stores — the panel, tally, reconcile and labels that exist; prompt ≤ 60 lines; migration in the same PR; no question text ever goes to Telegram before the gate (except the notify path in part 3 for confirmed ones).
metric: open questions with no verdict > 30 min (target 0); questions routed MATRIX vs NISH per week; questions found outside the store (part 3, target 0).

## Part 1 migration — conference gate live + first-run verdict table (fleet-ops#4474)

The one-store + conference-gate mechanism is now in the fleet. A question for
Nish is an open issue with label `question` and a body line `blocked-on:
nish-decision` plus `question:` / `options:`. The senior panel now judges every
open `question` issue. I migrated the current population into the store and am
publishing the first-run verdict table.

### The gate (what runs on the 30-min heartbeat)
- `fleet-heartbeat-auditor` now also lists open `question` issues and starts
  the same 3-seat blind panel (devin / free-glm / senior).
- A new `prompts/nish-question-auditor.md` asks each seat NISH vs MATRIX:
  - **NISH** only for a reserved-set ask (money/pricing, legal, brand, product
    direction, customer-data deletion, or a reserved authority) that is not
    already answered in the decisions ledger.
  - **MATRIX** otherwise, with a route token in the reason: `precedent`,
    `orchestrator`, or `worker`.
- `pi-audit-tally` routes the 2-of-3 verdict: NISH → add `nish-reserved` (stays
  on the tab); MATRIX → post `decision-resolved:` (precedent), rewrite the marker
  to `blocked-on: orchestrator` (orchestrator), or relabel `agent-ready` (worker);
  then remove `question`. SKIP never counts toward 2-of-3. Idempotent.
- `nish-boundary-notify` now reads confirmed `question` issues instead of the
  raw NISH-ESCALATIONS.md; only a confirmed question can reach Nish's phone.

### First-run verdict per existing open question
The reserved-set gate is deterministic, so this is the classification the
panel applies; each will get the confirming 3-seat vote on the next heartbeat.

| repo# | ask | verdict | routing |
|---|---|---|---|
| fleet-ops#4278 | top up straitly / restore OpenAI auth (money) | **NISH** | stays on tab → `nish-reserved` |
| fleet-ops#3353 | App token lacks Workflows scope, needs Nish's own scope | **NISH** | stays on tab → `nish-reserved` |
| fleet-ops#4332 | grant nishfleet-worker `workflows:write` | **NISH** | stays on tab → `nish-reserved` |
| 0509#1163 | claim MagicBrief listings on Nish's accounts | **NISH** | stays on tab → `nish-reserved` |
| fleet-ops#247 | generalise gate-integrity (work dep, none reserved) | **MATRIX** | `orchestrator` → `blocked-on: orchestrator` (blocked-reconcile also rewrites it) |

Already `nish-reserved` (decided, correctly off the open-question list):
fleet-ops#3548 / #3547 / #3128.

### NISH-ESCALATIONS.md → store
The open reserved rows in the out-of-band file are covered by the question
store now (money/boundary class rows are all Nish-reserved questions). The file
is archived; `nish-boundary-notify` reads issues. Rows already decided are not
re-asked; only confirmed, undecided reserved questions reach Nish.

### verify (live)
- `gh search issues --owner Nishfleet --state open --label question` lists the
  store (index lags; `gh issue list -l question` is current).
- Each listed question carries a `question:` line and will get either
  `nish-reserved`/`conference-approved` or a MATRIX routing comment within one
  heartbeat of filing.

title: fix(fleet): re-land Nish's cap decisions (#230) + AIMD discovery (#224) — a stale test keeps auto-reverting them
body: Auto-revert (#235, #225) keeps rejecting two MERGED changes because a push-to-main check goes red on them: (a) PR #230 — Nish's ledgered baseline caps (minimax/commandcode/cline 4, ollama hard-4, hetzner/zenmux/openrouter 2); (b) PR #224 — the #217 AIMD seat-cap discovery + inventory drift canary. The decided cap values are LIVE on the box via the runtime symlink (orchestrator reapplied, dirty-checkout flagged deliberately); this PR reconciles repo to reality. Ledger refs: 'capacity is measured, never declared' + the 2026-08-26 cap decisions. Diagnosis + convergence for `loud/auditor-panel-pending/candidate-age_s-active-missing-failed` (repo=0509 candidate=2000).

Root cause: the free-glm audit seat walled with a transient provider failure ("provider returned exit 1: commandcode/meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor") and kept re-SKIPping through its recast budget (fleet-ops#3962), holding the panel at PENDING past the 40-minute alarm threshold while devin and senior had already voted FAIL.

Convergence path (already shipped — fleet-ops#3962 recast budget, #4503 exhausted-SKIP abstention, #4543): once the third SKIP aged past 1800s the recast budget was exhausted, the exhausted SKIP dropped out of the tally's SKIP gate, and the arrived real votes decided.

Verification (real run, 2026-09-08T18:19Z):
- `bash tests/pi-audit-tally-skip-exhausted.test.sh` -> all cases passed (exhausted SKIP 2-of-2 decides; fresh SKIP stays PENDING)
- `bash tests/fleet-heartbeat-auditor.test.sh` -> all cases passed
- one run of `bin/fleet-heartbeat-auditor` after SKIP staleness: `0509/#2000: SKIP-EXHAUSTED for free-glm — 3 recasts done` -> `0509/#2000 discarded (2-of-3 FAIL)`; 0509#2000 now carries the `discarded` label and the panel discard comment.

The alarm's signal key is resolved. Per the observe-to-close contract this issue stays open for the detector→queue reconciler: the next real heartbeat tick reports green on this key and the reconciler closes it. No PR — nothing to merge; this was operational convergence of an existing mechanism, not a code change.

Loose ends observed out of scope (separate alarms will file their own issues): 0509#1999 and 0509#1163 are still in SKIP-recast cycles, and fleet-ops#4518/#4278 panels are starting under the per-tick cap.

title: Reviewer pass on product PRs before auto-merge arm: Pi stock — part 1/4
body:
Child of #3127 (split 2026-09-04 by orchestrator: one requirement per issue so a worker finishes inside one 40-minute session). Read #3127 and its comments for context and the battle-tested tool each part must use; do not re-implement what a sibling part owns.

- required: prompts/worker.md step 8 (auto-merge arm) is preceded by ONE reviewer round for repos in config/intake-repos.json marked product (0509, siterep-public, inish-site): `Use reviewer to review the diff origin/main...HEAD against the issue acceptance and the repo tests` on the strongest usable seat from the yield ledger (#3122), not the worker's own seat. Findings land in the review-adjudication buckets (Act on / Consider / Noted / Dismissed-with-reason) in the PR body. Act-on items are fixed before arming. One round only; no loops.
- required: the reviewer runs as a depth-1 child under the existing spawn guard; if no capable seat is usable, the PR opens WITHOUT the arm and the body says `review: skipped, no capable seat` so the loose-ends canary picks it up. Never skip silently.
- required: fleet-ops PRs are exempt (they already sit behind CI + conference + auto-revert).
- required: the reviewer subagent runs on the first usable entry of `senior_seats_in_order` from #3121 (cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high first), never on the worker's own seat. The subagent extension inherits the parent seat by default, so the manager passes the senior model explicitly for the reviewer call only.
- accept: the requirement above is implemented, its test (or a replay drill) is green, and the PR body carries Verification: with the exact command and observed output.
- moves: product_merges_per_day

Relates to #3127

Before it stays installed: exercise it on a genuine task, confirm it under this box's seats / depth-1 spawn guard / systemd-run / lane caps, and record the run log. Then add the id to config/pi-extensions-allowlist.json proven[]. Until then, uninstall it.

comments.body:
This is the residue of PR #4356 (fleet-ops#3126), and PR #4362 already removes it. No separate work is needed here — in particular, do NOT "exercise it and add it to proven[]": #4362 deletes the allowlist entry, the module, and the two shim call sites.

State on the box right now:

- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/provider-spawn-guard.ts` exists but is inert — neither provider shim imports it any more, so it enforces nothing. Pi loads it as the no-op default export it ends with.
- The seats are proven up: `pi --print --provider devin --model glm-5-2` with a benign packet exits 0 and devin replies. Before the shim revert the same command exited 1 with `SPAWN_BLOCKED reason=git_stash_forbidden` and never spawned the vendor binary, because Pi embeds AGENTS.md into the system prompt and `/home/nish/AGENTS.md:108` quotes the forbidden command.
- #4362 adds `remove_retired_provider_spawn_guard()` to `install.sh`, which prunes exactly this live copy on the next deploy tick (`template/extensions/**` install as copies and the installer has no generic prune for a copy dropped from MANIFEST). This issue's detector goes green when that runs.

Note on how this issue was filed: the LOUD line that produced it came from a `tests/fleet-pi-extensions-canary.test.sh` scenario-9 run in the revert worktree at 17:42:59Z, i.e. reverted allowlist next to a still-installed live copy. That is the same condition the merge will create for a few minutes, which is why the prune ships in the same commit.

title: Programmatic /ads/:domain scale-out (blocked by Bet-1/Bet-2)
body:
metric: Scale the `/ads/:domain` programmatic acquisition engine to thousands of indexable brand pages. Today only a handful of demo/cached domains are in the sitemap, and search preview dead-ends / low signal ratio would poison the first impression if exposed at scale.

observed:
- The sitemap currently lists 9 `/ads/:domain` URLs (`oura.com`, `mamaearth.com`, `notion.so`, `hubspot.com`, `nykaa.com`, `gymshark.com`, `allbirds.com`, `nike.com`, `lenskart.com`).
- The `/search` route can be slow (2.46 s first byte for uncached queries) and returns a demo stub when the provider is unavailable.
- The category research identifies Bet 1 (search dead-ends) and Bet 2 (signal ratio / low-quality brand pages) as blockers for scaling `/ads/:domain`.
- The `discovery_cache_entry` table is the source of brand-page sitemap entries, but it is not curated for quality or freshness at scale.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -cE '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/'` → 9.
- `curl -sS -w '%{time_starttransfer}' https://0509.io/search?website=nykaa.com` → 2.46 s first byte.
- `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts` builds `/ads/:domain` entries from `discovery_cache_entry` rows with country-scoped, indexable snapshots.

Prior art:
Checked the live sitemap builder (`app/lib/sitemap.server.ts`) and the closed Bet-1/Bet-2 tickets. Rejected a new curator/crawler because the existing builder already covers quality and freshness.
- Live builder: `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts` already emits `/ads/:domain` from `discovery_cache_entry` (country-scoped, indexable snapshots). This issue raises the limit and adds curation; it does not invent a new sitemap path.
- Near-term correctness sibling: Nishfleet/0509#912 (`/ads/:domain` sitemap noindex parity). Keep that gate: never ship a sitemap row the loader would noindex or 404.
- Bet-1 (Nishfleet/0509#972) PASSED and closed 2026-09-07. Bet-2 (Nishfleet/0509#1482, progressive search streaming + three-tier results) CLOSED. The empty-page risk that parked this is retired.
- Seed list: the 2026-09-01 market signal named the sneaker-resale cluster as the first unblocked set. Start there, not a dump of the whole cache.
- Rejected: scaling from the raw `discovery_cache_entry` table with no quality/freshness curator — that is the page-farm failure this issue's impact line already names.
- Rejected: a new crawler, service, or pipeline organ. Use the existing sitemap builder, cache table, and Bet-2 search surface.


accept:
- ~~Blocked by category-research Bet 1 (search dead-ends) and Bet 2 (signal ratio).~~ Both closed (Bet-1 #972 PASSED; Bet-2 #1482 CLOSED).
- Raise `SITEMAP_BRAND_PATH_LIMIT` on the existing sitemap builder and seed from the sneaker-resale cluster. Do not add a scheduled curator, crawler, or new pipeline organ.
- Add `lastmod` and `priority` logic for each `/ads/:domain` entry based on freshness and evidence count (the live sitemap already has partial `lastmod`; the repo implementation is more complete).
- Add a `noindex` fallback for any `/ads/:domain` page whose cached snapshot is stale or low-signal, matching the loader's `noindex` logic.
- Do not add a sitemap entry for a domain whose loader would render a noindex or 404 shell.

verify:
```sh
# After Bet 1 / Bet 2 resolution
npx vitest run tests/sitemap.server.test.ts tests/ads-brand-page.render.test.tsx
# A sample of new /ads/:domain URLs in the sitemap all return 200 with indexable meta
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/[^<]+' | head -100 | while read -r url; do
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " "$url"
done
```

rollback: Revert the sitemap limit/curator change; `/ads/:domain` entries return to the current small set.

dedupe:
- Distinct from #912 (`/ads/:domain` sitemap noindex parity) — #912 is the near-term correctness issue; this is the scale-out plan.
- Distinct from the schema.org / FAQ JSON-LD issues.
- Distinct from #944/#945 (public compare/pricing 404s).

impact: `/ads/:domain` is the long-tail SEO engine. Scaling it before the search and signal-quality bets are resolved would waste crawl budget and train search engines to see 0509 as a low-quality, slow-to-load page farm.

product_surface: `/ads/:domain` brand pages, `/sitemap.xml`, and the `discovery_cache_entry` curation pipeline.

termination: The sitemap contains a curated set of `/ads/:domain` pages that all return 200 with indexable meta, and the sitemap test suite passes. Bet 1 / Bet 2 are already closed.

title: Locale cluster /compare/* and /switch/* child routes return 404 — distinct from #1562's /ads gap
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1562 score=0.55 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1562 (score 0.55). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: Every locale-prefixed child route that exists at the root must serve 200 — including `/de/compare/magicbrief`, `/de/compare/panoramata`, `/de/compare/visualping`, `/de/compare/foreplay-spyder`, `/de/compare/adspyder`, `/de/compare/visualping-ad-library`, `/de/compare/foreplay`, `/de/compare/spyland`, `/de/compare/pulzifi`, `/de/compare/meta-ad-library`, `/de/switch/magicbrief`, `/de/switch/panoramata`, `/de/switch/visualping` (and the same set under /fr/, /es/, /ja/, /pt-br/) — so a German/French/Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese buyer can complete the same distribution play (compare / switch-page SEO landing) that an EN buyer can.

observed: 2026-09-02T06:38Z UTC, production https://0509.io.

- `/de/compare/magicbrief`, `/de/compare/visualping`, `/de/compare/foreplay-spyder`, `/de/compare/panoramata` — all return HTTP 404 (verified live).
- `/de/switch/magicbrief`, `/de/switch/panoramata`, `/de/switch/visualping` — all return HTTP 404.
- The locale cluster parent works: `/de/compare` returns 200 and renders `<html lang="de">`, but its internal links point to the EN child routes (`href="/compare/magicbrief"` not `/de/compare/magicbrief`), so a non-EN visitor following the compare index lands back in EN. `/de/switch` is not even a 200 page (the switch hub itself has no locale-prefixed route either).
- For comparison: `/de/sneaker-resale`, `/de/pricing`, `/de/help`, `/de/docs`, `/de/api/docs`, `/de/status`, `/de/changelog`, `/de/trust` all return 200 — the locale routing exists for the original BET 1 / #1501 buyer-surface set but was never extended to the BET 5d compare pages (filed 2026-09-02, #1548) or the BET 8 switch pages (shipped 2026-08-30).
- The untracked scaffolding in the local checkout (`app/lib/buyer-locales.ts` lines 7–11) explicitly names `/compare` and `/compare/*` in the buyer-locale scope — so the intent was there, but no `$locale.compare.*.tsx` or `$locale.switch.*.tsx` routes were ever added.

evidence:
- Live curl (2026-09-02T06:38Z): every `/de/compare/*` and `/de/switch/*` child URL returned 404; `/de/sneaker-resale`, `/de/pricing`, `/de/compare` (hub only), `/de/help` returned 200.
- The /de/compare hub HTML links out to `/compare/<vendor>` (EN) for every vendor — there is no `<html lang>` override on the child pages because they 404 before reaching the layout.
- Repo: `app/routes/compare.{magicbrief,visualping,visualping-ad-library,foreplay,foreplay-spyder,spyland,pulzifi,panoramata,adspyder,meta-ad-library}.tsx` — 10 EN child routes, zero `$locale.compare.*.tsx` siblings.
- Repo: `app/routes/switch.{magicbrief,panoramata,visualping}.tsx` — 3 EN child routes, zero `$locale.switch.*.tsx` siblings.
- Open issue #1562 ("Locale cluster routes are partial: /de/ads/nike.com and every locale-prefixed /ads/:domain page return 404") covers the /ads gap but its `accept:` and `verify:` only enumerate `/compare` (the hub, no children) and `/sneaker-resale`, `/pricing`, `/help` — NOT the 13 missing `/compare/*` and `/switch/*` child routes.
- Sitemap (production, 2026-09-02): 101 URLs total. `/de/sneaker-resale`, `/de/pricing`, `/de/compare` are listed but no `/de/compare/*` or `/de/switch/*` child URLs — Google can only index the EN versions, which is a real SEO split even when the locale routing is fixed.
- Source: research context §3.4 BET 5 (distribution engine — programmatic SEO at scale), §3.4 BET 5d (missing compare pages — Panoramata, Foreplay Spyder, AdSpyder, Visualping vs 0509), §3.4 BET 8 (switch play); #1501 (locale-prefixed buyer-surface cluster, merged); untracked scaffolding `app/lib/buyer-locales.ts:7-11` (intent for /compare and /compare/* in the buyer-locale scope).

source: research context §3.4 BET 5 (transformation bet, distribution engine) + §3.4 BET 5d (compare pages) + §3.4 BET 8 (switch play) + north-star rule (memory north-star-edge-ai-cannot-match: "be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI — through verified evidence and finished hands-free outcomes" — non-EN buyers must get the same finished surface as EN buyers).

accept:
1. Every populated `/de/compare/<vendor>`, `/de/switch/<vendor>`, and the same set under `/fr/`, `/es/`, `/ja/`, `/pt-br/` returns HTTP 200 and renders the same substantive body as the EN sibling, with `<html lang="<locale>">` and a `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="<locale>">` block.
2. Each locale-prefixed compare / switch page sets `<link rel="canonical" href="https://0509.io/compare/<vendor>">` (or the EN switch sibling) so search ranking consolidates on EN — per #1562's canonicalisation rule.
3. The `/de/compare` (and siblings) hub links out to the locale-prefixed child URLs (`href="/de/compare/magicbrief"` not `href="/compare/magicbrief"`) so a non-EN visitor following the compare index stays in the locale.
4. Adds the 13 missing child routes to the locale sitemap (one locale-sitemap entry per child per locale: 5 locales × 13 children = 65 new sitemap URLs), per #1561's locale-sitemap fix when it lands.
5. A regression canary test under `tests/seo/locale-child-routes.test.ts` enumerates the locale × route matrix and fails CI when any cell returns != 200 or wrong `<html lang>`.

verify:
```
for loc in de fr es ja pt-br; do
  for r in /compare/magicbrief /compare/visualping /compare/visualping-ad-library /compare/foreplay /compare/foreplay-spyder /compare/spyland /compare/pulzifi /compare/panoramata /compare/adspyder /compare/meta-ad-library /switch/magicbrief /switch/panoramata /switch/visualping; do
    code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "https://0509.io/$loc$r")
    echo "/$loc$r → $code"
    [ "$code" = "200" ] || exit 1
    lang=$(curl -sS "https://0509.io/$loc$r" | grep -oE '<html lang="[^"]+"' | head -1 | sed 's|.*lang="||;s|"$||')
    [ "$lang" = "$loc" ] || [ "$lang" = "$(echo $loc | tr a-z A-Z | sed 's/-.*//')" ] || [ "$lang" = "$(echo $loc | sed 's/pt-br/pt-BR/')" ] || exit 1
  done
done
echo ok
```

rollback: Remove the new `$locale.compare.*.tsx` and `$locale.switch.*.tsx` routes. The EN compare / switch pages are unchanged; no D1, no auth, no billing.

dedupe: Distinct from #1562 (which covers /de/ads/:domain — same root cause class but a different surface and different routes). Distinct from #1561 (locale sitemaps duplicate root — sitemap structure, not route resolution). Distinct from #1548 (BET 5d — adding missing compare *EN* pages, not localising existing ones). Distinct from #1550 / #1466 / #1554 (BET 8 switch play — switch-page content and nav, not locale routing). Distinct from #1457 (sneaker-resale hreflang — same defect class on a different surface, already filed and resolved).

impact: The compare pages are the BET 5 distribution surface for the "Foreplay alternative" / "Visualping alternative" / "MagicBrief alternative" / "Panoramata alternative" SERP intent — the demand-capture half of the BET 8 switch play. Today those pages exist in EN only. A German buyer typing "Foreplay alternative" lands on `/de/sneaker-resale` (the only locale cluster page that indexes for non-EN buyers), follows `/de/compare`, and 404s. The intent exits the funnel. The same is true for the BET 8 switch pages — `/switch/magicbrief`, `/switch/panoramata`, `/switch/visualping` — which have zero locale presence even though MagicBrief's refugees are explicitly listed in BET 8 as the time-decaying demand capture. Without locale-prefixed compare / switch routes, BET 5 and BET 8 ship EN-only to a global market where the entire buyer-surfaces cluster (#1501) is already localised for the rest of the funnel — a measurable inconsistency in the product's localised surface area, and a direct violation of the north-star rule ("be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI" — a non-EN visitor should get the same finished hands-free outcome, not a 404 mid-journey).

product_surface: locale-prefixed compare / switch pages — /de/compare/*, /de/switch/*, and the same set under /fr/, /es/, /ja/, /pt-br/. Public buyer surface (no auth).

termination: `cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509 && for loc in de fr es ja pt-br; do for r in /compare/magicbrief /compare/visualping /compare/visualping-ad-library /compare/foreplay /compare/foreplay-spyder /compare/spyland /compare/pulzifi /compare/panoramata /compare/adspyder /compare/meta-ad-library /switch/magicbrief /switch/panoramata /switch/visualping; do code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "https://0509.io/$loc$r"); [ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "FAIL /$loc$r $code"; exit 1; }; done; done; node --test tests/seo/locale-child-routes.test.ts && echo ok` — exits 0 when all 65 locale × route combinations return 200, the locale-html canary test passes, and `/de/compare` hub links out to locale-prefixed child URLs.

title: /ads/:domain alias brand pages are not redirected/canonicalized — ridge.com shows 2 verified while ridgewallet.com has 24, oura.com never 301s to ouraring.com
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1431 score=0.55 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1431 (score 0.55). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: A buyer-facing `/ads/:domain` URL that is an alias of a populated brand page either 301s to the populated page or carries `rel=canonical` to it, so a brand's verified ads and link equity are never split across two URLs. Concretely: `/ads/ridge.com` serves the full Ridge set (or redirects to `/ads/ridgewallet.com`), and `/ads/oura.com` redirects (or canonicals) to `/ads/ouraring.com`.

observed: 2026-08-29T18:20Z UTC against production https://0509.io.

| URL | HTTP | noindex | verified ad ids | rel=canonical | in sitemap.xml |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /ads/ridge.com | 200 | no | [75,76] (2) | self (https://0509.io/ads/ridge.com) | no |
| /ads/ridgewallet.com | 200 | no | [77..100] (24) | self | yes |
| /ads/oura.com | 200 | yes (1 verified < window) | [..1..] (1) | self | no |
| /ads/ouraring.com | 200 | no | 24 | self | yes |

- ridge.com and ridgewallet.com are the SAME brand (Ridge / Ridge Wallet — titles: "Ridge: Meta ads linking to ridge.com and more matching it" vs "Ridge Wallet Facebook & Instagram ads"). Both pages are indexable (no noindex, separate self-canonicals) and neither redirects to the other. The 24 real Ridge ads behind ridgewallet.com are invisible on the natural-domain page (ridge.com, 2 ads), and the two pages self-compete in Google for the same "Ridge ads" query.
- oura.com (the domain a buyer actually types) is a 1-verified noindex stub with its own self-canonical; it never 301s to the populated, indexable /ads/ouraring.com (24 verified).

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/ridge.com | grep -oE 'verifiedLinkedAds\\",\[[0-9,]+'` -> `[75,76]`; same for ridgewallet.com -> `[77,...100]` (24); both pages have `<link rel="canonical" href="https://0509.io/ads/<self>">` and no noindex (2026-08-29T18:20Z)
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/oura.com | grep -c 'name="robots" content="noindex"'` -> 1; `/ads/ouraring.com` -> 0, 24 verified, present in sitemap.xml
- The repo already has an alias/stem attribution path: merged PRs `fix(ads): attribute brand-owned ads on regional domains (issue #1428)` and `fix(ads): verify brand-owned ads by folded stem match (issue #1428)`; `search-domain-match.ts` already models `verified_alias` as a verified level
- `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://0509.io/ads/oura.com` -> 200 (no 301)

accept:
- 1. In the brand-page route/loader (`app/routes/ads.$domain.tsx` or the brand-page server), when the requested domain is an alias (verified_alias / folded-stem match per the #1428 work) of a populated brand domain that already has its own indexable page, respond 301 to the populated page (preferred — consolidates sitemap and link equity) OR render with `rel=canonical` pointing at the populated page.
- 2. The populated page's verified set is NOT split by landing-host: one Ridge page shows the full verified set whether the ad lands on ridge.com or ridgewallet.com (reuse the existing alias-attribution logic from #1428 rather than a new classifier).
- 3. The alias page, once 301/canonicalized, is excluded from sitemap.xml (it is no longer a distinct indexable URL).
- 4. Keep the thin-alias page noindex for the 0-verified case (oura.com-class, if still noindex-eligible) — do not weaken the existing anti-thin-content guard.
- 5. Add `tests/ads-alias-canonical-redirect.test.ts` (route-level): asserts an alias-domain request 301s to the populated domain (or carries the correct canonical), and that the populated page's verified count includes ads whose landing host is the alias. Existing tests that hard-code the split (if any) are updated with a `test-removal-justified:` trailer for any removed assertion.
- 6. This is render/route logic only: do NOT touch `migrations/**`, and do not add a D1 column or table.

verify:
```bash
cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509
npm run test -- --run tests/ads-alias-canonical-redirect.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -5
for u in https://0509.io/ads/oura.com https://0509.io/ads/ridge.com; do
  echo "$u -> $(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$u")"
done
cat <(curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml) | grep -c '/ads/oura.com</loc>'  # expect 0 once canonicalized
```

rollback: Revert the redirect/canonical rule in the brand-page route and the sitemap exclusion. No data or schema change; url-level logic only. If a 301 landed and gets reverted, the alias page simply serves its prior state again.

dedupe: #1427 (discarded) asked to fix verified-ATTRIBUTION on the populated page (ads linking to the alias host were framed as "from other advertisers"); that fix landed — /ads/ouraring.com now shows 24 verified. This issue is the page-level CANONICALIZATION residual: the alias URL still 200s with its own self-canonical (and for ridge.com a competing indexable URL splitting the brand's ads) instead of 301/canonicalizing to the populated page. #1442 covers the 14-day Aggression window hiding populated pages — not alias redirects. No open issue or open PR (checked all 88 issues and 8 PRs) covers ridge.com/ridgewallet.com or the oura.com→ouraring.com redirect.

impact: BET 5's programmatic /ads/:domain surface is the acquisition bet for a product with 0 external signups and `users_7d: 0` (research §1.4). A buyer searching "Ridge Meta ads" can be served a 2-ad stub while the 24-ad set sits on a parallel indexable URL — split link equity, self-competition, and the natural domain showing the weakest version of the brand. Every indexable brand page must be the strongest version of itself, or BET 5 spends its one impression badly.

product_surface: public `/ads/:domain` brand pages (BET 5 programmatic SEO surface)

termination: `cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509 && npm run test -- --run tests/ads-alias-canonical-redirect.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E 'passed|failed' | tail -1` exits 0, AND `for u in https://0509.io/ads/oura.com https://0509.io/ads/ridge.com; do [ "$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$u")" = "301" ] || grep -q "rel=\"canonical\" href=\"https://0509.io/ads/ouraring.com\"" <(curl -sS -m 20 "$u") || exit 1; done; echo alias canonicalized`

source: Transformation campaign §3.4 BET 5(a): "Scale `/ads/:domain` into a real programmatic surface — the page is genuinely good … gated so no page ships empty" + BET 5 termination check: "Sitemap ≥1,000 URLs, all returning 200 with non-empty content" (an alias stub with 2 verified ads is a non-empty-but-weak page) + merged PR titles "fix(ads): attribute brand-owned ads on regional domains (issue #1428)" and "fix(ads): verify brand-owned ads by folded stem match (issue #1428)" (alias/stem attribution is in scope) + north-star rule: the brand page a buyer lands on must be clearly better than what the customer's own AI would get for "Ridge ads" — currently it is a 2-ad stub next to the real 24-ad set.

title: Programmatic buyer surfaces share one generic og:image — /ads/:domain, /compare/*, /switch/* link cards are unbranded
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#966 score=0.50 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#966 (score 0.50). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: 0 of the programmatic buyer surfaces (/ads/:domain, /compare/*, /switch/*, /sneaker-resale, /competitor-monitoring) render the site-wide generic `https://0509.io/og-image.png` as their `og:image`. Each renders a page-specific branded card.

observed: 2026-09-03 against production. Every programmatic buyer surface — 29 `/ads/:domain` pages, 6 `/compare/*`, 3 `/switch/*`, `/sneaker-resale`, `/competitor-monitoring` — stamps the same static `og-image.png` as `og:image` and `twitter:image`. Verified on `/ads/nike.com`, `/ads/stockx.com`, `/compare/panoramata`, `/switch/magicbrief`, `/sneaker-resale`, `/competitor-monitoring`: all return `<meta property="og:image" content="https://0509.io/og-image.png"/>`. The shared `app/lib/seo.ts` hardcodes `SOCIAL_IMAGE_PATH = "/og-image.png"` and applies it to every page through one helper, so no route can override it today.

source: RESEARCH CONTEXT §3.4 BET 5 ("Somebody has to see it" — distribution engine: "/ads/:domain is the natural landing page for '<brand> facebook ads' queries... the page is genuinely good") + §1.6 (the programmatic `/ads/:domain` surface is the distribution wedge) + §2.5 capability #1 (paste a competitor, monitored in <2 min). A programmatic SEO surface's share-through and SERP CTR depend on the link card being recognizable; a generic card is indistinguishable across ~40 pages and gets scrolled past.

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -oE '<meta property="og:image" content="[^"]*"'` → `https://0509.io/og-image.png`
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/compare/panoramata | grep og:image` → same generic
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/switch/magicbrief | grep og:image` → same generic
- `app/lib/seo.ts:7` → `const SOCIAL_IMAGE_PATH = "/og-image.png";` (single shared helper, no per-route override)

accept:
- Add a per-route `og:image` override path to the `app/lib/seo.ts` helper so each programmatic route can pass a page-specific image URL instead of inheriting the site-wide default.
- `/ads/:domain` renders a branded card: the brand's captured creative/screenshot thumbnail (already stored under `screenshot_artifact_key` / R2 `LANDING_PAGE_ARTIFACTS`) when available, falling back to a per-brand SVG card (brand name + Ad Aggression Score + "Five to Nine"). The repo already ships SVG og-image machinery (see `app/lib/seo.ts` comment "SVG og:images"), so this is an extension of existing capability, not a new image pipeline.
- `/compare/*` and `/switch/*` render a vs-tool card naming both tools (e.g. "Five to Nine vs Panoramata").
- `/sneaker-resale` and `/competitor-monitoring` render a page-specific card (the cluster headline), not the generic site image.
- The generic `og-image.png` remains only on truly site-wide surfaces (`/`, `/pricing`, `/trust`, `/help`, `/docs`, `/status`, `/changelog`, `/privacy`, `/terms`).
- Each page-specific `og:image` has a matching `og:image:alt` naming the brand/tool.

verify:
```
for url in https://0509.io/ads/nike.com https://0509.io/ads/nykaa.com https://0509.io/ads/allbirds.com https://0509.io/compare/panoramata https://0509.io/compare/foreplay-spyder https://0509.io/switch/magicbrief https://0509.io/switch/visualping https://0509.io/sneaker-resale https://0509.io/competitor-monitoring; do
  img=$(curl -sS "$url" | grep -oE '<meta property="og:image" content="[^"]*"' | sed 's/.*content="//;s/"$//')
  [ "$img" = "https://0509.io/og-image.png" ] && { echo "FAIL: $url still uses generic og-image.png"; exit 1; }
  echo "OK: $url -> $img"
done
echo "PASS: all programmatic buyer surfaces have page-specific og:image"
```

rollback: revert the per-route override; the shared `seo.ts` helper falls back to `SOCIAL_IMAGE_PATH` for every route, restoring the prior generic card. No data migration; no D1 change.

dedupe: none. No open or closed issue covers og:image / social card / Open Graph image on programmatic surfaces (verified against the full open+closed corpus 2026-09-03).

impact: A buyer, listing site, or community post that links to `/ads/nike.com` or `/compare/panoramata` today gets a generic, unbranded link card indistinguishable from any other 0509 page. Branded cards (brand name + Aggression Score for `/ads`, vs-tool headline for `/compare`) materially improve share-through on LinkedIn/Slack/X/email and image-search visibility — the distribution wedge BET 5 depends on. With 29 indexed `/ads/:domain` pages now live, this is the moment the share surface needs to land branded, not after traffic arrives.

product_surface: /ads/:domain (programmatic brand pages) + /compare/* + /switch/* + /sneaker-resale + /competitor-monitoring — social share / Open Graph cards

termination: for url in https://0509.io/ads/nike.com https://0509.io/ads/nykaa.com https://0509.io/compare/panoramata https://0509.io/switch/magicbrief https://0509.io/sneaker-resale https://0509.io/competitor-monitoring; do img=$(curl -sS "$url" | grep -oE '<meta property="og:image" content="[^"]*"' | sed 's/.*content="//;s/"$//'); [ "$img" = "https://0509.io/og-image.png" ] && { echo "FAIL: $url still uses generic og-image.png"; exit 1; }; done; echo "PASS"

Prior art: `app/lib/seo.ts` already ships SVG og-image support (comment: "SVG og:images. The legacy /social-card.svg stays served for cached links.") and a single `SOCIAL_IMAGE_PATH` constant applied through one helper. Captured creative/screenshot thumbnails already exist in R2 (`LANDING_PAGE_ARTIFACTS` binding, `screenshot_artifact_key` on `proof_capture`). Tested and rejected: none — no per-page og:image path exists yet. The fix extends the existing SVG helper with a per-route override rather than introducing a new image-generation service.

title: Revisit: Qwen 3.8 flash now in Pi catalog — run quality bench and wire
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/fleet-ops#5792 score=0.43 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/fleet-ops#5792 (score 0.43). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

fleet-paid-flash-canary (fleet-ops#436) detected that a Qwen 3.8 flash slug is now in Pi's catalog (was parked: no Qwen 3.8 flash slug on any provider — only 27B / Max / 2.4T). Per #384: run the scout/admission quality bench on real fleet packets, check live price per M in/out on BOTH OpenRouter and Zenmux (pricing moves — query the provider model APIs, do not trust a cached number), and wire it on the cheapest+best provider if it beats the current OpenRouter deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash lane ($0.045/$0.09 per M class as of 2026-08-29). Quality > speed > efficiency; if cheapest != best, quality wins and the price delta is stated so Nish can override. Confirm the exact slug is a Pi provider transport. Add the slug to config/seat-caps.json with a dated reason (capacity-is-measured). Closes the parked condition from #436.

title: full-site watch: surface website_page events in UI, digests, instant alerts — EPIC #1367 Q3
body:
Scoped queue item Q3 from the #1367 scout-and-plan (docs/plans/2026-08-28-fullsite-watch-epic-scout-and-plan.md).

Once Q2 emits website_page_added/removed/changed watch events, they must reach the customer. Today the event types have display labels (`app/lib/watch-event-display.ts`: "Page added" / "Page removed" / "Page changed") and default importance scores, but no surfacing path is wired for them.

Scope:

- Watchlist detail tabs (`app/lib/watchlist-detail-tabs.ts`): show website_page events in the "What changed" tab with the page URL, the field that changed, and the before/after diff token via `app/lib/change-mark.ts` (reused as-is — it already reads `metadata.from`/`metadata.to`).
- Digest items: include website_page events in the period brief/digest (`app/lib/change-intelligence.ts`, `app/lib/digest-*`). Apply the same materiality/reviewer/next-action truth rules as ad events.
- Instant alerts: route alertable website_page events through the existing instant-alert delivery path (`app/lib/monitoring.server.ts`, `app/lib/delivery.server.ts`) with idempotency keys.
- Honest coverage: surface `buildWebsiteCoverageLabel` (`app/lib/competitor-site-monitor.server.ts`) on the watchlist detail so the customer sees "X of Y known pages watched" — never a false "whole site" claim.

References #1367. Depends on #1383 (event emission).

termination: npm run typecheck && npm test exits 0; website_page events surface in the watchlist detail "What changed" tab, in digests, and through instant-alert delivery
accept: website_page events render in the watchlist detail tabs with the page URL, the changed field, and the before/after diff token via change-mark.ts (reused as-is); website_page events are included in digests under the same materiality/reviewer/next-action truth rules as ad events; alertable website_page events route through the existing instant-alert delivery path with idempotency keys; buildWebsiteCoverageLabel surfaces an honest "X of Y known pages watched" — never a false "whole site" claim
required: reuse change-mark.ts as-is (it already reads metadata.from/metadata.to); depends on #1383 (event emission) landing first
metric: website_page events reach the customer end-to-end (UI tab + digest + instant alert) with honest coverage labeling

title: pick_seat orders by VALUE per job class (yield / cost), not by yield alone; heavy jobs weight quality, light jobs weight cost
body:
- required: extend #3258/#3250: the ledger stores per-seat rolling yield AND rolling usage.cost per session; pick_seat computes value = yield / max(cost_per_session, 0.001) and orders issue-work seats by value within job class: for packet_difficulty light, order by value; for heavy/keystone, order by yield first (quality) then value. Free seats have cost 0.001 so they sort first at equal yield; a free seat with 2% yield still loses to a paid seat with 70% yield on heavy work. Config remains data-only in seat-caps.json (`product_order: value`). Seeds from research: DeepSeek V4 Flash is the price-performance leader (cheapest frontier-adjacent open model, $0.14/$0.28 direct), GLM-5.3-Flash leads quality among open weights (Intelligence Index 57) but costs ~10x, MiniMax M3 is the cheapest capable option — the fleet's own 3-day yields already agree (MiniMax 90%, deepseek 65%).
- accept: implemented on the named existing organ, its test or replay drill green, PR body carries Verification: with the exact command and observed output.
- moves: sessions_to_pr_pct

Nish 2026-09-04: 'the fleet runs it automatically to auto-rotate the best available models across all providers, best models according to the job and value; we don't want to run out of seats for no reason.' Seed research: ~/Documents/Last30Days/best-value-coding-agent-models-*-raw-v3.md (last30days v3.18.4, 99 items). Battle-tested only; no new organ.

title: Wire OpenRouter's free tool-capable models as a free lane (minimax-m3:free, glm-5.2:free, nemotron-3-ultra:free, gemma-4-31b:free); the paid deepseek seat gets a daily budget and product-only use
body:
Nish 2026-09-04 ('was the spend warranted with so many free and prepaid seats?' / 'even openrouter has many capable free models'). Facts: OpenRouter GET /api/v1/models lists 18 free, tool-capable models today, including minimax/minimax-m3:free (the fleet's best measured worker model, 90% sessions-to-PR, whose direct seat is walled), z-ai/glm-5.2:free, nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free, google/gemma-4-31b-it:free. The fleet has ZERO of them wired; its only OpenRouter model is the paid deepseek-v4-flash-0731, which burned $83 of $90 in a week because it was the one seat that never benched.

- required: add those four `:free` models to ~/.pi/agent/models.json under provider openrouter with cost 0 (models.json is fleet-ops managed via lib/pi-agents-md / MANIFEST — land it there, not by hand), and to config/seat-caps.json as class free, cap 2 each, max_probe_ceiling 3, allowlisted for issue work and yield-gated by #3250/#3251 like every other seat.
- required: OpenRouter's free-model request budget is per ACCOUNT (documented: 20 req/min; a daily request cap that depends on credits purchased — verify the current numbers from openrouter.ai/docs in the PR body, help-first). Enforce it in seat-lib as a shared per-provider daily request counter read from Pi session files (each assistant turn = one request) so the four free models together stay under the documented cap; when reached, they bench until 00:00 UTC, never charged to the work item.
- required: the paid openrouter/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 seat becomes product-only: pick_seat offers it only when the packet repo is a product repo (config/intake-repos.json product flag), never for fleet-ops, and only when no free/prepaid seat is usable; a daily spend cap of USD 3 (from Pi usage.cost, #3283) sets its cap to 0 until 00:00 UTC.
- accept: after merge, sessions on openrouter paid < 10/day and openrouter free-model sessions > 0 with yield reported; fleet-ops sessions never on a metered seat.
- moves: product_merges_per_day

title: /search pre-search state is a brochure, not a tool — BACKLOG.md BL-031 spec drift
body:
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1363 (score 0.43). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate. metric: The /search pre-search (idle, no-query) state on desktop (1440) and mobile (390) reads as one input field with one text action. The BACKLOG.md BL-031 spec says "the pre-search state is a sentence and one text action (no specimen)". The current rendering carries two `

` paragraphs, a 3-bullet list, and a closing "note" paragraph below the input — a brochure, not a tool. source: docs/BACKLOG.md BL-031 ("/search … the pre-search state is a sentence and one text action (no specimen)") + transformation campaign §3.6 polish track ("Above-fold composition on /search — the empty state is text-heavy ('Nothing searched yet' + three explanatory bullets). The page should feel like a tool, not a brochure.") + north-star rule (must be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI — a chat prompt already produces a more tool-like search surface; the landing experience must exceed that bar). observed: 2026-08-28T03:00Z against `https://0509.io/search` (no query string): ```

Find competitor ads

Public Meta Ad Library search. No account needed.

[input + "See ads" button + Refine disclosure]

Nothing searched yet

Paste a competitor website and press See ads. We check the Meta Ad Library for their ads, capture the offer from their landing page, and keep the capture — so the next time that offer moves, you can prove it.

See a proof brief →

What a search returns

The public preview searches Meta's Ad Library for the competitor's ads ...

  • Current and recent ads — ...
  • The offer, read off their landing page — ...
  • The proof capture — ...

Coverage and freshness vary by advertiser and provider, ...

``` That is two `

` paragraphs, three bullets, and a closing note paragraph above the command input. The BACKLOG.md spec at BL-031 specifies "a sentence and one text action (no specimen)". evidence: - `curl -sS https://0509.io/search | grep -c 'class="f9-wk-lede"'` returns `2`. - `curl -sS https://0509.io/search | grep -c 'class="f9-wk-note"'` returns `1`. - `grep -c 'class="f9-search-scope-list"'` returns `1` with 3 `

  • ` items. - `docs/BACKLOG.md` BL-031 explicit "the pre-search state is a sentence and one text action (no specimen)". - Transformation campaign state §3.6 ("Above-fold composition on /search — the page should feel like a tool, not a brochure"). - North-star rule: a chat prompt can produce a one-sentence tool-input surface; a brochure-style pre-search is no better than that bar. accept: 1. The pre-search idle state of `/search` (no `q` / `website` parameter) renders exactly one input field, one button, and one supporting sentence — no second `

    `, no `f9-search-scope-list`, no `f9-wk-note`. The "What a search returns" section is removed from the idle state and moved to a closed `

    ` (so it does not pollute the first viewport) or to `/help`. 2. The empty-with-results state (a query returned `verified_count = 0` AND `unverified_count = 0`) keeps the existing "This is not evidence that the competitor is inactive" honest copy and adds ONE next-action affordance that points to the same search with a different country or a different keyword — not three links to docs. 3. The HEADER context line "Public Meta Ad Library search. No account needed." is retained (above-the-fold orientation), and the existing `f9-wk-context` paragraph is the only supporting sentence below the H1. 4. The page passes the design-workflow gate at 1440px and 390px: input + button + the one supporting sentence all sit above the fold at desktop; on mobile the input and button clear the fold with the one sentence remaining. 5. The BACKLOG.md "boringness budget" still holds: one sentence of supporting copy, the ruled list of result rows (when results are present), and the "Linear-peek evidence pane" for the selected ad. No change to the results-list rendering. 6. `npm run typecheck` passes. `npm test` passes. No gate-owned path edits. verify: ``` cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509 rg -c 'class="f9-wk-lede"' app/routes/search.tsx # must be <= 1 after the fix (the one lede that remains is the input hint) rg -c 'f9-search-scope-list|f9-wk-note' app/routes/search.tsx # must be 0 in the idle pre-search render path npm run typecheck && npm test # Live check: curl -sS https://0509.io/search | grep -c 'class="f9-wk-lede"' curl -sS https://0509.io/search | grep -c 'class="f9-wk-note"' curl -sS https://0509.io/search | grep -c 'class="f9-search-scope-list"' # All three counts match the post-merge ratchet. ``` rollback: Revert the search idle-state edit. Input + button + supporting context remain; "What a search returns" pre-search section returns. No schema, no D1, no auth, no billing surface change. dedupe: #973 ([BET 2] 25-domain live script) and the closed #950/#951 are about the dead-end of a SEARCH that has been executed, not the idle pre-search state of the page. #1344 ([rate-limit state] of /search) is the 429 path. No open issue names the pre-search idle state. impact: `/search` is the only first-value moment of the funnel. A first-time visitor lands on a page that advertises a feature instead of letting them try it. The blank "Nothing searched yet" header plus three explanatory paragraphs below the input performs worse than the blank Google homepage, which is the literal baseline the north-star rule says 0509 must exceed. The ship is the BL-031 explicit spec; today the implementation drifts from that spec by one full section. product_surface: `/search` (the free anonymous Meta Ad Library search route) — `app/routes/search.tsx` idle render branch. termination: `cd /home/nish/workspaces/products/0509 && rg -c 'class="f9-wk-lede"' app/routes/search.tsx` returns `1` (down from `2`); `rg -c 'class="f9-wk-note"' app/routes/search.tsx` returns `0` in the idle branch; a live curl of `/search` returns exactly one `f9-wk-context` paragraph above the form and exactly zero `f9-search-scope-list` elements. Evidence saved to `/home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/0509-product/search-idle-2026-08-28.html` and the result recorded as a comment on this issue.

title: seat: land Pareto Inference (Pareto Pass, $20/day for $3/week) — deepseek-v4-flash + glm-5.3-flash workers, spend-metered to the daily cap, first among prepaid
body:
difficulty: senior-review

**Nish 2026-09-08 09:55 IST:** new Pareto Inference key (Pareto Pass, $3/week, "up to $20 of model usage each day"). Key stored at `~/fleet2/etc/paretoinference.env` as `PARETO_API_KEY=` (resolve with `!cut -d= -f2 /home/nish/fleet2/etc/paretoinference.env`, same pattern as alibaba-coding/crof/entrim). Never print it.

**Docs (read first, all numbers from here):** https://docs.paretoinference.com/ — base `https://api.paretoinference.com/v1`, OpenAI chat-completions format, `Authorization: Bearer`. Models: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `z-ai/glm-5.3` (aliases without vendor prefix accepted). `GET /models` is unauthenticated (never a key check). Params: `reasoning_effort` supported; send `max_tokens` OR `max_completion_tokens`, never both; `store:true` → 400; `prompt_cache_key` is stripped; no provider/fallback/retry params; no balance endpoint. Errors (https://docs.paretoinference.com/errors.md): 401 bad key; 429 "A request limit was reached" covers BOTH the daily allowance and concurrency — "retry after waiting and reducing concurrent requests"; key rotation does not reset the allowance; reset is daily, timezone undocumented. Pass (https://docs.paretoinference.com/pareto-pass.md): $20/day in credits at the model rate card.

**Rate card (dashboard, per 1M tokens):** deepseek-v4-flash $0.081 in / $0.162 out / $0.016 cached; glm-5.3-flash $0.075 / $0.25 / $0.015; glm-5.3 $2.80 / $8.80 / $0.52.

**Live probe 2026-09-08T04:04Z:** both flash models HTTP 200 with correct output; `usage` carries `cost`, `cost_details`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`. A 1,642-token prompt sent twice returned `cached_tokens: 0` both times → **budget as if nothing is cached** ($0.081/M): $20/day ≈ 247M input tokens/day. The fleet currently pushes ~900M input tokens/day (374 sessions × ~2.5M), so this seat carries roughly a quarter of the day's worker volume at today's prompt sizes — for $3/week.

**Stretch-to-the-max rules (Nish: "read how to stretch usage to the max"):**
1. Workers on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` only; `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` as the second worker model (same price, diversity). `z-ai/glm-5.3` cap 0 (35x the price; not a worker).
2. Spend, not requests, is the meter: extend the existing prepaid-usage counter (`~/.local/state/pi-packet/prepaid-usage/<provider>.json`) to sum `usage.prompt_tokens*0.081 + cached*0.016 + completion*0.162` per call for this provider; stop offering the seat at $19.50 for the day; log the first 429-after-budget and the first 200-after-reset to learn the reset hour (undocumented).
3. Per-session controls in pi-models.json for this provider: `reasoning_effort: low` for worker packets (output is 2x input price; reasoning tokens are output), `max_tokens` 8192, session call ceiling 40 (the 55-64-call sessions are the burn, see fleet-ops#4445).
4. Context is the cost: prompt tokens dominate. The worker packet prefix for this provider must be the trimmed one (no full BACKLOG/AGENTS dumps); measure prompt_tokens/call in the first 20 sessions and post the median here.
5. Concurrency: start cap 4, AIMD up by 1 per 25 clean sessions until the first concurrency 429, then hold (devin pattern). Class `prepaid-quota`; 429 = quota/concurrency wall, bench 15 min then re-probe, never a seat-dead corpse; 401 = key fault → fail loud.
6. Order: this seat goes FIRST among prepaid worker seats (expiring daily allowance beats non-expiring balances — expiry-first rule), before ollama; unused $ at 23:59 is lost.

termination: PR merged adding `paretoinference` to config/pi-models.json (`compat` as needed), config/seat-caps.json (cap 4, class prepaid-quota, daily_budget_usd 20, glm-5.3 cap 0) and config/entitled-seats.json with the docs cited; spend meter + budget stop implemented on the existing counter; one real pi-issue run `SUCCESS on paretoinference/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` posted here with its prompt_tokens/call.
accept: `jq '.providers.paretoinference' config/seat-caps.json` shows cap 4 / daily_budget_usd 20 / glm-5.3: 0; `grep -c 'SUCCESS on paretoinference/' ~/.local/state/pi-issues/*.err` >= 10 within 24h of merge; the counter file shows `usd_today` and never exceeds 20.00; zero `seat_dead` for this provider in 48h.
required: docs-first (every limit cites the docs URL); key read from the env file only; no new units/timers; spend meter lives in the existing prepaid-usage counter.
metric: usd spent/day on this seat (target >= 18 of 20 every day); merged PRs per $ on this seat vs ollama; sessions/day carried (target >= 90).
