title: BET 6 — Move read-only MCP / API access down to free + Scout
body:
source: Transformation campaign state PART 3 §3.4 BET 6 ("Agent-native change history, ungated") + 2026-08-27 market-signal inventory (users 15, paid 0, 0 keys ever issued, agent surface "gated to €135 Agency" with 0 customer_api_key rows in D1); north-star rule (be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI — locking the unique intersection behind the one plan that has never sold violates the rule).

metric: A free-tier (or Scout-tier) account can create a `customer_api_key` and use it to call read-only MCP/API endpoints (`get_change_history`, `get_offer_state_at`, `diff_offer`, `list_suppressed`) with the response including evidence links and capture timestamps. `customer_api_key` row count for non-Nish accounts > 0 within 14 days of ship.

observed: 2026-08-27, live D1 + `/api/docs`. `app/routes/api.mcp.ts:24` hard-codes `const API_PLAN_REQUIREMENT = "Agency"`; `app/routes/api.docs.tsx:50` reads "Developer API and connected-tool access require Agency." Production D1 has `customer_api_key: 0` rows. Meanwhile Visualping, Foreplay, and GetHookd ship agent access on their free/entry tiers and already own the "you can call us from your agent" search-result real estate. The 0509 agent surface (22 audited actions, real MCP) is the richest in the category by content, and the most locked by packaging.

evidence:
- https://github.com/Nishfleet/0509/blob/main/app/routes/api.mcp.ts (line 24, plan-gate constant)
- https://github.com/Nishfleet/0509/blob/main/app/routes/api.docs.tsx (lines 50, 61 — Agency gate copy)
- https://0509.io/api/docs (live page reads "require Agency")
- D1 query result recorded in `docs/2026-08-25-five-to-nine-north-star.md` (Part 1.4) — `customer_api_key: 0`
- Category landscape: Visualping MCP on free tier, Foreplay MCP on all plans, GetHookd MCP on free tier

accept:
- `app/routes/api.mcp.ts` separates the plan gate into a per-action allowlist: read-only tools (`get_change_history`, `get_offer_state_at`, `diff_offer`, `list_suppressed`, `workspace_readiness`, `collection.read`, `watchlist.read`, `digest.read`, `memory.read`, `web_mentions.list`) work for free + Scout; write/export tools stay on Starter/Agency; account-mutation tools stay on Agency.
- `customer_api_key` issuance moves to the free-tier developer-access UI with a free-tier key defaulting to read-only scope; write scopes require Starter+.
- `/api/docs` copy is rewritten to match: "Read-only access on free + Scout. Writes and exports on Starter+. Full agent actions on Agency." Cite the per-tool tier on the docs page itself (a one-line per-tool table), not a buried link.
- An integration test under `tests/integration/api-mcp-tier-gating.test.ts` (real D1 binding, not mocked) asserts: free key can call each read-only tool and gets a 200; free key calling a write tool gets a clean 402/403 with the documented tier message; Scout key matches the same surface.
- `app/lib/plan-feature-gate.server.ts` is the single source of truth; no per-route ad-hoc `requireAgency()` checks remain that contradict it.

verify:
```
npm run test:integration -- api-mcp-tier-gating
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREE_KEY" https://0509.io/api/mcp -d '{"method":"get_offer_state_at","params":{"domain":"nike.com","date":"2026-08-20"}}' | jq '.ok, .evidence_url'
gh api -X POST repos/Nishfleet/0509/issues/comments/$(gh issue list -R Nishfleet/0509 --search 'BET 6 — Move read-only MCP' --json number --jq '.[0].number') -f body='free key returns offer state with evidence link'
```

rollback: Revert the plan-gate change in `app/routes/api.mcp.ts` and `app/lib/plan-feature-gate.server.ts`; existing free-tier keys created under the new model are revoked in one SQL (`UPDATE customer_api_key SET revoked_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE plan_at_creation IN ('free','scout') AND created_at > <merge_sha_time>`). Copy revert in `/api/docs` is a single PR. No D1 schema change, so no down-migration risk.

dedupe: No open issue covers ungating the agent surface. #1163 is about *external listing* of MagicBrief pages (different flow, external venues). #1132/#1137 are about the sitelink search path (different surface, no API). #1264 is the capture-validity rules page (different mechanism, no API).

impact: Unlocks the only differentiator §2.5 row 6 names (cross-competitor change history spanning ads AND landing pages, queryable from an agent). Without this, BET 3's longitudinal history is read-only inside the UI; with it, it becomes the only read-anything-with-an-agent entry point in the category that is not just "view my saved pages." The north-star rule says: be clearly better than the customer's own AI. The customer can already do "summarise my saved ads" with their AI; they cannot do "tell me what changed on nike.com in June with receipts" — and right now neither can 0509 unless the buyer is on a €135 plan that nobody has bought.

product_surface: `/api/mcp`, `/api/v1/*`, `/api/docs`, `/app/developer-access`

termination: `tests/integration/api-mcp-tier-gating.test.ts` exits 0 against a real D1 binding and the free + Scout cases both pass; `npm run canary:agent-ungate` (new script) hits production with a freshly issued free-tier key and returns 200 for `get_offer_state_at(domain='nike.com', date='2026-08-20')` with a non-null `evidence_url` in the response.

notes-for-worker: Per the project's design system, do not regress the bone/ink/signal-green case-file look on the developer-access UI if it needs new copy; keep mono evidence tags. Tier decision in `[NISH]` boundaries: if the worker is told to keep read access on Scout (not free), that is acceptable as long as the gate move lands; the BET 6 spec says "free + Scout" but the panel can downgrade free to Scout-only.

title: feat(gate): pass PR author and pusher into the gate-integrity context bundle
body:
Follow-up to #1140.

`gate-integrity.sh` now reads `author` and `pusher` as implementers (same rule as fleet-ops#413). The live `gate-integrity.yml` context step does not yet put those fields in the bundle, because nishfleet-worker cannot push `.github/workflows/**`.

Until this lands, the live gate-integrity check still rejects a worker attestor (the bot cannot attest) but cannot see PR author or head-commit pusher, so the overlap case (worker plus human among implementers, human attests) is unenforceable on that gate.

`required-verifier-integrity.yml` already passes `author`. This issue is only the gate-integrity workflow: add PR author (`github.event.pull_request.user.login`) and the head-commit GitHub login (`.author.login // .committer.login`) to the bundle as `author` and `pusher`.

Needs a token with Workflows permission. Do not land from nishfleet-worker.

comments.body: lifecycle-label: agent-ready by fleet-heartbeat at 2026-08-26T19:49:11Z (unlabeled open issue; fleet-ops#376)
claimed by pi-issue-0509-1176 at 2026-08-26T20:15:36Z

nishfleet-worker cannot land this. The issue already says so: this file lives under `.github/workflows/**`, and the App has no Workflows permission. A push of that path is rejected at GitHub.

Do not dispatch this issue to nishfleet-worker again. Land it with a token that has Workflows permission (Nish's own GitHub identity). After that, a repository admin other than the PR author posts the sha-bound `gate-integrity-attest:` comment. Do not attest from the worker that would have opened the PR.

## What to change

Only `.github/workflows/gate-integrity.yml`, context step `Resolve candidate context through the GitHub API`. Mirror `required-verifier-integrity.yml`'s `AUTHOR` env, then add the head-commit GitHub login as `pusher`.

`gate-integrity.sh` on claim/issue-1140 (PR #1178) already reads `author` and `pusher` as implementers. Extra keys are ignored on current main, so this can land before or after #1140. The overlap case (worker + human among implementers, human attests) stays unenforceable until both land.

### 1. Add AUTHOR to the context step env (next to PR_BODY)

```yaml
          AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
```

### 2. After the commits_json fetch, resolve pusher from the head commit

Use the GitHub user on the commit object, not the git name/email:

```bash
          pusher="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA" \
            --jq '.author.login // .committer.login // ""')"
```

### 3. Pass both into the bundle jq

Add:

```bash
            --arg author "${AUTHOR:-}" \
            --arg pusher "$pusher" \
```

And include them on the object (same jq -n that already writes `head_sha` / `pr_body`):

```
author: $author, pusher: $pusher
```

The emitted bundle must contain `"author"` and `"pusher"` as strings (empty string if GitHub has no linked user on the head commit).

## Lock-test to include in the same PR

In `.github/scripts/test-gate-integrity.sh`, add a grep against the live workflow file so dropping these fields fails the fixture job:

- `.github/workflows/gate-integrity.yml` contains `github.event.pull_request.user.login`
- it contains `.author.login // .committer.login`
- the bundle jq object includes `author: $author` and `pusher: $pusher`

That is the prevention: a later edit that builds the bundle without those two fields is red before it merges.

## Verify after landing

```
bash .github/scripts/test-gate-integrity.sh
actionlint .github/workflows/gate-integrity.yml
```

Live: a PR whose implementers include `nishfleet-worker[bot]` plus a human, with a human `gate-integrity-attest:` at head sha, must FAIL once #1140 is also on main. Today that case cannot fail because the live bundle has neither field.

title: Verify or retire /compare/pulzifi and /compare/spyland — no verifiable primary source for either product
body:
metric: Zero compare pages targeting products without a verifiable, cited primary source (live pricing page, public docs, or credible third-party listing).

observed: 2026-08-27T08:35Z UTC. Two live `/compare/` pages ship in the sitemap and are linked from the footer:
- `/compare/pulzifi` — cites `https://pulzifi.com/` as the pricing source
- `/compare/spyland` — cites `https://spyland.ing/` as the pricing source

category-research.md §2.2 explicitly flags both: "Not real / mischaracterised: Pulzifi, Spyland... no verifiable primary source found (0509 ships compare pages for two of them)." Publishing comparisons against phantom or unverified products is a credibility risk — a prospect who checks the source finds nothing, or a mischaracterised product, and concludes 0509's other comparisons are equally untrustworthy.

source: category-research.md §2.2 — "Not real / mischaracterised: Pulzifi, Spyland... no verifiable primary source found (0509 ships compare pages for two of them)."

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep compare` — both URLs present in sitemap
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/compare/pulzifi` — page cites "check the live source at https://pulzifi.com/ for current limits"
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/compare/spyland` — page cites "Confirm current plans on the live source at https://spyland.ing/"
- `category-research.md` §2.2: "Not real / mischaracterised: Pulzifi, Spyland... no verifiable primary source found"

accept:
1. For each page (`/compare/pulzifi`, `/compare/spyland`): either (a) a cited, live, verifiable pricing/product page is added to the compare page's "honest trade-off" section (with a working URL that returns 200 and shows the product), OR (b) the route, its sitemap entry, and its footer link are removed.
2. No 404 or phantom compare pages remain in the sitemap.
3. A one-line note in the compare page doc (or code comment) recording the verification outcome and source URL.

verify:
```bash
# Check sitemap no longer contains the retired URLs (if retired)
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -E '(pulzifi|spyland)' && echo "STILL PRESENT" || echo "CLEAN"

# If kept: verify the cited source URL returns 200 and shows a real product
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://pulzifi.com/
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://spyland.ing/
```

rollback: Restore the compare route files (`app/routes/compare.pulzifi.tsx`, `app/routes/compare.spyland.tsx`) and sitemap entries. No data stores touched.

dedupe: Checked against all open issues/PRs on 2026-08-27. No existing issue covers these two specific compare pages. #1163 (MagicBrief wind-down listings) is about external submissions, not compare-page accuracy. Q7 in category-research.md §3.5 names this exact item as unfiled.

impact: The compare pages are high-trust SEO surfaces — a prospect evaluating 0509 reads them to understand the category. Citing unverified or non-existent competitors undermines every other comparison (Visualping, Panoramata, Foreplay, AdSpyder) which are real and verifiable.

product_surface: `/compare/pulzifi`, `/compare/spyland`, sitemap.xml, footer compare links.

termination: curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -E '(pulzifi|spyland)' returns nothing (if retired) OR both cited source URLs return HTTP 200 with verifiable product content (if kept).

title: fleet-gap-closure-slo: unmeasured SLO inputs compute as failing (fail closed) — implements #4297
body: All three auditors converged. In bin/fleet-gap-closure-slo (which reads config/slo-definitions.json), any required field that is null or empty computes as budget-exhausted, not pass: queue_starvation_minutes=null -> fail; time_to_repair_per_class={} -> fail; same rule for any future required field. green=true only when every required field is measured AND passing. The snapshot must record measured:true|false per field so a reader can distinguish 'unmeasured' from 'zero'. Burn semantics: compute remaining budget from the underlying series per slo-definitions.json rather than a single boolean, and wire lib/precedence-band.sh to read burn state — while a product-lane SLO is burning or unmeasured, the machinery priority multiplier goes to zero (machinery claims freeze except the repair claim itself). Acceptance: with today's live data (queue_starvation_minutes null, time_to_repair_per_class {}, pct_auto_repaired 0.0) the snapshot computes green=false and machinery intake freezes; a synthetic fully-measured passing input yields green=true. Constraints: change inside the existing SLO organ and precedence band; add a test; no new files beyond that.

comments.body:
subsumed-by #5125 — #5125's body now carries the #5119 clauses it lacked: measured:true|false per required field (distinguishing "unmeasured" from "zero", so a measured zero does not appear in unmeasured[]), and the machinery multiplier 0 while burning/unmeasured — machinery intake gates on remaining budget, machinery claims freeze except the repair claim itself.

decision-resolved: close as subsumed by #5125 (dedupe #6496, #5734 precedent: the newer #5125 provably subsumes — it adds intake-gates-on-remaining-budget). Do not re-label agent-ready (fleet-ops#5723).

title: BET 4: Capture-validity gate — render-validated proof before any diff becomes an event
body:
metric: Zero phantom change events from render failures (500, Cloudflare challenge, cookie wall, partial SPA load, site-down-restore, timestamp-only edit, rotating banner)

observed: 95.4% of all watch events are ad_new/ad_inactive pings (research §1.5a). The #1 and #2 buyer complaints category-wide are alert noise and phantom changes from render failures (research §2.3). Visualping concedes 83% of detections are unimportant and false positives "will never reach zero" (research §2.2). BET 4 research §3.4 identifies this as a wide-open differentiator: "Nobody advertises solving it."

evidence:
- Research §2.3: "Phantom changes from render failures — partial loads, error pages, takedown/restore cycles, JS-heavy SPAs, bot walls. Every vendor concedes it; none advertises solving it."
- Research §2.2: Visualping blog admits 83% of detected changes classified as not important
- Research §3.4 BET 4 Build: "A capture-validity gate before any diff is allowed to become an event: HTTP status class, minimum content signature, known error/challenge-page fingerprints, cookie-banner and consent-wall detection, and a cross-check that an extracted price/CTA change is corroborated by the screenshot rather than by markdown extraction alone."
- Research §3.4 BET 4 Termination: "Adversarial fixture suite — 500 error page, Cloudflare challenge, cookie wall, partially-loaded SPA, site-down-then-restored, timestamp-only edit, rotating banner — produces zero events, all recorded as capture_failed/suppressed with reasons; a genuine price edit in the same suite still produces one event."
- Existing issues #1476 (capture_failed visibility only), #1320 (cross-link only) cover visibility, not the validation gate itself

accept:
1. Implement capture-validity gate in the monitoring pipeline that runs before any diff evaluation:
   - Reject captures with non-2xx HTTP status or known challenge-page fingerprints (Cloudflare, CAPTCHA, WAF)
   - Require minimum content signature (byte count, DOM node count, text ratio) vs baseline
   - Detect and suppress cookie-banner/consent-wall render states
   - Cross-check extracted price/CTA/offer changes against screenshot OCR/visual diff, not just markdown
2. Failed captures enter explicit `capture_failed` state with reason code (never generate alerts, visible in run history)
3. Add adversarial fixture test suite under `tests/integration/capture-validity/` covering all 7 adversarial cases from termination check
4. Gate: the fixture suite must pass in CI before merge

verify:
```
# Run the adversarial fixture suite
npm run test:integration -- tests/integration/capture-validity/
# Verify zero events emitted for adversarial fixtures
# Verify genuine price edit still produces one event
```

rollback: Revert the capture-validity gate module and fixture tests; monitoring reverts to previous diff-only behavior

dedupe: None — existing issues #1476 (UI visibility), #1320 (cross-link), #1455/#1454 (canaries) cover adjacent concerns but not the validation gate implementation

impact: This is the category's #1-2 buyer complaint (alert noise + phantom changes). Solving it makes "proof-backed" a genuine claim, not marketing copy. Directly enables BET 1 (signal ratio) by ensuring only real changes reach the digest.

product_surface: Monitoring pipeline → daily/weekly digests, instant alerts, run history

termination: npm run test:integration -- tests/integration/capture-validity/ && echo "PASS: adversarial suite blocks all 7 phantom cases, genuine price edit passes"

source: Research §3.4 BET 4 (rank 4, wide-open differentiator) — "Nobody advertises solving it" + termination check adversarial fixture suite

body:
Filed automatically from the Kimi K3 Max 11-lens recommendations pass on 0509 (lens: Architecture and refactoring, ref R2, impact/size H/S). Scope is exactly the `do:` line below — no judgment calls, no extra files. If it cannot be done as written, stop and comment.

why: `event_candidate` and `watch_event` both hard-CHECK the event vocabulary (migrations/0007_proof_first_change_alerts.sql:11 and :258). Adding website events required recreating the entire `watch_event` table as `watch_event_site_monitoring_next` (migrations/0077:40-60). Every queued source brings new event types → five more full-table rebuilds of a table that only grows.

files: migrations/0007_proof_first_change_alerts.sql, migrations/0077
do: one migration that rebuilds `watch_event`/`event_candidate` once more, replacing the CHECK with `source_kind TEXT` + unconstrained `event_type TEXT` (validated in code via the adapter registry from R1).
must-not: touch files outside `files:` and the files named in the `do:` step; add a new mechanism, script, or organ; invent product copy, pricing, or unsourced claims; weaken or skip a test.
termination: npm test
accept: the next new event type lands as an adapter file change with zero migration; `npm run test` integration suite passes against the rebuilt schema.
metric: H-impact / S-size per the lens ranking.
depends-on: none
owner-decision: no

- Replace `depends-on: none` with `depends-on: #2333` — it validates "via the adapter registry from R1".
- Replace `files: migrations/0007_proof_first_change_alerts.sql, migrations/0077` with `files: migrations/0088_event_type_free_text.sql (new)` — applied migrations are immutable.
- Append to `do:`: "Preserve every existing row: create `_next` tables, `INSERT ... SELECT`, drop, rename — the same pattern as 0077:40-60. Row counts must be identical before and after." — a literal worker could otherwise DROP-and-recreate a growing events table.

title: ci(d1): production migration safety gate — dry-run on a restored scratch copy with a per-table row-count invariant before any --remote apply (never again: fleet-ops#4999)
body:
metric: no migration can reach production D1 unless the SAME migration set was first applied to a scratch D1 restored from the pre-migration backup and every business table's row count is >= its pre-apply count (or the migration file carries an explicit, PR-reviewed `-- expects-row-loss: <table>[,<table>]` annotation naming each table allowed to shrink). The gate is a required step in `.github/workflows/d1-remote-restore-evidence.yml` before `wrangler d1 migrations apply 0509 --remote`, AND the same check runs on every PR touching `migrations/` against the seeded fixture, so a destructive migration is red before merge, not at prod apply.

observed: 2026-09-09T23:09Z — `d1-remote-restore-evidence.yml:191` applied `0087` to production on the push trigger. The only guard was `steps.pre_migration_backup.outcome == 'success'` (an R2 backup). Nothing checked what the migration DID. 0087's `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` is a no-op inside D1's transaction, `DROP TABLE user` cascaded through 55 `ON DELETE CASCADE` children, and user_plan/watchlist/delivery_attempt/proof_capture/session went to 0 rows (fleet-ops#4999). Nish's decision 2026-09-11: accept the loss; make this class impossible, structurally — no patches.

evidence:
- `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/d1-remote-restore-evidence.yml | sed -n '161,192p'` — backup, reconfirm-main, apply; no dry-run, no invariant.
- The workflow already provisions and cleans a scratch D1 ("Prepare/Generate D1 remote restore evidence", "Confirm scratch D1 cleanup" jobs) — the gate rides those rails, no new organ.
- fleet-ops#4999 census: `user_plan 0 | watchlist 0 | delivery_attempt 0 | proof_capture 0 | session 0 | users 15`.
- Sibling class fixes already filed: 0509#2774 (rewrite 0087 + lint banning `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` in migrations), 0509#2507 (migration sort-order detector). This issue is the invariant that catches what lints cannot foresee.

do:
1. In `d1-remote-restore-evidence.yml`, between the pre-migration backup and the remote apply: restore that backup into the scratch D1, apply the pending migrations there, snapshot `SELECT name, (SELECT COUNT(*) ...)` for every table in `sqlite_master` before and after, and fail the job (and therefore never reach `--remote`) on any decrease not covered by an `-- expects-row-loss:` annotation in the migration file that caused it. Print the per-table diff in the job summary.
2. Record the D1 Time Travel bookmark (`wrangler d1 time-travel info 0509 --timestamp <now>`) immediately before the remote apply and write it to the run summary and the restore-evidence manifest, so a rollback is one known command.
3. On PRs touching `migrations/**`: the same before/after row-count check against the existing seeded test fixture (local D1 / better-sqlite3 with `foreign_keys=ON`, applied inside a transaction to mirror D1). Required check.
4. Tests: a fixture migration that drops-and-recreates a parent table with cascading children must turn the gate red; the same migration with the annotation must pass; a purely additive migration must pass. The gate must FAIL on the current 0087 file.
5. Judge question for the PR (not a blocker): should production migrations apply on push to main at all, or only inside the Nish-gated deploy? Answer in the PR description with reasoning; do not change the trigger in this PR.

termination: PR merged; a deliberately destructive fixture migration on a branch goes red at the PR check; the workflow's remote-apply step is `if:`-guarded on the gate step's outcome; fleet-ops#4999 is closed with Nish's decision and links here.
accept: prod applies get slower by one scratch restore + apply (minutes). Correct trade — the alternative was 2 days of silent data loss.
required: none. No new machinery: an added step in an existing workflow, an added required check, tests.

title: gate-integrity: jq --argjson E2BIG on large PRs — patch bundle must go through a temp file, not argv
body:
Observed on Nishfleet/0509 PR #1980 (issue #1958): the `Resolve candidate context through the GitHub API` step fails with `/usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long` + exit 126.

Root cause: gate-integrity.yml builds `files_json` (PR patch +/- lines only) and passes it as a single `--argjson files` CLI argument to `jq -n`. The kernel caps a single argument at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes). A PR whose +/- payload exceeds ~110KB (after JSON escaping) can never pass the gate — no amount of retry fixes it; the PR is structurally unmergeable.

Evidence: PR #1980 diff has 3164 +/- lines / 137,772 bytes raw (~160KB escaped); the job log shows the jq -n invocation erroring on line 79 with E2BIG.

Fix direction: write each JSON blob (`files_json`, `comments_json`, `commits_json`) to $RUNNER_TEMP files and build the bundle with `jq -n --slurpfile` (or cat | jq), so no single argument carries the payload. Keep everything else identical.

Blocked a real fix PR (0509#1980) — treating as fleet-ops infra, not 0509 scope.

title: Every sitemap /ads/:domain URL serves noindex in production — programmatic SEO surface is dead
body:
metric: Every URL `<loc>https://0509.io/ads/:domain</loc>` in `https://0509.io/sitemap.xml` returns HTML without a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` tag. Sitemap membership and noindex state must agree, or Google treats the sitemap as untrustworthy and the entire programmatic acquisition channel goes dark.

observed: 2026-08-27T06:35Z against `https://0509.io`:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -cE '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/'` → 35
- Of 28 `/ads/:domain` URLs curled (nike.com, nykaa.com, allbirds.com, lenskart.com, mamaearth.com, bombayshavingcompany.com, decathlon.com, figma.com, celonis.com, sephora.com, walmart.com, amazon.com, ulta.com, asos.com, hm.com, adidas.com, adobe.com, atlassian.com, stripe.com, shopify.com, canva.com, ridge.com, ouraring.com, personio.com, sugarcosmetics.com, mcaffeine.com, zoho.com, bombas.com) **all 28 return HTTP 200 with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` and `<link rel="canonical" href="https://0509.io/ads/<domain>">`**.
- Allbirds live data: `hasCachedAds:true, brandOwnedAdCount:13, verifiedLinkCount:9, unverifiedMatchCount:4, checkedAgo:"about 15 minutes ago"`, Ad Aggression Score 48/100 over 132 days. The page is fully populated. Only noindex is wrong.
- Lenskart: same shape, 18 brand-owned ads, 12 verified. Still noindex.
- Nike: 16 brand-owned, 95 ads in the wall. Still noindex.
- Saucony / Asics (the 2026-08-27 market-signal swing) are also noindex shells per #1282.

This is a **regression of #912** (closed 2026-08-24) and #1071 (closed, "superseded by merged #922"). PR #865 was the original fix, then commit `010a219b` "sitemap: list only /ads pages the loader can actually render indexable" was meant to be the durable fix. Empirically it did not stick: the parity the merge claimed to enforce is broken in production. The most likely cause is `PUBLIC_BRAND_PAGES_INDEXABLE="0"` being set as the emergency brake somewhere outside the repo (Cloudflare dashboard env), so every `/ads/:domain` loader returns `noindex=true` regardless of cache freshness — but the same loader still includes the URLs in the sitemap (the `sitemap.server.ts` filter does not read `PUBLIC_BRAND_PAGES_INDEXABLE` for the *served page* state, only for the *sitemap emission* per rule 5 of its docblock).

evidence:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/[^<]+</loc>' | wc -l` → 35
- 28/28 of the sampled `/ads/:domain` URLs return `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` in the HTML body
- The page `loaders` only set `noindex = emergencyNoindex || !snapshot || !snapshot.freshForIndexing` (`app/routes/ads.$domain.tsx:170`), so a 15-min-old verified cache cannot explain the noindex. The `emergencyNoindex` branch is the only path that produces this for a populated page.
- `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts:306` does honor `PUBLIC_BRAND_PAGES_INDEXABLE="0"` by suppressing dynamic entries — yet the sitemap still contains 35 entries. That means the env is not `"0"` for sitemap-emission, but the page is being served with noindex anyway. Either the env is being applied only at the page layer and not the sitemap layer, or the page is calling a different `emergencyNoindex` source.
- Recent merged commits touching this surface: `010a219b` (sitemap parity, 2026-08-25), `c36f626c` (verified count for brand-owned), `746e2f42` (restored compare pages in sitemap/llms.txt).
- Closed but re-emerged: #912, #1071, #1120, #1142.

source: 2026-08-27 market-signal report — 0509 has had **0 external signups in 63 days, 0 paid accounts, 0 customer_api_keys, 2 plausible external users**; §1.6 transformation roadmap — "19 URLs in the sitemap … 5 `/ads/:domain` pages" (the 35-URL scale-out is BET 5's dependency); §3.4 BET 5 ("Somebody has to see it") — "Generate from a curated seed list of a few thousand advertisers with real ad coverage, gated so no page ships empty (bet 2 is the dependency)" and "Scale `/ads/:domain` into a real programmatic surface". The /ads pages already exist with real ad coverage and they are dead-letter because of this noindex regression. North-star rule: "be clearly BETTER than the customer's own AI" — the SEO surface cannot outperform edge AI discovery if Google is told the URLs don't exist.

accept:
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/allbirds.com | grep -ic noindex` → 0
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/nike.com | grep -ic noindex` → 0
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/lenskart.com | grep -ic noindex` → 0
- `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/saucony.com | grep -ic noindex` → 0 (the empty-shell branch per #1282 is the only legitimate noindex case)
- For every `<loc>https://0509.io/ads/:domain</loc>` in the sitemap, the page returns `<meta name="robots" content="...">` that is *not* "noindex" (or no robots meta at all)
- The fix must be either (a) flipping the production env so the parity check matches the page state, or (b) tightening `sitemap.server.ts` to *only* emit entries that pass the same `noindex` predicate the page loader uses — so the two cannot drift again.
- **Prevention mechanism (per mechanical-fix rule / fleet-ops#366):** add a CI check that runs `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml` + `curl -sS` for every `/ads/:domain` URL and asserts `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` count is 0 for each. The check lives in `tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh` and runs on every PR via the `seo-parity` job. It fails closed (the PR is blocked, not a warning). Without the CI guard, this is the third time we have closed the same bug; the recurrence itself is the evidence the manual fix is not durable.
- Reopen or supersede #912 with a back-link in this issue's "closing evidence".

verify:
```
# Live (production) — must report 0 for every populated brand page
for d in allbirds.com nike.com lenskart.com mamaearth.com ridge.com nykaa.com figma.com stripe.com adidas.com; do
  noidx=$(curl -sS "https://0509.io/ads/$d" | grep -c 'noindex')
  echo "$d $noidx"
done
# Sitemap size still 35 (no scope regression)
curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/[^<]+</loc>' | wc -l
# Local CI guard
npx vitest run tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh 2>/dev/null || bash tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh
```

rollback: Revert the parity fix. Sitemap reverts to the over-listing state. Risk: no worse than the current broken state.

dedupe: Supersedes #912 (closed) and #1071 (closed). Live partial coverage in #966 (scale-out, still open and explicitly "blocked by Bet-1/Bet-2") — fix this first and #966 unblocks at the SEO layer. The empty-shell branch of #1282 is the only legitimate noindex for the `/ads/:domain` surface and must be preserved (no proof → noindex, with proof → index).

impact: The single biggest SEO bug on the production site. Sitemap-vs-noindex is the worst kind of search-engine signal because it tells Google "trust neither the list nor the page" — the entire 35-URL programmatic acquisition surface is invisible to search, which is the exact distribution problem the transformation roadmap identifies in §3.4 BET 5 and §1.6 ("0 signups in 63 days"). The fix is also a prerequisite for BET 5 (scale-out to thousands of brand pages) — without the parity, scaling makes the bug worse.

product_surface: Public `/ads/:domain` brand pages, `/sitemap.xml`, Google Search Console indexing of 0509 brand pages.

termination: `bash tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh` exits 0, AND `curl -sS https://0509.io/ads/allbirds.com | grep -c 'noindex'` returns 0, AND `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -oE '<loc>https://0509.io/ads/[^<]+</loc>' | wc -l` returns 35 (no scope regression). All three must hold on the same production deploy.

title: Manager loop for heavy/keystone issues: worker plans phases, spawns a fresh implementer per phase with handoff, reviewer per phase; replaces the never-used phases: manifest (Nish 2026-09-04)
body:
Decision (Nish, 2026-09-04) after the Manager Loop write-up. Facts: the fleet-ops#1383 `phases:` manifest has been written into 0 packets ever and only routes seats; Pi's stock subagent extension is now installed and proven (see fleet-ops#3127 comment); large issues today die in one flat 42-min session (69 hang kills) or get split into follow-up issues that lose the plan through intake.

Shape (inside ONE claim, ONE systemd unit, no second queue — the fleet2 ban stays):
- required: packet_difficulty heavy|keystone -> the pi-issue worker runs as MANAGER: (1) `Use planner` to write a phased checklist into the worktree at `.fleet/plan.md` (one line per acceptance bullet, grouped into <= 6 phases); (2) for each phase, spawn a FRESH `worker` subagent with the task "Complete phase N extremely well" plus a written handoff (plan.md + git log since last phase + the previous phase's final message); (3) `Use reviewer` on the phase diff; act-on findings go back to a fresh worker once; (4) tick boxes in plan.md and commit after each phase; (5) manager opens the PR and arms auto-merge as today. Light issues stay flat.
- required: stall rule at both levels: a phase with no box ticked in 10 min is closed with what works and a `stalled:` note; the manager may amend the plan (add/drop phases) with a one-line reason in plan.md — the implementer may propose, the manager decides.
- required: delete the dead `phases:` manifest path (seat-lib packet_has_phases/packet_phases, intake step 3d keystone branch, PI_PACKET_PHASES export) in the same PR. Net lines must be negative.
- required: install.sh owns the subagent extension symlinks + unpinned agent defs (MANIFEST), so a pi reinstall cannot silently drop delegation again; pi-transport-check asserts `EXTLOAD` for subagent when a worker starts.
- required: wording: 'extremely well', never 'perfect'.
- accept: one real heavy 0509 issue run end-to-end through the manager loop with plan.md committed, >= 2 phases, reviewer output in the PR body; PR merged. Journal transcript in the PR as run-proof.
- metric: fleet_manager_phases_total, fleet_phase_stalls_total, sessions_to_pr_pct for heavy issues (baseline: heavy sessions currently 42-min-kill or single-shot).
- moves: sessions_to_pr_pct

title: /ads/:domain ad wall renders verified and unverified cards identically — buyers can't tell which ads the Aggression Score is built from
body:
<!-- possible-duplicate-of: Nishfleet/0509#1442 score=0.54 -->
Possible duplicate of Nishfleet/0509#1442 (score 0.54). Weekly Review: confirm or close as duplicate.

metric: A first-time visitor on a populated `/ads/:domain` page can visually distinguish, on each card, whether the ad is verified-link (used by the Aggression Score and "what changed" feed) or a search-only match.

observed: 2026-08-30T22:36Z UTC, production https://0509.io.

- `/ads/notion.so` (page H1: "Notion was running 2 Meta ads at the last check", subline: "Another 9 ads matched the search without a verified link to notion.so") renders a wall titled "All 11 ads, on the wall" containing 5 visible cards. All 5 cards use the same `f9-ads-card` wrapper, the same `f9-ads-card-adv` advertiser slot, and the same `f9-ads-card-pill` row. 2 cards are verified-Notion (advertiser: "Notion · fb.me" / "T-Pain with Notion · notion.com"), 3 are search-only matches with the same visual treatment. The 2 verified-link cards have no badge, no border treatment, and no ordering that distinguishes them from the 3 unverified ones. A buyer evaluating Notion cannot tell which 2 ads the Aggression Score is computed from.
- Same defect visible on every populated `/ads/:domain` that mixes verified-link and search-match ads (e.g. `/ads/allbirds.com`, `/ads/ridge.com`, `/ads/nike.com` cache-miss strips — anything where the snapshot returned > `verifiedLinkCount` rows). The page text in the hero copy and honest-tail paragraph is accurate; the wall itself is not.
- This violates the north-star rule ("If it is not verified, say so. If it is verified, do not present it as unverified.") — verified cards are presented alongside unverified cards with no visual hierarchy.

evidence:
- https://0509.io/ads/notion.so live HTML, 2026-08-30: H1 "Notion was running 2 Meta ads…", subline "Another 9 ads matched the search without a verified link…", wall title "All 11 ads, on the wall", 5 cards each carrying `f9-ads-card-adv` with no verified/unverified distinction.
- Repo: `app/components/ads/brand-ad-wall.tsx` lines 80–120 — `BrandAdCard` renders every entry of the `ads` array with the same `<article className="f9-ads-card">` and `BrandAdCard` does not consult `verifiedLink` / `linkVerifiedDomain` / equivalent on the `AdRecord`.
- Repo: `app/routes/ads.$domain.tsx` lines 178–196 — `verifiedLinkedAds` and `snapshotAds` (search-only) are tracked separately upstream; the breakdown is surfaced in the hero copy and the honest-tail paragraph but not passed through to `BrandAdWall`.
- Repo: `app/routes/ads.$domain.tsx` line 497 — wall title uses the total count: `All ${totalCount} ${adWord}, on the wall`.
- Market signal 2026-08-30 §1.8: "3 of 6 uncached, obviously-advertising brands returned 'No verified ads found.'" — the empty-state copy is honest, but when the page does render a wall it puts both kinds in the same grid.
- Market signal 2026-08-30 §1.5: "landing-page_snapshot and website_watch_target are both empty" — the canonical differentiator (the verified evidence trail) currently has zero visual signature on the wall.
- North-star memory (global-standing-rules + memory_id: north-star-edge-ai-cannot-match): verified copy must match the verified state on the most-shared surface.

source: north-star rule + 2026-08-30 market-signal §1.5 + §1.8 + transformation bet BET 5 ("the prospective buyer … can actually find this product").

accept:
1. Each `/ads/:domain` ad card carries a visible verified-link signal — a pill, an outline, an ordering rule, or equivalent — when the card's `AdRecord` is in the `verifiedLinkedAds` set. The signal must be readable in a single glance, not buried in the advertiser-name text.
2. When the wall contains both verified-link and search-only cards, the verified set renders first (or otherwise clearly separated), and the wall header reports both counts (e.g. "All 11 ads — 2 verified, 9 matched the search").
3. `BrandAdCard` consumes the verified/unverified distinction via the existing `AdRecord` shape (extend the type if needed; do not pass booleans by prop drilling). The Aggression Score and the change-feed continue to compute from `verifiedLinkedAds` only — the wall change is presentation, not scoring.
4. A new Playwright prod-public test asserts: on `/ads/notion.so`, the verified-Notion cards carry the new signal; the search-only cards (e.g. "Notion Press Publishing") do not.
5. The honest-tail paragraph at the bottom of the page still names the verified/unverified split, so the page is honest in both prose and visual.

verify:
```
npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts --project=prod-public tests/e2e/ads-wall-verified-label.spec.ts
```
The new test must load `/ads/notion.so` and assert (a) the wall header reports both verified and total counts, (b) the verified-Notion cards carry the new signal class, and (c) the "Notion Press Publishing" card does not. The test must exit 0.

rollback: revert the commit. The `AdRecord` shape is preserved; the visual signal is purely additive.

dedupe: not a duplicate of #1440 (search-side tier labels), #1455 (noindex/canary), #1446 (alias 301s), #1411 (compare-cite sources), or #1462 (docs proof-label drift). #1440 covers the /search?q=brand result rows; this issue covers the public `/ads/:domain` wall rendering.

impact: `/ads/:domain` is the only programmatic SEO surface that ranks for "<brand> facebook ads" queries (transformation bet BET 5) and is the only place a buyer lands from organic search for their competitor's name. If the wall is the first thing they evaluate and it presents unverified ads identically to verified ones, the product's entire "verified proof" claim reads as decoration. This is also the page that backs the #1272 `/timeline/:domain` surface once it ships, so the verified-card signal has to be in place before that surface is indexable.

product_surface: /ads/:domain programmatic brand-ads pages (e.g. /ads/notion.so, /ads/ouraring.com, /ads/allbirds.com)

termination: `npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts --project=prod-public tests/e2e/ads-wall-verified-label.spec.ts` exits 0 against production https://0509.io/ads/notion.so AND the wall header reports the verified vs search-only split numerically.

title: Every loud alarm produces a postmortem with a detector-coverage section, and unactionable alarms do not page
body:
WHY: One alarm class re-files without end - FAILED-COMMAND-SWALLOWED is open at #5090, #5089, #5067, #5066, #5065, #5044, #5043, #5041, #5033, #5032, #5011 and #5010 - while playbook debt is counted and never paid (DEBUG-PLAYBOOK-FAIL #4883: missing=55, debt=54). glm-5-2 proposed postmortems as tracked artifacts; nothing currently links recurrence back to the prior fix.

CHANGE:
1. In the existing alarm-filing path (the unit or script that opens an issue for a loud alarm), generate a postmortem file per loud alarm from the alarm's own journal window (journalctl for the emitting unit, alarm time minus 30m). Required sections: timeline, root cause, detector coverage (why the detector did not catch it earlier), action items.
2. File each action item as its own issue carrying agent-ready and a parent-alarm reference; include the playbook link when one exists.
3. Actionability gate: an alarm reaches the human/Nish surface only with a playbook link AND a named action. Unlinked alarms are suppressed and increment the missing-playbook debt counter that feeds #4883, instead of filing another open issue.
4. Recurrence: if an open issue already exists for the same alarm class, append the new occurrence to it and mark the prior postmortem failed; do not open a new issue.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Replay an existing loud alarm fixture: postmortem file exists, detector-coverage section non-empty, at least one action-item issue created, and one suppression counter increment for a no-playbook alarm.
- Replay the same alarm twice: exactly one open issue, second occurrence appended.

ROLLBACK: revert.
OUT OF SCOPE: no new timer; hook into the existing filing path.

subsumed-by #5120 — #5120's body now carries the #5127 clauses it lacked: the actionability gate (an alarm reaches the human/Nish surface only with a playbook link AND a named action; alarms without one are suppressed and increment the missing-playbook debt counter that feeds #4883, instead of filing another open issue), action-item issues carrying agent-ready and a parent-alarm reference (playbook link when it exists) with the exactly-one-open-issue-per-class recurrence (a recurrence appends while the class issue is open), and the journalctl-for-the-emitting-unit, alarm-time-minus-30m source window.

title: feat(ci): migrate to fleet-ops thin callers where safe
body:
## What

P11-B (Nishfleet/fleet-ops#240) stood up reusable workflows in fleet-ops:
- `reusable-gitleaks.yml` — pinned-gitleaks secret scan
- `reusable-semgrep.yml` — canonical semgrep gate
- `reusable-review-gate.yml` — rationed deep review
- `reusable-auto-enqueue.yml` — declarative merge-queue arm

0509 is marked `local-richer` in the standards sync because it carries hardened local gates (required-verifier-integrity with sole-admin attestation, gate-integrity with auto-revert waiver). Those must NOT be overwritten.

## Task

Migrate the gates that are SAFE to thin-call (no loss of hardness):
1. `review-gate.yml` → thin caller to `reusable-review-gate.yml` (0509's review-gate is the same budget-backpressure logic; the reusable version generalizes it).
2. Add `auto-enqueue.yml` thin caller (new, no existing local equivalent).
3. Evaluate `secret-scan.yml` → `reusable-gitleaks.yml` (0509's version may have extra protections — audit before migrating).
4. Do NOT migrate `required-verifier-integrity.yml` or `gate-integrity.yml` — they are 0509-specific and tracked by the generalization issue (fleet-ops#TBD).

## Why

One CI standard, defined once, consumed everywhere. 0509 keeps its hardened gates but adopts the portable ones where there is no loss.

## Dependency

Nishfleet/fleet-ops#240 must merge first.

Cannot land this yet. Two independent blockers, both live.

**1. The reusable workflows this issue calls are not on fleet-ops main.**

P11-B (fleet-ops#240) shipped `reusable-review-gate.yml`, `reusable-gitleaks.yml`, and `reusable-auto-enqueue.yml`. Each land was auto-reverted (#281, then re-lands #294/#305 reverted by #295/#306) because P14 tests are still red on main (fleet-ops#308). fleet-ops#469 tracks the re-land and says do not try again until #308 is green. A thin caller pointed at files that do not exist would break 0509 CI.

**2. This runner cannot push `.github/workflows/**`.**

nishfleet-worker has Contents/PRs/Issues write and no Workflows permission. A push that touches workflow files is rejected at GitHub (same class as fleet-ops#216). Landing this needs Nish's workflow-scoped identity, or a later comment with `decision-resolved:` after that identity is available. This unit has already hit StartLimitBurst five times on this issue by retrying the same wall.

**review-gate.yml — migrate when #469 lands.** Local file is the same budget-backpressure logic the reusable version generalizes. Reverted reusable at `6b7434d` already accepts `monthly-cap` (default `"30"`, matches 0509) and `deep-label` (`review:deep`). Intended caller:

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, ready_for_review, reopened]
jobs:
  review-gate:
    uses: Nishfleet/fleet-ops/.github/workflows/reusable-review-gate.yml@<fleet-ops-main-sha>
    with:
      monthly-cap: "30"
```

Pin the SHA, not `@main`.

**auto-enqueue.yml — do not add a second workflow.** The issue said there was no local equivalent. There is: `.github/workflows/auto-merge-arm.yml`, already live. fleet-ops main already hosts `reusable-auto-merge-arm.yml`. Adding `auto-enqueue.yml` beside `auto-merge-arm.yml` would arm every PR twice.

**secret-scan.yml — do not migrate.** Extra hardness the generic reusable does not replace:

- required-context no-skip (no job-level `if:`, no `needs`) so a skipped check cannot go green
- repo-bound authorizer (`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` must be `Nishfleet/0509`)
- `workflow_dispatch` SHA pin, fork PRs fail closed
- pinned gitleaks binary 8.30.1 + SHA-256, not the licensed action wrapper

Issue said audit before migrating. Audit result: keep local.

**required-verifier-integrity.yml / gate-integrity.yml — leave alone**, as the issue already said.

Any PR that edits `.github/workflows/**` is a gate-path change. A repository admin (different identity from the PR author) must post `gate-integrity-attest: <sha>`. The worker that authors the PR must not attest.

One PR, SHA-pinned thin callers only for review-gate and auto-merge-arm (or auto-enqueue if renamed). secret-scan and the two 0509-only integrity gates stay local. Then `bin/prove-one-run-check` plus a real workflow run-proof before merge.

title: fleet_oomd_kills_6h has no producer — FleetOomdKillsHigh can never fire (detector half of #4838)
body:
`FleetOomdKillsHigh` (config/fleet_rules.yml:434) alerts on `sum(fleet_oomd_kills_6h) > 3` and its description prescribes a concrete repair. The metric has no producer, so the alert can never fire.

Proof (2026-09-10 10:25 IST):
```
$ curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/query?query=fleet_oomd_kills_6h' | jq -c '.data.result'
[]
$ curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/label/__name__/values' | jq -r '.data[]|select(test("oom|kill";"i"))'
node_vmstat_oom_kill
```

Prior art:
- Exists: `FleetOomdKillsHigh` already lives in `config/fleet_rules.yml` (main L433) on `sum(fleet_oomd_kills_6h) > 3`. node_exporter already exports `node_vmstat_oom_kill` (live 2026-09-10: one series, value 10, job=node). Prometheus recording rules already ship in the same file. PR #4871 merged the concurrency half of #4838.
- Tested this turn: `curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/query?query=fleet_oomd_kills_6h'` returns `[]`. Label values matching oom|kill only return `node_vmstat_oom_kill`.
- Rejected: a new exporter, collector, timer, or organ for unit-labelled oomd kills (standing rule: new machinery needs Nish endorsement; this ticket's must-not). Deleting or weakening the alert (must-not). Scraping journald/oomd logs into a custom metric (new organ).

Cost of the gap: the OOM class it guards ran unchecked and the senior auditor escalated it to Nish five times in 24h (22:21Z, 22:33Z, 01:59Z, 03:40Z, 04:37Z) rather than the fleet self-repairing. The concurrency half is fixed in PR #4871; this is the detector half.

files: config/fleet_rules.yml
do: give `fleet_oomd_kills_6h` a producer. `node_vmstat_oom_kill` already exists as a counter, so the cheapest honest option is a recording rule over `increase(node_vmstat_oom_kill[6h])`. Note in the rule comment that this is host-wide and carries NO `unit=` label, so the alert description's reference to `fleet_oomd_kills_6h{unit=...}` must be reworded to match what the metric actually provides.
must-not: build a new exporter, collector, timer or organ for unit-labelled oomd kills without Nish's explicit endorsement (global-standing-rules: new machinery requires endorsement); weaken or delete the alert instead of wiring it; touch files outside `files:`.
termination: `promtool check rules config/fleet_rules.yml` passes AND `curl -s '127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/query?query=fleet_oomd_kills_6h' | jq '.data.result|length'` returns > 0 after the rules reload.
accept: the alert can fire. A judge can quote a non-empty result for the query above.
metric: zero un-fireable alerts referencing a non-existent metric.
owner-decision: none (no money, no product direction).

Blind-spot note (fleet-ops#4460): an alert whose metric has no producer is invisible to every existing check. A sweep for the whole class — every `expr` in fleet_rules.yml whose metric names return empty from Prometheus — is the general fix and is worth folding into this ticket's `do:` if it stays one command.

title: seat: Kimi K3 (cursor/kimi-k3-max, local cursor-agent CLI) as JUDGE/ORCHESTRATOR ONLY — hourly-as-affordable fable-check POV + senior packets; worker cap 0; drain the Ultra 'Other Models' $400/month bucket (Nish 2026-09-08)
body:
**Decision (Nish, 2026-09-08 10:40-11:00 IST, final): "kimi k3 only" → "k3 is only judge / orchestrator".** Kimi K3 is NOT a worker seat. It is a judge/orchestrator seat: hourly fable-check POV, senior-review, planner/spec packets, review-adjudication, conference seats. Worker cap 0. The Cursor Ultra "Other Models" bucket ($400/month of third-party usage at API price, docs https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/usage-limits; dashboard shows 1% used) is consumed on Kimi K3 only, through judge/orchestrator packets, drained to ~95% per cycle. The dashboard's separate "On-Demand $0.00 / $400" is the overage spend limit (https://cursor.com/docs/account/billing/spend-limits); never spend it — Nish sets it to 0.

**Proven 2026-09-08 04:45Z, local, no cloud agents needed:** `CURSOR_API_KEY=$(cut -d= -f2 ~/fleet2/etc/cursor.env) cursor-agent -p -f --model kimi-k3-max --output-format text "Reply with exactly: KIMI-OK"` → `KIMI-OK`, rc 0. `cursor-agent --list-models` lists `kimi-k3-low`, `kimi-k3-high`, `kimi-k3-max` ("Kimi K3"), `kimi-k2.7-code`. Pi's existing `cursor` provider (api `cursor-cli`, the same CLI) returned empty for `--model kimi-k3-max` only because the id is not registered in models.json ("not found for provider cursor. Using custom model id"). So this is CONFIG on the existing provider, not a new organ. The Cloud Agent API path from the earlier body is dropped.

**Do:**
1. config/pi-models.json, provider `cursor`: add `kimi-k3-max` (default) and `kimi-k3-high`; contextWindow/maxTokens from Cursor's model docs (cite the URL; do not guess). Prove `echo 'Reply with exactly: PI-KIMI-OK' | pi --print --provider cursor --model kimi-k3-max` prints it.
2. config/seat-caps.json + entitled-seats.json: `cursor/kimi-k3-max` is keystone/senior/judge-only exactly like the other cursor ids (fleet-ops#1167 stays) — pi-issue WORKER cap 0; senior-review / planner / spec / adjudication / conference packets allowed, cap 2; the hourly judge unit (step 4) is its main consumer. Class prepaid-quota; bucket = Other Models, $400/month at API price; reset = Cursor billing cycle. No `fast`/`low` variants.
3. Pacing (expiry-first, drain to the max): the bucket is a monthly $400 at API price. Meter it from the #4232 dashboard scrape ("Other Models: N% used") — until that lands, from Kimi K3's API list price × session usage in the prepaid-usage counter (cite the price). **Nish 2026-09-08 11:05 IST: "use generously to use up the $400 before sub expires."** Pace by DAYS LEFT, not month-average: the Cursor monthly window resets about 2026-09-22 04:02Z (fleet-metrics cursor-quota-cache; confirm on the dashboard), so ~$396 must go in ~14 days ≈ $28/day. The counter computes `usd_per_day_target = remaining_usd / days_left` every run and the judge timer + senior-packet cap are set to hit it; if the bucket is behind pace at any check, add judge runs (hourly, then every 30 min) and raise the senior-packet cap (2 → 4 → 6) until on pace. Bench only at 97%. Unused $ at reset is the failure, not overspend.
4. Judge POV: clone the `fable-fleet-check-opus` unit pattern as `fable-fleet-check-kimi.service/.timer` in systemd/ (repo-sourced), ExecStart `pi --print --provider cursor --model kimi-k3-max` with `/home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/fleet-landing-watch/fable-check.md` on stdin, `timeout --kill-after=60s 2400`, same Environment. ## Docs-first: Cursor Cloud Agents API numbers (all URLs verified live 2026-09-08)

Step 1 of this issue is the docs-first read. Here are the numbers with their docs URLs.

### Endpoint + auth
- **Create an agent:** `POST https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents` (also `GET /v1/agents`, `GET /v1/agents/{id}`, `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}`, `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage`, `GET /v1/models`, SSE `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream`).
- **Public beta:** "The Cloud Agents API v1 is in public beta. APIs may change."
- **Auth:** Basic or Bearer. `curl ... -u YOUR_API_KEY:`. Key from **Cursor Dashboard → API Keys** (`https://cursor.com/dashboard/api`) or a **service account key** from Team settings. User API keys bill to the user's plan; service-account keys bill to the team (SDK "Usage and billing").
- **URL:** https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints

### Launch against a GitHub repo + branch
`POST /v1/agents` body:
```
{ "prompt": { "text": "..." },
  "model": { "id": "composer-2.5" },
  "repos": [ { "url": "https://github.com/Nishfleet/<repo>", "startingRef": "main" } ],
  "autoCreatePR": true, "mode": "agent" }
```
- `repos[].url` required; `startingRef` = branch or SHA; `prUrl` to work on an open PR (then `startingRef` ignored).
- `workOnCurrentBranch` (default false): on false, Cursor pushes to a new auto-generated branch `cursor/...` based on `startingRef`.
- `autoCreatePR: true` opens a PR when the run completes.
- `mode`: `plan` (draft plan first) or `agent` (implement directly).
- **Completion/PR reporting:** `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}` returns `status: FINISHED | ERROR | CANCELLED | EXPIRED`, `result` (final reply), `durationMs`, and `git.branches[]` with `{ repoUrl, branch, prUrl }` — the pushed branch and the PR URL it opened.

### Model selection — NO fast variants (Nish constraint)
- Model id comes from **`GET /v1/models`** (catalog: recommended models + `params` + `variants`). Omit `model` to use the account/team/system default.
- The catalog list differs per account/key; the examples show `composer-2` (SDK docs note Composer 2 is **retired and rerouted to Composer 2.5**, and that `composer-2-fast` is rerouted too), plus third-party ids.
- **No `-fast` variants anywhere**: the memory (Nish 2026-09-07 "never ever use the fast models") forbids them. Cursor Models pricing table lists `Grok 4.6 (Fast)` and `Composer 2.5 (Fast)` at **double** the non-fast price — so fast is both banned and worse value. The non-fast candidates are `Grok 4.6` or `Composer 2.5`; the exact `grok-4.6` API id must be confirmed by running `GET /v1/models` with the key.
- **URL:** https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints (Create An Agent `model`, `List Models`) and https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript (model ids, Router/Auto).

### Pricing (per million tokens) — Cursor Models pool
From https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing:
| Model | Input | Cache Read | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Grok 4.6** | $2 | $0.5 | $6 |
| Grok 4.6 (Fast) | $4 | $1 | $12 |
| Composer 2.5 | $0.5 | $0.2 | $2.5 |
- **Per-run cost** is fetched from usage: `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage` (per-run token usage) or SDK `Agent.getUsage()` ("billed usage and dollar cost"). This is what feeds the spend meter.
- SDK "Usage and billing": "SDK runs follow the same pricing, request pools, and Privacy Mode rules as runs from the IDE and Cloud Agents. Spend shows up in your team's usage dashboard."

### Pool expiry + concurrency
- **Expiry:** "There are two separate usage pools, each **resetting with your monthly billing cycle**." The $400 "API Usage" on-demand pool (spendLimitUsage, already read by `bin/fleet-prepaid-util-canary` via api2.cursor.sh) is the Ultra on-demand pool; the budget resets at the billing cycle. The earlier seat-caps `cursor` reason pinned reset ~2026-09-22.
- **Concurrency:** "You can run as many agents as you want in parallel" (Cloud Agents — no hard documented numeric cap on parallel cloud agents; it is capacity/plan-limited). The API **control-plane** rate limit is **20 requests/min per endpoint** by default (rate limits: "Unless an endpoint documents a different limit, the default is 20 requests per minute," `429 Too Many Requests` on exceed). Exception: `/v1/repositories` is 1/user/min & 30/user/hour. This 20 r/min is the control-plane ceiling, not the model-inference cap.

### SDK (TypeScript) — the devin-style remote agent shape
`@cursor/sdk`: `Agent.create({ apiKey, model:{id}, cloud:{ repos:[{url, startingRef}], autoCreatePR:true } })`, `agent.send(prompt)`, `await run.wait()`. Cloud agents get `bc-<uuid>` ids, shown in Cursor Web under Filter → Source → SDK. URL: https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript

title: Route product work by measured yield: replace volume-first order with yield-ranked order (Nish 2026-09-04)
body:
Decision (Nish, 2026-09-04) supersedes the 2026-08-27 volume-first order (ollama -> devin -> commandcode -> cline). Measured 3-day yield per seat (sessions -> PR): minimax/MiniMax-M3 90%, xai-oauth/grok-4.6 86%, devin/glm-5-2 70%, openrouter/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 65%, opencode/nemotron 19%, commandcode/poolside 2%, opencode/mimo 0%. The order put the last three first and the first one last. Report F3. Companion: fleet-ops#3122 (yield ledger + <30% gate), fleet-ops#3120 (packet size).

- required: config/seat-caps.json: `_comment_volume_order` and `volume_providers_in_order` retired; add `product_order: yield` and pick_seat (lib/seat-lib.sh) orders issue-work seats by the rolling yield ledger from #3122, ties broken by class (prepaid-quota before metered before free) so prepaid subs still drain first among equal performers.
- required: seats with fewer than 20 sessions get a provisional yield of 50% so new seats are tried, not starved.
- required: scouts, canaries and audits keep the free-first order (they are cheap and their yield is not PR-shaped).
- required: raise xai-oauth/grok-4.6 issue-work cap from 1 to 2 (86% yield, prepaid, sub-backed) and keep devin glm-5-2 at 3 (hard ceiling stays).
- accept: sessions-with-PR / sessions >= 75% over the 3 days after merge (baseline 55%); pick_seat log shows the yield order once per pick.
- metric: fleet_seat_yield{seat}, fleet_sessions_no_pr_total.
